path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 11. Courts to be open; suits against the Commonwealth
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 11. Courts to be open; suits against the Commonwealth
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 11. Courts to be open; suits against the Commonwealth (2023)
content:
All courts shall be open;  and every man for an injury done him in his lands, goods,
   person or reputation shall have remedy by due course of law, and right and justice
   administered without sale, denial or delay.  Suits may be brought against the Commonwealth in such manner, in such courts and
   in such cases as the Legislature may by law direct.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, Preamble
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, Preamble
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, Preamble (2023)
content:
That the general, great and essential principles of liberty and free government may
   be recognized and unalterably established, WE DECLARE THAT--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 13. Bail, fines and punishments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 13. Bail, fines and punishments
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 13. Bail, fines and punishments (2023)
content:
Excessive bail shall not be required, nor excessive fines imposed, nor cruel punishments
   inflicted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 10. Initiation of criminal proceedings; twice in jeopardy; eminent domain
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 10. Initiation of criminal proceedings; twice in jeopardy; eminent domain
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 10. Initiation of criminal proceedings; twice in jeopardy; eminent domain (2023)
content:
Except as hereinafter provided no person shall, for any indictable offense, be proceeded
   against criminally by information, except in cases arising in the land or naval forces,
   or in the militia, when in actual service, in time of war or public danger, or by
   leave of the court for oppression or misdemeanor in office.  Each of the several courts of common pleas may, with the approval of the Supreme
   Court, provide for the initiation of criminal proceedings therein by information filed
   in the manner provided by law.  No person shall, for the same offense, be twice put in jeopardy of life or limb;
   nor shall private property be taken or applied to public use, without authority of
   law and without just compensation being first made or secured.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 12. Power of suspending laws
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 12. Power of suspending laws
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 12. Power of suspending laws (2023)
content:
No power of suspending laws shall be exercised unless by the Legislature or by its
   authority.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 14. Prisoners to be bailable; habeas corpus
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 14. Prisoners to be bailable; habeas corpus
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 14. Prisoners to be bailable; habeas corpus (2023)
content:
All prisoners shall be bailable by sufficient sureties, unless for capital offenses
   or for offenses for which the maximum sentence is life imprisonment or unless no condition
   or combination of conditions other than imprisonment will reasonably assure the safety
   of any person and the community when the proof is evident or presumption great;  and
   the privilege of the writ of habeas corpus shall not be suspended, unless when in
   case of rebellion or invasion the public safety may require it.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 7. Freedom of press and speech; libels
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 7. Freedom of press and speech; libels
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 7. Freedom of press and speech; libels (2023)
content:
The printing press shall be free to every person who may undertake to examine the
   proceedings of the Legislature or any branch of government, and no law shall ever
   be made to restrain the right thereof.  The free communication of thoughts and opinions is one of the invaluable rights
   of man, and every citizen may freely speak, write and print on any subject, being
   responsible for the abuse of that liberty.  No conviction shall be had in any prosecution for the publication of papers relating
   to the official conduct of officers or men in public capacity, or to any other matter
   proper for public investigation or information, where the fact that such publication
   was not maliciously or negligently made shall be established to the satisfaction of
   the jury;  and in all indictments for libels the jury shall have the right to determine
   the law and the facts, under the direction of the court, as in other cases.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 5. Elections
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 5. Elections
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 5. Elections (2023)
content:
Elections shall be free and equal;  and no power, civil or military, shall at any
   time interfere to prevent the free exercise of the right of suffrage.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 8. Security from searches and seizures
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 8. Security from searches and seizures
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 8. Security from searches and seizures (2023)
content:
The people shall be secure in their persons, houses, papers and possessions from unreasonable
   searches and seizures, and no warrant to search any place or to seize any person or
   things shall issue without describing them as nearly as may be, nor without probable
   cause, supported by oath or affirmation subscribed to by the affiant.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 3. Religious freedom
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 3. Religious freedom
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 3. Religious freedom (2023)
content:
All men have a natural and indefeasible right to worship Almighty God according to
   the dictates of their own consciences;  no man can of right be compelled to attend,
   erect or support any place of worship, or to maintain any ministry against his consent;
   no human authority can, in any case whatever, control or interfere with the rights
   of conscience, and no preference shall ever be given by law to any religious establishments
   or modes of worship.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 1. Inherent rights of mankind
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 1. Inherent rights of mankind
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 1. Inherent rights of mankind (2023)
content:
All men are born equally free and independent, and have certain inherent and indefeasible
   rights, among which are those of enjoying and defending life and liberty, of acquiring,
   possessing and protecting property and reputation, and of pursuing their own happiness.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 2. Political powers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 2. Political powers
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 2. Political powers (2023)
content:
All power is inherent in the people, and all free governments are founded on their
   authority and instituted for their peace, safety and happiness.  For the advancement of these ends they have at all times an inalienable and indefeasible
   right to alter, reform or abolish their government in such manner as they may think
   proper.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 9. Rights of accused in criminal prosecutions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 9. Rights of accused in criminal prosecutions
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 9. Rights of accused in criminal prosecutions (2023)
content:
In all criminal prosecutions the accused hath a right to be heard by himself and his
   counsel, to demand the nature and cause of the accusation against him, to be confronted
   with the witnesses against him, to have compulsory process for obtaining witnesses
   in his favor, and, in prosecutions by indictment or information, a speedy public trial
   by an impartial jury of the vicinage;  he cannot be compelled to give evidence against
   himself, nor can he be deprived of his life, liberty or property, unless by the judgment
   of his peers or the law of the land.  The use of a suppressed voluntary admission or voluntary confession to impeach the
   credibility of a person may be permitted and shall not be construed as compelling
   a person to give evidence against himself.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 16. Insolvent debtors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 16. Insolvent debtors
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 16. Insolvent debtors (2023)
content:
The person of a debtor, where there is not strong presumption of fraud, shall not
   be continued in prison after delivering up his estate for the benefit of his creditors
   in such manner as shall be prescribed by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 6. Trial by jury
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 6. Trial by jury
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 6. Trial by jury (2023)
content:
Trial by jury shall be as heretofore, and the right thereof remain inviolate.  The General Assembly may provide, however, by law, that a verdict may be rendered
   by not less than five-sixths of the jury in any civil case.  Furthermore, in criminal cases the Commonwealth shall have the same right to trial
   by jury as does the accused.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 15. Special criminal tribunals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 15. Special criminal tribunals
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 15. Special criminal tribunals (2023)
content:
No commission shall issue creating special temporary criminal tribunals to try particular
   individuals or particular classes of cases.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 21. Right to bear arms
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 21. Right to bear arms
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 21. Right to bear arms (2023)
content:
The right of the citizens to bear arms in defence of themselves and the State shall
   not be questioned.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 20. Right of petition
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 20. Right of petition
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 20. Right of petition (2023)
content:
The citizens have a right in a peaceable manner to assemble together for their common
   good, and to apply to those invested with the powers of government for redress of
   grievances or other proper purposes, by petition, address or remonstrance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 18. Attainder
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 18. Attainder
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 18. Attainder (2023)
content: No person shall be attainted of treason or felony by the Legislature.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 19. Attainder limited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 19. Attainder limited
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 19. Attainder limited (2023)
content:
No attainder shall work corruption of blood, nor, except during the life of the offender,
   forfeiture of estate to the Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 17. Ex post facto laws; impairment of contracts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 17. Ex post facto laws; impairment of contracts
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 17. Ex post facto laws; impairment of contracts (2023)
content:
Noex post factolaw, nor any law impairing the obligation of contracts, or making irrevocable any
   grant of special privileges or immunities, shall be passed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article II. The Legislature›PA CONST Art. II, § 1. Legislative power
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article II. The Legislature › PA CONST Art. II, § 1. Legislative power
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. II, § 1. Legislative power (2023)
content:
The legislative power of this Commonwealth shall be vested in a General Assembly,
   which shall consist of a Senate and a House of Representatives.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 4. Religion
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 4. Religion
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 4. Religion (2023)
content:
No person who acknowledges the being of a God and a future state of rewards and punishments
   shall, on account of his religious sentiments, be disqualified to hold any office
   or place of trust or profit under this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 22. Standing army; military subordinate to civil power
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 22. Standing army; military subordinate to civil power
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 22. Standing army; military subordinate to civil power (2023)
content:
No standing army shall, in time of peace, be kept up without the consent of the Legislature,
   and the military shall in all cases and at all times be in strict subordination to
   the civil power.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 24. Titles and offices
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 24. Titles and offices
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 24. Titles and offices (2023)
content:
The Legislature shall not grant any title of nobility or hereditary distinction, nor
   create any office the appointment to which shall be for a longer term than during
   good behavior.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 23. Quartering of troops
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 23. Quartering of troops
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 23. Quartering of troops (2023)
content:
No soldier shall in time of peace be quartered in any house without the consent of
   the owner, nor in time of war but in a manner to be prescribed by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 28. Prohibition against denial or abridgment of equality of rights because of sex
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 28. Prohibition against denial or abridgment of equality of rights because of sex
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 28. Prohibition against denial or abridgment of equality of rights because of sex (2023)
content:
Equality of rights under the law shall not be denied or abridged in the Commonwealth
   of Pennsylvania because of the sex of the individual.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article II. The Legislature›PA CONST Art. II, § 4. Sessions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article II. The Legislature › PA CONST Art. II, § 4. Sessions
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. II, § 4. Sessions (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall be a continuing body during the term for which its Representatives
   are elected.  It shall meet at twelve o'clock noon on the first Tuesday of January each year.  Special sessions shall be called by the Governor on petition of a majority of the
   members elected to each House or may be called by the Governor whenever in his opinion
   the public interest requires.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 27. Natural resources and the public estate
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 27. Natural resources and the public estate
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 27. Natural resources and the public estate (2023)
content:
The people have a right to clean air, pure water, and to the preservation of the natural,
   scenic, historic and esthetic values of the environment.  Pennsylvania's public natural resources are the common property of all the people,
   including generations yet to come.  As trustee of these resources, the Commonwealth shall conserve and maintain them
   for the benefit of all the people.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 26. No discrimination by Commonwealth and its political subdivisions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 26. No discrimination by Commonwealth and its political subdivisions
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 26. No discrimination by Commonwealth and its political subdivisions (2023)
content:
Neither the Commonwealth nor any political subdivision thereof shall deny to any person
   the enjoyment of any civil right, nor discriminate against any person in the exercise
   of any civil right.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article II. The Legislature›PA CONST Art. II, § 3. Terms of members
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article II. The Legislature › PA CONST Art. II, § 3. Terms of members
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. II, § 3. Terms of members (2023)
content:
Senators shall be elected for the term of four years and Representatives for the term
   of two years.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 25. Reservation of powers in people
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 25. Reservation of powers in people
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 25. Reservation of powers in people (2023)
content:
To guard against transgressions of the high powers which we have delegated, we declare
   that everything in this article is excepted out of the general powers of government
   and shall forever remain inviolate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article I. Declaration of Rights›PA CONST Art. I, § 29. Prohibition against denial or abridgment of equality of rights because of race and ethnicity
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article I. Declaration of Rights › PA CONST Art. I, § 29. Prohibition against denial or abridgment of equality of rights because of race and ethnicity
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. I, § 29. Prohibition against denial or abridgment of equality of rights because of race and ethnicity (2023)
content:
Equality of rights under the law shall not be denied or abridged in the Commonwealth
   of Pennsylvania because of the race or ethnicity of the individual.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article II. The Legislature›PA CONST Art. II, § 2. Election of members; vacancies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article II. The Legislature › PA CONST Art. II, § 2. Election of members; vacancies
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. II, § 2. Election of members; vacancies (2023)
content:
Members of the General Assembly shall be chosen at the general election every second
   year.  Their term of service shall begin on the first day of December next after their
   election.  Whenever a vacancy shall occur in either House, the presiding officer thereof shall
   issue a writ of election to fill such vacancy for the remainder of the term.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article II. The Legislature›PA CONST Art. II, § 7. Ineligibility by criminal convictions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article II. The Legislature › PA CONST Art. II, § 7. Ineligibility by criminal convictions
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. II, § 7. Ineligibility by criminal convictions (2023)
content:
No person hereafter convicted of embezzlement of public moneys, bribery, perjury or
   other infamous crime, shall be eligible to the General Assembly, or capable of holding
   any office of trust or profit in this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article II. The Legislature›PA CONST Art. II, § 6. Disqualification to hold other office
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article II. The Legislature › PA CONST Art. II, § 6. Disqualification to hold other office
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. II, § 6. Disqualification to hold other office (2023)
content:
No Senator or Representative shall, during the time for which he was elected, be appointed
   to any civil office under this Commonwealth to which a salary, fee or perquisite is
   attached.  No member of Congress or other person holding any office (except of attorney-at-law
   or in the national guard or in a reserve component of the armed forces of the United
   States) under the United States or this Commonwealth to which a salary, fee or perquisite
   is attached shall be a member of either House during his continuance in office.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article II. The Legislature›PA CONST Art. II, § 11. Powers of each house; expulsion
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article II. The Legislature › PA CONST Art. II, § 11. Powers of each house; expulsion
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. II, § 11. Powers of each house; expulsion (2023)
content:
Each House shall have power to determine the rules of its proceedings and punish its
   members or other persons for contempt or disorderly behavior in its presence, to enforce
   obedience to its process, to protect its members against violence or offers of bribes
   or private solicitation, and, with the concurrence of two-thirds, to expel a member,
   but not a second time for the same cause, and shall have all other powers necessary
   for the Legislature of a free State.  A member expelled for corruption shall not thereafter be eligible to either House,
   and punishment for contempt or disorderly behavior shall not bar an indictment for
   the same offense.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article II. The Legislature›PA CONST Art. II, § 5. Qualifications of members
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article II. The Legislature › PA CONST Art. II, § 5. Qualifications of members
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. II, § 5. Qualifications of members (2023)
content:
Senators shall be at least twenty-five years of age and Representatives twenty-one
   years of age.  They shall have been citizens and inhabitants of the State four years, and inhabitants
   of their respective districts one year next before their election (unless absent on
   the public business of the United States or of this State), and shall reside in their
   respective districts during their terms of service.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article II. The Legislature›PA CONST Art. II, § 9. Election of officers; judge of election and qualifications of members
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article II. The Legislature › PA CONST Art. II, § 9. Election of officers; judge of election and qualifications of members
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. II, § 9. Election of officers; judge of election and qualifications of members (2023)
content:
The Senate shall, at the beginning and close of each regular session and at such other
   times as may be necessary, elect one of its members Presidentpro tempore,who shall perform the duties of the Lieutenant Governor, in any case of absence or
   disability of that officer, and whenever the said office of Lieutenant Governor shall
   be vacant.  The House of Representatives shall elect one of its members as Speaker.  Each House shall choose its other officers, and shall judge of the election and
   qualifications of its members.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article II. The Legislature›PA CONST Art. II, § 15. Privileges of members
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article II. The Legislature › PA CONST Art. II, § 15. Privileges of members
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. II, § 15. Privileges of members (2023)
content:
The members of the General Assembly shall in all cases, except treason, felony, violation
   of their oath of office, and breach or surety of the peace, be privileged from arrest
   during their attendance at the sessions of their respective Houses and in going to
   and returning from the same;  and for any speech or debate in either House they shall
   not be questioned in any other place.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article II. The Legislature›PA CONST Art. II, § 10. Quorum
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article II. The Legislature › PA CONST Art. II, § 10. Quorum
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. II, § 10. Quorum (2023)
content:
A majority of each House shall constitute a quorum, but a smaller number may adjourn
   from day to day and compel the attendance of absent members.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article II. The Legislature›PA CONST Art. II, § 12. Journals; yeas and nays
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article II. The Legislature › PA CONST Art. II, § 12. Journals; yeas and nays
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. II, § 12. Journals; yeas and nays (2023)
content:
Each House shall keep a journal of its proceedings and from time to time publish the
   same, except such parts as require secrecy, and the yeas and nays of the members on
   any question shall, at the desire of any two of them, be entered on the journal.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article II. The Legislature›PA CONST Art. II, § 17. Legislative Reapportionment Commission
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article II. The Legislature › PA CONST Art. II, § 17. Legislative Reapportionment Commission
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. II, § 17. Legislative Reapportionment Commission (2023)
content:
(a) In each year following the year of the Federal decennial census, a Legislative
      Reapportionment Commission shall be constituted for the purpose of reapportioning
      the Commonwealth.  The commission shall act by a majority of its entire membership.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›A. Procedure›PA CONST Art. III, § 2. Reference to committee; printing
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › A. Procedure › PA CONST Art. III, § 2. Reference to committee; printing
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 2. Reference to committee; printing (2023)
content:
No bill shall be considered unless referred to a committee, printed for the use of
   the members and returned therefrom.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article II. The Legislature›PA CONST Art. II, § 8. Compensation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article II. The Legislature › PA CONST Art. II, § 8. Compensation
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. II, § 8. Compensation (2023)
content:
The members of the General Assembly shall receive such salary and mileage for regular
   and special sessions as shall be fixed by law, and no other compensation whatever,
   whether for service upon committee or otherwise.  No member of either House shall during the term for which he may have been elected,
   receive any increase of salary, or mileage, under any law passed during such term.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›A. Procedure›PA CONST Art. III, § 1. Passage of laws
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › A. Procedure › PA CONST Art. III, § 1. Passage of laws
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 1. Passage of laws (2023)
content:
No law shall be passed except by bill, and no bill shall be so altered or amended,
   on its passage through either House, as to change its original purpose.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article II. The Legislature›PA CONST Art. II, § 13. Open sessions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article II. The Legislature › PA CONST Art. II, § 13. Open sessions
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. II, § 13. Open sessions (2023)
content:
The sessions of each House and of committees of the whole shall be open, unless when
   the business is such as ought to be kept secret.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article II. The Legislature›PA CONST Art. II, § 14. Adjournments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article II. The Legislature › PA CONST Art. II, § 14. Adjournments
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. II, § 14. Adjournments (2023)
content:
Neither House shall, without the consent of the other, adjourn for more than three
   days, nor to any other place than that in which the two Houses shall be sitting.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›A. Procedure›PA CONST Art. III, § 3. Form of bills
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › A. Procedure › PA CONST Art. III, § 3. Form of bills
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 3. Form of bills (2023)
content:
No bill shall be passed containing more than one subject, which shall be clearly expressed
   in its title, except a general appropriation bill or a bill codifying or compiling
   the law or a part thereof.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article II. The Legislature›PA CONST Art. II, § 16. Legislative districts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article II. The Legislature › PA CONST Art. II, § 16. Legislative districts
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. II, § 16. Legislative districts (2023)
content:
The Commonwealth shall be divided into fifty senatorial and two hundred three representative
   districts, which shall be composed of compact and contiguous territory as nearly equal
   in population as practicable.  Each senatorial district shall elect one Senator, and each representative district
   one Representative.  Unless absolutely necessary no county, city, incorporated town, borough, township
   or ward shall be divided in forming either a senatorial or representative district.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›A. Procedure›PA CONST Art. III, § 4. Consideration of bills
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › A. Procedure › PA CONST Art. III, § 4. Consideration of bills
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 4. Consideration of bills (2023)
content:
Every bill shall be considered on three different days in each House.  All amendments made thereto shall be printed for the use of the members before the
   final vote is taken on the bill and before the final vote is taken, upon written request
   addressed to the presiding officer of either House by at least twenty-five per cent
   of the members elected to that House, any bill shall be read at length in that House.  No bill shall become a law, unless on its final passage the vote is taken by yeas
   and nays, the names of the persons voting for and against it are entered on the journal,
   and a majority of the members elected to each House is recorded thereon as voting
   in its favor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›A. Procedure›PA CONST Art. III, § 5. Concurring in amendments; conference committee reports
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › A. Procedure › PA CONST Art. III, § 5. Concurring in amendments; conference committee reports
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 5. Concurring in amendments; conference committee reports (2023)
content:
No amendment to bills by one House shall be concurred in by the other, except by the
   vote of a majority of the members elected thereto, taken by yeas and nays, and the
   names of those voting for and against recorded upon the journal thereof;  and reports
   of committees of conference shall be adopted in either House only by the vote of a
   majority of the members elected thereto, taken by yeas and nays, and the names of
   those voting recorded upon the journals.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›A. Procedure›PA CONST Art. III, § 6. Revival and amendment of laws
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › A. Procedure › PA CONST Art. III, § 6. Revival and amendment of laws
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 6. Revival and amendment of laws (2023)
content:
No law shall be revived, amended, or the provisions thereof extended or conferred,
   by reference to its title only, but so much thereof as is revived, amended, extended
   or conferred shall be re-enacted and published at length.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›A. Procedure›PA CONST Art. III, § 7. Notice of local and special bills
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › A. Procedure › PA CONST Art. III, § 7. Notice of local and special bills
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 7. Notice of local and special bills (2023)
content:
No local or special bill shall be passed unless notice of the intention to apply therefor
   shall have been published in the locality where the matter or the thing to be effected
   may be situated, which notice shall be at least thirty days prior to the introduction
   into the General Assembly of such bill and in the manner to be provided by law;  the
   evidence of such notice having been published, shall be exhibited in the General Assembly,
   before such act shall be passed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›A. Procedure›PA CONST Art. III, § 9. Action on concurrent orders and resolutions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › A. Procedure › PA CONST Art. III, § 9. Action on concurrent orders and resolutions
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 9. Action on concurrent orders and resolutions (2023)
content:
Every order, resolution or vote, to which the concurrence of both Houses may be necessary,
   except on the questions of adjournment or termination or extension of a disaster emergency
   declaration as declared by an executive order or proclamation, or portion of a disaster
   emergency declaration as declared by an executive order or proclamation, shall be
   presented to the Governor and before it shall take effect be approved by him, or being
   disapproved, shall be repassed by two-thirds of both Houses according to the rules
   and limitations prescribed in case of a bill.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›A. Procedure›PA CONST Art. III, § 11. Appropriation bills
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › A. Procedure › PA CONST Art. III, § 11. Appropriation bills
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 11. Appropriation bills (2023)
content:
The general appropriation bill shall embrace nothing but appropriations for the executive,
   legislative and judicial departments of the Commonwealth, for the public debt and
   for public schools.  All other appropriations shall be made by separate bills, each embracing but one
   subject.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›A. Procedure›PA CONST Art. III, § 8. Signing of bills
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › A. Procedure › PA CONST Art. III, § 8. Signing of bills
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 8. Signing of bills (2023)
content:
The presiding officer of each House shall, in the presence of the House over which
   he presides, sign all bills and joint resolutions passed by the General Assembly,
   after their titles have been publicly read immediately before signing;  and the fact
   of signing shall be entered on the journal.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›A. Procedure›PA CONST Art. III, § 10. Revenue bills
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › A. Procedure › PA CONST Art. III, § 10. Revenue bills
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 10. Revenue bills (2023)
content:
All bills for raising revenue shall originate in the House of Representatives, but
   the Senate may propose amendments as in other bills.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›C. National Guard›PA CONST Art. III, § 16. National Guard to be organized and maintained
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › C. National Guard › PA CONST Art. III, § 16. National Guard to be organized and maintained
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 16. National Guard to be organized and maintained (2023)
content:
The citizens of this Commonwealth shall be armed, organized and disciplined for its
   defense when and in such manner as may be directed by law.  The General Assembly shall provide for maintaining the National Guard by appropriations
   from the Treasury of the Commonwealth, and may exempt from State military service
   persons having conscientious scruples against bearing arms.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›A. Procedure›PA CONST Art. III, § 12. Legislation designated by Governor at special sessions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › A. Procedure › PA CONST Art. III, § 12. Legislation designated by Governor at special sessions
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 12. Legislation designated by Governor at special sessions (2023)
content:
When the General Assembly shall be convened in special session, there shall be no
   legislation upon subjects other than those designated in the proclamation of the Governor
   calling such session.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›B. Education›PA CONST Art. III, § 15. Public school money not available to sectarian schools
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › B. Education › PA CONST Art. III, § 15. Public school money not available to sectarian schools
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 15. Public school money not available to sectarian schools (2023)
content:
No money raised for the support of the public schools of the Commonwealth shall be
   appropriated to or used for the support of any sectarian school.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›B. Education›PA CONST Art. III, § 14. Public school system
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › B. Education › PA CONST Art. III, § 14. Public school system
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 14. Public school system (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall provide for the maintenance and support of a thorough and
   efficient system of public education to serve the needs of the Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized›PA CONST Art. III, § 18. Compensation laws allowed to General Assembly
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized › PA CONST Art. III, § 18. Compensation laws allowed to General Assembly
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 18. Compensation laws allowed to General Assembly (2023)
content:
The General Assembly may enact laws requiring the payment by employers, or employers
   and employes jointly, of reasonable compensation for injuries to employes arising
   in the course of their employment, and for occupational diseases of employes, whether
   or not such injuries or diseases result in death, and regardless of fault of employer
   or employe, and fixing the basis of ascertainment of such compensation and the maximum
   and minimum limits thereof, and providing special or general remedies for the collection
   thereof;  but in no other cases shall the General Assembly limit the amount to be
   recovered for injuries resulting in death, or for injuries to persons or property,
   and in case of death from such injuries, the right of action shall survive, and the
   General Assembly shall prescribe for whose benefit such actions shall be prosecuted.  No act shall prescribe any limitations of time within which suits may be brought
   against corporations for injuries to persons or property, or for other causes different
   from those fixed by general laws regulating actions against natural persons, and such
   acts now existing are avoided.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›A. Procedure›PA CONST Art. III, § 13. Vote denied members with personal interest
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › A. Procedure › PA CONST Art. III, § 13. Vote denied members with personal interest
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 13. Vote denied members with personal interest (2023)
content:
A member who has a personal or private interest in any measure or bill proposed or
   pending before the General Assembly shall disclose the fact to the House of which
   he is a member, and shall not vote thereon.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized›PA CONST Art. III, § 19. Appropriations for support of widows and orphans of persons who served in the armed forces
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized › PA CONST Art. III, § 19. Appropriations for support of widows and orphans of persons who served in the armed forces
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 19. Appropriations for support of widows and orphans of persons who served in the armed forces (2023)
content:
The General Assembly may make appropriations of money to institutions wherein the
   widows of persons who served in the armed forces are supported or assisted, or the
   orphans of persons who served in the armed forces are maintained and educated;  but
   such appropriations shall be applied exclusively to the support of such widows and
   orphans.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized›PA CONST Art. III, § 20. Classification of municipalities
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized › PA CONST Art. III, § 20. Classification of municipalities
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 20. Classification of municipalities (2023)
content:
The Legislature shall have power to classify counties, cities, boroughs, school districts,
   and townships according to population, and all laws passed relating to each class,
   and all laws passed relating to, and regulating procedure and proceedings in court
   with reference to, any class, shall be deemed general legislation within the meaning
   of this Constitution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized›PA CONST Art. III, § 17. Appointment of legislative officers and employees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized › PA CONST Art. III, § 17. Appointment of legislative officers and employees
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 17. Appointment of legislative officers and employees (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall prescribe by law the number, duties and compensation of
   the officers and employees of each House, and no payment shall be made from the State
   Treasury, or be in any way authorized, to any person, except to an acting officer
   or employee elected or appointed in pursuance of law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized›PA CONST Art. III, § 22. State purchases
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized › PA CONST Art. III, § 22. State purchases
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 22. State purchases (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall maintain by law a system of competitive bidding under which
   all purchases of materials, printing, supplies or other personal property used by
   the government of this Commonwealth shall so far as practicable be made.  The law shall provide that no officer or employe of the Commonwealth shall be in
   any way interested in any purchase made by the Commonwealth under contract or otherwise.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized›PA CONST Art. III, § 21. Land title registration
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized › PA CONST Art. III, § 21. Land title registration
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 21. Land title registration (2023)
content:
Laws may be passed providing for a system of registering, transferring, insuring of
   and guaranteeing land titles by the State, or by the counties thereof, and for settling
   and determining adverse or other claims to and interest in lands the titles to which
   are so registered, transferred, insured, and guaranteed;  and for the creation and
   collection of indemnity funds;  and for carrying the system and powers hereby provided
   for into effect by such existing courts as may be designated by the Legislature.  Such laws may provide for continuing the registering, transferring, insuring, and
   guaranteeing such titles after the first or original registration has been perfected
   by the court, and provision may be made for raising the necessary funds for expenses
   and salaries of officers, which shall be paid out of the treasury of the several counties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized›PA CONST Art. III, § 23. Change of venue
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized › PA CONST Art. III, § 23. Change of venue
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 23. Change of venue (2023)
content:
The power to change the venue in civil and criminal cases shall be vested in the courts,
   to be exercised in such manner as shall be provided by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized›PA CONST Art. III, § 26. Extra compensation prohibited; claims against the Commonwealth; pensions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized › PA CONST Art. III, § 26. Extra compensation prohibited; claims against the Commonwealth; pensions
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 26. Extra compensation prohibited; claims against the Commonwealth; pensions (2023)
content:
No bill shall be passed giving any extra compensation to any public officer, servant,
   employe, agent or contractor, after services shall have been rendered or contract
   made, nor providing for the payment of any claim against the Commonwealth without
   previous authority of law:  Provided, however, That nothing in this Constitution shall
   be construed to prohibit the General Assembly from authorizing the increase of retirement
   allowances or pensions of members of a retirement or pension system now in effect
   or hereafter legally constituted by the Commonwealth, its political subdivisions,
   agencies or instrumentalities, after the termination of the services of said member.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›E. Restrictions on Legislative Power›PA CONST Art. III, § 28. Change of permanent location of State Capital
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › E. Restrictions on Legislative Power › PA CONST Art. III, § 28. Change of permanent location of State Capital
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 28. Change of permanent location of State Capital (2023)
content:
No law changing the permanent location of the Capital of the State shall be valid
   until the same shall have been submitted to the qualified electors of the Commonwealth
   at a general election and ratified and approved by them.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized›PA CONST Art. III, § 25. Emergency seats of government
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized › PA CONST Art. III, § 25. Emergency seats of government
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 25. Emergency seats of government (2023)
content:
The General Assembly may provide, by law, during any session, for the continuity of
   the executive, legislative, and judicial functions of the government of the Commonwealth,
   and its political subdivisions, and the establishment of emergency seats thereof and
   any such laws heretofore enacted are validated.  Such legislation shall become effective in the event of an attack by an enemy of
   the United States.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized›PA CONST Art. III, § 27. Changes in term of office or salary prohibited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized › PA CONST Art. III, § 27. Changes in term of office or salary prohibited
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 27. Changes in term of office or salary prohibited (2023)
content:
No law shall extend the term of any public officer, or increase or diminish his salary
   or emoluments, after his election or appointment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 4. Lieutenant Governor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 4. Lieutenant Governor
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 4. Lieutenant Governor (2023)
content:
A Lieutenant Governor shall be chosen jointly with the Governor by the casting by
   each voter of a single vote applicable to both offices, for the same term, and subject
   to the same provisions as the Governor;  he shall be President of the Senate.  As such, he may vote in case of a tie on any question except the final passage of
   a bill or joint resolution, the adoption of a conference report or the concurrence
   in amendments made by the House of Representatives.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 2. Duties of Governor; election procedure; tie or contest
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 2. Duties of Governor; election procedure; tie or contest
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 2. Duties of Governor; election procedure; tie or contest (2023)
content:
The supreme executive power shall be vested in the Governor, who shall take care that
   the laws be faithfully executed;  he shall be chosen on the day of the general election,
   by the qualified electors of the Commonwealth, at the places where they shall vote
   for Representatives.  The returns of every election for Governor shall be sealed up and transmitted to
   the seat of government, directed to the President of the Senate, who shall open and
   publish them in the presence of the members of both Houses of the General Assembly.  The person having the highest number of votes shall be Governor, but if two or more
   be equal and highest in votes, one of them shall be chosen Governor by the joint vote
   of the members of both Houses.  Contested elections shall be determined by a committee, to be selected from both
   Houses of the General Assembly, and formed and regulated in such manner as shall be
   directed by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized›PA CONST Art. III, § 24. Paying out public moneys
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › D. Other Legislation Specifically Authorized › PA CONST Art. III, § 24. Paying out public moneys
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 24. Paying out public moneys (2023)
content:
No money shall be paid out of the treasury, except on appropriations made by law and
   on warrant issued by the proper officers;  but cash refunds of taxes, licenses, fees
   and other charges paid or collected, but not legally due, may be paid, as provided
   by law, without appropriation from the fund into which they were paid on warrant of
   the proper officer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 1. Executive Department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 1. Executive Department
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 1. Executive Department (2023)
content:
The Executive Department of this Commonwealth shall consist of a Governor, Lieutenant
   Governor, Attorney General, Auditor General, State Treasurer, and Superintendent of
   Public Instruction1and such other officers as the General Assembly may from time to time prescribe.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›E. Restrictions on Legislative Power›PA CONST Art. III, § 29. Appropriations for public assistance, military service, scholarships
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › E. Restrictions on Legislative Power › PA CONST Art. III, § 29. Appropriations for public assistance, military service, scholarships
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 29. Appropriations for public assistance, military service, scholarships (2023)
content:
No appropriation shall be made for charitable, educational or benevolent purposes
   to any person or community nor to any denominational and sectarian institution, corporation
   or association:  Provided, That appropriations may be made for pensions or gratuities
   for military service and to blind persons twenty-one years of age and upwards and
   for assistance to mothers having dependent children and to aged persons without adequate
   means of support and in the form of scholarship grants or loans for higher educational
   purposes to residents of the Commonwealth enrolled in institutions of higher learning
   except that no scholarship, grants or loans for higher educational purposes shall
   be given to persons enrolled in a theological seminary or school of theology.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›E. Restrictions on Legislative Power›PA CONST Art. III, § 32. Certain local and special laws
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › E. Restrictions on Legislative Power › PA CONST Art. III, § 32. Certain local and special laws
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 32. Certain local and special laws (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall pass no local or special law in any case which has been
   or can be provided for by general law and specifically the General Assembly shall
   not pass any local or special law:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›E. Restrictions on Legislative Power›PA CONST Art. III, § 30. Charitable and educational appropriations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › E. Restrictions on Legislative Power › PA CONST Art. III, § 30. Charitable and educational appropriations
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 30. Charitable and educational appropriations (2023)
content:
No appropriation shall be made to any charitable or educational institution not under
   the absolute control of the Commonwealth, other than normal schools established by
   law for the professional training of teachers for the public schools of the State,
   except by a vote of two-thirds of all the members elected to each House.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article III. Legislation›E. Restrictions on Legislative Power›PA CONST Art. III, § 31. Delegation of certain powers prohibited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article III. Legislation › E. Restrictions on Legislative Power › PA CONST Art. III, § 31. Delegation of certain powers prohibited
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. III, § 31. Delegation of certain powers prohibited (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall not delegate to any special commission, private corporation
   or association, any power to make, supervise or interfere with any municipal improvement,
   money, property or effects, whether held in trust or otherwise, or to levy taxes or
   perform any municipal function whatever.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 6. Disqualification for offices of Governor, Lieutenant Governor and Attorney General
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 6. Disqualification for offices of Governor, Lieutenant Governor and Attorney General
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 6. Disqualification for offices of Governor, Lieutenant Governor and Attorney General (2023)
content:
No member of Congress or person holding any office (except of attorney-at-law or in
   the National Guard or in a reserve component of the armed forces of the United States)
   under the United States or this Commonwealth shall exercise the office of Governor,
   Lieutenant Governor or Attorney General.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 3. Terms of office of Governor; number of terms
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 3. Terms of office of Governor; number of terms
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 3. Terms of office of Governor; number of terms (2023)
content:
The Governor shall hold his office during four years from the third Tuesday of January
   next ensuing his election.  Except for the Governor who may be in office when this amendment is adopted, he
   shall be eligible to succeed himself for one additional term.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 4.1. Attorney General
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 4.1. Attorney General
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 4.1. Attorney General (2023)
content:
An Attorney General shall be chosen by the qualified electors of the Commonwealth
   on the day the general election is held for the Auditor General and State Treasurer;
   he shall hold his office during four years from the third Tuesday of January next
   ensuing his election and shall not be eligible to serve continuously for more than
   two successive terms;  he shall be the chief law officer of the Commonwealth and shall
   exercise such powers and perform such duties as may be imposed by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 8. Appointing power
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 8. Appointing power
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 8. Appointing power (2023)
content:
(a) The Governor shall appoint a Secretary of Education and such other officers as
      he shall be authorized by law to appoint.  The appointment of the Secretary of Education and of such other officers as may
      be specified by law, shall be subject to the consent of two-thirds or a majority of
      the members elected to the Senate as is specified by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 7. Military power
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 7. Military power
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 7. Military power (2023)
content:
The Governor shall be commander-in-chief of the military forces of the Commonwealth,
   except when they shall be called into actual service of the United States.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 10. Information from department officials
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 10. Information from department officials
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 10. Information from department officials (2023)
content:
The Governor may require information in writing from the officers of the Executive
   Department, upon any subject relating to the duties of their respective offices.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 12. Power to convene and adjourn the General Assembly
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 12. Power to convene and adjourn the General Assembly
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 12. Power to convene and adjourn the General Assembly (2023)
content:
He may, on extraordinary occasions, convene the General Assembly, and in case of disagreement
   between the two Houses, with respect to the time of adjournment, adjourn them to such
   time as he shall think proper, not exceeding four months.  He shall have power to convene the Senate in extraordinary session by proclamation
   for the transaction of Executive business.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 11. Messages to the General Assembly
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 11. Messages to the General Assembly
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 11. Messages to the General Assembly (2023)
content:
He shall, from time to time, give to the General Assembly information of the state
   of the Commonwealth, and recommend to their consideration such measures as he may
   judge expedient.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 13. When Lieutenant Governor to act as Governor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 13. When Lieutenant Governor to act as Governor
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 13. When Lieutenant Governor to act as Governor (2023)
content:
In the case of the death, conviction on impeachment, failure to qualify or resignation
   of the Governor, the Lieutenant Governor shall become Governor for the remainder of
   the term and in the case of the disability of the Governor, the powers, duties and
   emoluments of the office shall devolve upon the Lieutenant Governor until the disability
   is removed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 5. Qualifications of Governor, Lieutenant Governor and Attorney General
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 5. Qualifications of Governor, Lieutenant Governor and Attorney General
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 5. Qualifications of Governor, Lieutenant Governor and Attorney General (2023)
content:
No person shall be eligible to the office of Governor, Lieutenant Governor or Attorney
   General except a citizen of the United States, who shall have attained the age of
   30 years, and have been seven years next preceding his election an inhabitant of this
   Commonwealth, unless he shall have been absent on the public business of the United
   States or of this Commonwealth.  No person shall be eligible to the office of Attorney General except a member of
   the bar of the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 16. Partial disapproval of appropriation bills
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 16. Partial disapproval of appropriation bills
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 16. Partial disapproval of appropriation bills (2023)
content:
The Governor shall have power to disapprove of any item or items of any bill, making
   appropriations of money, embracing distinct items, and the part or parts of the bill
   approved shall be the law, and the item or items of appropriation disapproved shall
   be void, unless re-passed according to the rules and limitations prescribed for the
   passage of other bills over the Executive veto.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 17. Contested elections of Governor, Lieutenant Governor and Attorney General; when succeeded
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 17. Contested elections of Governor, Lieutenant Governor and Attorney General; when succeeded
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 17. Contested elections of Governor, Lieutenant Governor and Attorney General; when succeeded (2023)
content:
The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court shall preside upon the trial of any contested
   election of Governor, Lieutenant Governor or Attorney General and shall decide questions
   regarding the admissibility of evidence, and shall, upon request of the committee,
   pronounce his opinion upon other questions of law involved in the trial.  The Governor, Lieutenant Governor and Attorney General shall exercise the duties
   of their respective offices until their successors shall be duly qualified.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 20. Disaster emergency declaration and management
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 20. Disaster emergency declaration and management
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 20. Disaster emergency declaration and management (2023)
content:
(a) A disaster emergency declaration may be declared by executive order or proclamation
      of the Governor upon finding that a disaster has occurred or that the occurrence or
      threat of a disaster is imminent that threatens the health, safety or welfare of this
      Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 14. Vacancy in office of Lieutenant Governor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 14. Vacancy in office of Lieutenant Governor
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 14. Vacancy in office of Lieutenant Governor (2023)
content:
In case of the death, conviction on impeachment, failure to qualify or resignation
   of the Lieutenant Governor, or in case he should become Governor under the preceding
   section, the President pro tempore of the Senate shall become Lieutenant Governor
   for the remainder of the term.  In case of the disability of the Lieutenant Governor, the powers, duties and emoluments
   of the office shall devolve upon the President pro tempore of the Senate until the
   disability is removed.  Should there be no Lieutenant Governor, the President pro tempore of the Senate
   shall become Governor if a vacancy shall occur in the office of Governor and in case
   of the disability of the Governor, the powers, duties and emoluments of the office
   shall devolve upon the President pro tempore of the Senate until the disability is
   removed.  His seat as Senator shall become vacant whenever he shall become Governor and shall
   be filled by election as any other vacancy in the Senate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 9. Pardoning power; Board of Pardons
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 9. Pardoning power; Board of Pardons
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 9. Pardoning power; Board of Pardons (2023)
content:
(a) In all criminal cases except impeachment the Governor shall have power to remit
      fines and forfeitures, to grant reprieves, commutation of sentences and pardons; 
      but no pardon shall be granted, nor sentence commuted, except on the recommendation
      in writing of a majority of the Board of Pardons, and, in the case of a sentence of
      death or life imprisonment, on the unanimous recommendation in writing of the Board
      of Pardons, after full hearing in open session, upon due public notice.  The recommendation, with the reasons therefor at length, shall be delivered to the
      Governor and a copy thereof shall be kept on file in the office of the Lieutenant
      Governor in a docket kept for that purpose.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 15. Approval of bills; vetoes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 15. Approval of bills; vetoes
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 15. Approval of bills; vetoes (2023)
content:
Every bill which shall have passed both Houses shall be presented to the Governor;
   if he approves he shall sign it, but if he shall not approve he shall return it with
   his objections to the House in which it shall have originated, which House shall enter
   the objections at large upon their journal, and proceed to re-consider it.  If after such re-consideration, two-thirds of all the members elected to that House
   shall agree to pass the bill, it shall be sent with the objections to the other House
   by which likewise it shall be re-considered, and if approved by two-thirds of all
