   the members elected to that House it shall be a law;  but in such cases the votes
   of both Houses shall be determined by yeas and nays, and the names of the members
   voting for and against the bill shall be entered on the journals of each House, respectively.  If any bill shall not be returned by the Governor within ten days after it shall
   have been presented to him, the same shall be a law in like manner as if he had signed
   it, unless the General Assembly, by their adjournment, prevent its return, in which
   case it shall be a law, unless he shall file the same, with his objections, in the
   office of the Secretary of the Commonwealth, and give notice thereof by public proclamation
   within thirty days after such adjournment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article V. The Judiciary›PA CONST Art. V, § 1. Unified judicial system
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article V. The Judiciary › PA CONST Art. V, § 1. Unified judicial system
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. V, § 1. Unified judicial system (2023)
content:
The judicial power of the Commonwealth shall be vested in a unified judicial system
   consisting of the Supreme Court, the Superior Court, the Commonwealth Court, courts
   of common pleas, community courts, municipal courts in the City of Philadelphia, such
   other courts as may be provided by law and justices of the peace.1All courts and justices of the peace and their jurisdiction shall be in this unified
   judicial system.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 19. State seal; commissions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 19. State seal; commissions
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 19. State seal; commissions (2023)
content:
The present Great Seal of Pennsylvania shall be the seal of the State.  All commissions shall be in the name and by authority of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania,
   and be sealed with the State seal and signed by the Governor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article V. The Judiciary›PA CONST Art. V, § 3. Superior Court
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article V. The Judiciary › PA CONST Art. V, § 3. Superior Court
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. V, § 3. Superior Court (2023)
content:
The Superior Court shall be a statewide court, and shall consist of the number of
   judges, which shall be not less than seven judges, and have such jurisdiction as shall
   be provided by this Constitution or by the General Assembly.  One of its judges shall be the president judge.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article V. The Judiciary›PA CONST Art. V, § 6. Community courts; Philadelphia Municipal Court
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article V. The Judiciary › PA CONST Art. V, § 6. Community courts; Philadelphia Municipal Court
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. V, § 6. Community courts; Philadelphia Municipal Court (2023)

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article V. The Judiciary›PA CONST Art. V, § 2. Supreme Court
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article V. The Judiciary › PA CONST Art. V, § 2. Supreme Court
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. V, § 2. Supreme Court (2023)
content:
The Supreme Court (a) shall be the highest court of the Commonwealth and in this court
      shall be reposed the supreme judicial power of the Commonwealth;

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IV. The Executive›PA CONST Art. IV, § 18. Terms of office of Auditor General and State Treasurer; number of terms; eligibility of State Treasurer to become Auditor General
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IV. The Executive › PA CONST Art. IV, § 18. Terms of office of Auditor General and State Treasurer; number of terms; eligibility of State Treasurer to become Auditor General
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IV, § 18. Terms of office of Auditor General and State Treasurer; number of terms; eligibility of State Treasurer to become Auditor General (2023)
content:
The terms of the Auditor General and of the State Treasurer shall each be four years
   from the third Tuesday of January next ensuing his election.  They shall be chosen by the qualified electors of the Commonwealth at general elections
   but shall not be eligible to serve continuously for more than two successive terms.  The State Treasurer shall not be eligible to the office of Auditor General until
   four years after he has been State Treasurer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article V. The Judiciary›PA CONST Art. V, § 5. Courts of common pleas
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article V. The Judiciary › PA CONST Art. V, § 5. Courts of common pleas
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. V, § 5. Courts of common pleas (2023)
content:
There shall be one court of common pleas for each judicial district (a) having such
      divisions and consisting of such number of judges as shall be provided by law, one
      of whom shall be the president judge;  and

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article V. The Judiciary›PA CONST Art. V, § 7. Justices of the peace; magisterial districts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article V. The Judiciary › PA CONST Art. V, § 7. Justices of the peace; magisterial districts
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. V, § 7. Justices of the peace; magisterial districts (2023)
content:
(a) In any judicial district, other than the City of Philadelphia, where a community
      court has not been established or where one has been discontinued there shall be one
      justice of the peace1in each magisterial district.  The jurisdiction of the justice of the peace shall be as provided by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article V. The Judiciary›PA CONST Art. V, § 4. Commonwealth Court
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article V. The Judiciary › PA CONST Art. V, § 4. Commonwealth Court
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. V, § 4. Commonwealth Court (2023)
content:
The Commonwealth Court shall be a statewide court, and shall consist of the number
   of judges and have such jurisdiction as shall be provided by law.  One of its judges shall be the president judge.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article V. The Judiciary›PA CONST Art. V, § 12. Qualifications of justices, judges and justices of the peace
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article V. The Judiciary › PA CONST Art. V, § 12. Qualifications of justices, judges and justices of the peace
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. V, § 12. Qualifications of justices, judges and justices of the peace (2023)
content:
(a) Justices, judges and justices of the peace1shall be citizens of the Commonwealth.  Justices and judges, except the judges of the traffic court in the City of Philadelphia,
      shall be members of the bar of the Supreme Court.  Justices and judges of statewide courts, for a period of one year preceding their
      election or appointment and during their continuance in office, shall reside within
      the Commonwealth.  Other judges and justices of the peace, for a period of one year preceding their
      election or appointment and during their continuance in office, shall reside within
      their respective districts, except as provided in this article for temporary assignments.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article V. The Judiciary›PA CONST Art. V, § 10. Judicial administration
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article V. The Judiciary › PA CONST Art. V, § 10. Judicial administration
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. V, § 10. Judicial administration (2023)
content:
(a) The Supreme Court shall exercise general supervisory and administrative authority
      over all the courts and justices of the peace,1including authority to temporarily assign judges and justices of the peace from one
      court or district to another as it deems appropriate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article V. The Judiciary›PA CONST Art. V, § 9. Right of appeal
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article V. The Judiciary › PA CONST Art. V, § 9. Right of appeal
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. V, § 9. Right of appeal (2023)
content:
There shall be a right of appeal in all cases to a court of record from a court not
   of record;  and there shall also be a right of appeal from a court of record or from
   an administrative agency to a court of record or to an appellate court, the selection
   of such court to be as provided by law;  and there shall be such other rights of appeal
   as may be provided by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article V. The Judiciary›PA CONST Art. V, § 8. Other courts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article V. The Judiciary › PA CONST Art. V, § 8. Other courts
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. V, § 8. Other courts (2023)
content:
The General Assembly may establish additional courts or divisions of existing courts,
   as needed, or abolish any statutory court or division thereof.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article V. The Judiciary›PA CONST Art. V, § 11. Judicial districts; boundaries
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article V. The Judiciary › PA CONST Art. V, § 11. Judicial districts; boundaries
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. V, § 11. Judicial districts; boundaries (2023)
content:
The number and boundaries of judicial districts shall be changed by the General Assembly
   only with the advice and consent of the Supreme Court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article V. The Judiciary›PA CONST Art. V, § 13. Election of justices, judges and justices of the peace; vacancies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article V. The Judiciary › PA CONST Art. V, § 13. Election of justices, judges and justices of the peace; vacancies
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. V, § 13. Election of justices, judges and justices of the peace; vacancies (2023)
content:
(a) Justices, judges and justices of the peace1shall be elected at the municipal election next preceding the commencement of their
      respective terms of office by the electors of the Commonwealth or the respective districts
      in which they are to serve.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article V. The Judiciary›PA CONST Art. V, § 14. Judicial Qualifications Commission
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article V. The Judiciary › PA CONST Art. V, § 14. Judicial Qualifications Commission
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. V, § 14. Judicial Qualifications Commission (2023)
content:
(a) Should the method of judicial selection be adopted as provided insection 13(d), there shall be a Judicial Qualifications Commission, composed of four non-lawyer
      electors appointed by the Governor and three non-judge members of the bar of the Supreme
      Court appointed by the Supreme Court.  No more than four members shall be of the same political party.  The members of the commission shall serve for terms of seven years, with one member
      being selected each year.  The commission shall consider all names submitted to it and recommend to the Governor
      not fewer than ten nor more than twenty of those qualified for each vacancy to be
      filled.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article V. The Judiciary›PA CONST Art. V, § 15. Tenure of justices, judges and justices of the peace
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article V. The Judiciary › PA CONST Art. V, § 15. Tenure of justices, judges and justices of the peace
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. V, § 15. Tenure of justices, judges and justices of the peace (2023)
content:
(a) The regular term of office of justices and judges shall be ten years and the regular
      term of office for judges of the municipal court in the City of Philadelphia and of
      justices of the peace1shall be six years.  The tenure of any justice or judge shall not be affected by changes in judicial
      districts or by reduction in the number of judges.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VI. Public Officers›PA CONST Art. VI, § 1. Selection of officers not otherwise provided for in Constitution
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VI. Public Officers › PA CONST Art. VI, § 1. Selection of officers not otherwise provided for in Constitution
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VI, § 1. Selection of officers not otherwise provided for in Constitution (2023)
content:
All officers, whose selection is not provided for in this Constitution, shall be elected
   or appointed as may be directed by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VI. Public Officers›PA CONST Art. VI, § 2. Incompatible offices
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VI. Public Officers › PA CONST Art. VI, § 2. Incompatible offices
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VI, § 2. Incompatible offices (2023)
content:
No member of Congress from this State, nor any person holding or exercising any office
   or appointment of trust or profit under the United States, shall at the same time
   hold or exercise any office in this State to which a salary, fees or perquisites shall
   be attached.  The General Assembly may by law declare what offices are incompatible.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VI. Public Officers›PA CONST Art. VI, § 5. Trial of impeachments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VI. Public Officers › PA CONST Art. VI, § 5. Trial of impeachments
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VI, § 5. Trial of impeachments (2023)
content:
All impeachments shall be tried by the Senate.  When sitting for that purpose the Senators shall be upon oath or affirmation.  No person shall be convicted without the concurrence of two-thirds of the members
   present.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article V. The Judiciary›PA CONST Art. V, § 17. Prohibited activities
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article V. The Judiciary › PA CONST Art. V, § 17. Prohibited activities
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. V, § 17. Prohibited activities (2023)
content:
(a) Justices and judges shall devote full time to their judicial duties, and shall
      not engage in the practice of law, hold office in a political party or political organization,
      or hold an office or position of profit in the government of the United States, the
      Commonwealth or any municipal corporation or political subdivision thereof, except
      in the armed service of the United States or the Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article V. The Judiciary›PA CONST Art. V, § 18. Suspension, removal, discipline and other sanctions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article V. The Judiciary › PA CONST Art. V, § 18. Suspension, removal, discipline and other sanctions
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. V, § 18. Suspension, removal, discipline and other sanctions (2023)
content:
(a) There shall be an independent board within the Judicial Branch, known as the Judicial
      Conduct Board, the composition, powers and duties of which shall be as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VII. Elections›PA CONST Art. VII, § 3. Municipal election day; offices to be filled on election days
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VII. Elections › PA CONST Art. VII, § 3. Municipal election day; offices to be filled on election days
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VII, § 3. Municipal election day; offices to be filled on election days (2023)
content:
All judges elected by the electors of the State at large may be elected at either
   a general or municipal election, as circumstances may require.  All elections for judges of the courts for the several judicial districts, and for
   county, city, ward, borough, and township officers, for regular terms of service,
   shall be held on the municipal election day;  namely, the Tuesday next following the
   first Monday of November in each odd-numbered year, but the General Assembly may by
   law fix a different day, two-thirds of all the members of each House consenting thereto:
   Provided, That such elections shall be held in an odd-numbered year:  Provided further,
   That all judges for the courts of the several judicial districts holding office at
   the present time, whose terms of office may end in an odd-numbered year, shall continue
   to hold their offices until the first Monday of January in the next succeeding even-numbered
   year.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article V. The Judiciary›PA CONST Art. V, § 16. Compensation and retirement of justices, judges and justices of the peace
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article V. The Judiciary › PA CONST Art. V, § 16. Compensation and retirement of justices, judges and justices of the peace
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. V, § 16. Compensation and retirement of justices, judges and justices of the peace (2023)
content:
(a) Justices, judges and justices of the peace1shall be compensated by the Commonwealth as provided by law.  Their compensation shall not be diminished during their terms of office, unless
      by law applying generally to all salaried officers of the Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VII. Elections›PA CONST Art. VII, § 2. General election day
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VII. Elections › PA CONST Art. VII, § 2. General election day
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VII, § 2. General election day (2023)
content:
The general election shall be held biennially on the Tuesday next following the first
   Monday of November in each even-numbered year, but the General Assembly may by law
   fix a different day, two-thirds of all the members of each House consenting thereto:
   Provided, That such election shall always be held in an even-numbered year.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VII. Elections›PA CONST Art. VII, § 1. Qualifications of electors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VII. Elections › PA CONST Art. VII, § 1. Qualifications of electors
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VII, § 1. Qualifications of electors (2023)
content:
Every citizen twenty-one years of age, possessing the following qualifications, shall
   be entitled to vote at all elections subject, however, to such laws requiring and
   regulating the registration of electors as the General Assembly may enact.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VII. Elections›PA CONST Art. VII, § 4. Method of elections; secrecy in voting
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VII. Elections › PA CONST Art. VII, § 4. Method of elections; secrecy in voting
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VII, § 4. Method of elections; secrecy in voting (2023)
content:
All elections by the citizens shall be by ballot or by such other method as may be
   prescribed by law:  Provided, That secrecy in voting be preserved.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VI. Public Officers›PA CONST Art. VI, § 6. Officers liable to impeachment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VI. Public Officers › PA CONST Art. VI, § 6. Officers liable to impeachment
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VI, § 6. Officers liable to impeachment (2023)
content:
The Governor and all other civil officers shall be liable to impeachment for any misbehavior
   in office, but judgment in such cases shall not extend further than to removal from
   office and disqualification to hold any office of trust or profit under this Commonwealth.  The person accused, whether convicted or acquitted, shall nevertheless be liable
   to indictment, trial, judgment and punishment according to law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VI. Public Officers›PA CONST Art. VI, § 3. Oath of office
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VI. Public Officers › PA CONST Art. VI, § 3. Oath of office
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VI, § 3. Oath of office (2023)
content:
Senators, Representatives and all judicial, State and county officers shall, before
   entering on the duties of their respective offices, take and subscribe the following
   oath or affirmation before a person authorized to administer oaths.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VI. Public Officers›PA CONST Art. VI, § 4. Power of impeachment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VI. Public Officers › PA CONST Art. VI, § 4. Power of impeachment
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VI, § 4. Power of impeachment (2023)
content: The House of Representatives shall have the sole power of impeachment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VI. Public Officers›PA CONST Art. VI, § 7. Removal of civil officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VI. Public Officers › PA CONST Art. VI, § 7. Removal of civil officers
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VI, § 7. Removal of civil officers (2023)
content:
All civil officers shall hold their offices on the condition that they behave themselves
   well while in office, and shall be removed on conviction of misbehavior in office
   or of any infamous crime.  Appointed civil officers, other than judges of the courts of record, may be removed
   at the pleasure of the power by which they shall have been appointed.  All civil officers elected by the people, except the Governor, the Lieutenant Governor,
   members of the General Assembly and judges of the courts of record, shall be removed
   by the Governor for reasonable cause, after due notice and full hearing, on the address
   of two-thirds of the Senate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VII. Elections›PA CONST Art. VII, § 8. Witnesses in contested elections
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VII. Elections › PA CONST Art. VII, § 8. Witnesses in contested elections
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VII, § 8. Witnesses in contested elections (2023)
content:
In trials of contested elections and in proceedings for the investigation of elections,
   no person shall be permitted to withhold his testimony upon the ground that it may
   criminate himself or subject him to public infamy;  but such testimony shall not afterwards
   be used against him in any judicial proceedings except for perjury in giving such
   testimony.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VII. Elections›PA CONST Art. VII, § 5. Electors privileged from arrest
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VII. Elections › PA CONST Art. VII, § 5. Electors privileged from arrest
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VII, § 5. Electors privileged from arrest (2023)
content:
Electors shall in all cases except treason, felony and breach or surety of the peace,
   be privileged from arrest during their attendance on elections and in going to and
   returning therefrom.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VII. Elections›PA CONST Art. VII, § 7. Bribery of electors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VII. Elections › PA CONST Art. VII, § 7. Bribery of electors
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VII, § 7. Bribery of electors (2023)
content:
Any person who shall give, or promise or offer to give, to an elector, any money,
   reward or other valuable consideration for his vote at an election, or for withholding
   the same, or who shall give or promise to give such consideration to any other person
   or party for such elector's vote or for the withholding thereof, and any elector who
   shall receive or agree to receive, for himself or for another, any money, reward or
   other valuable consideration for his vote at an election, or for withholding the same,
   shall thereby forfeit the right to vote at such election, and any elector whose right
   to vote shall be challenged for such cause before the election officers, shall be
   required to swear or affirm that the matter of the challenge is untrue before his
   vote shall be received.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VII. Elections›PA CONST Art. VII, § 11. Election officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VII. Elections › PA CONST Art. VII, § 11. Election officers
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VII, § 11. Election officers (2023)
content:
District election boards shall consist of a judge and two inspectors, who shall be
   chosen at municipal elections for such terms as may be provided by law.  Each elector shall have the right to vote for the judge and one inspector, and each
   inspector shall appoint one clerk.  The first election board for any new district shall be selected, and vacancies in
   election boards filled, as shall be provided by law.  Election officers shall be privileged from arrest upon days of election, and while
   engaged in making up and transmitting returns, except upon warrant of a court of record
   or judge thereof, for an election fraud, for felony, or for wanton breach of the peace.  In cities they may claim exemption from jury duty during their terms of service.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VII. Elections›PA CONST Art. VII, § 9. Fixing election districts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VII. Elections › PA CONST Art. VII, § 9. Fixing election districts
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VII, § 9. Fixing election districts (2023)
content:
Townships and wards of cities and boroughs shall form or be divided into election
   districts of compact and contiguous territory and their boundaries fixed and changed
   in such manner as may be provided by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VII. Elections›PA CONST Art. VII, § 10. Viva voce elections
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VII. Elections › PA CONST Art. VII, § 10. Viva voce elections
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VII, § 10. Viva voce elections (2023)
content: All elections by persons in a representative capacity shall beviva voceor by automatic recording device publicly indicating how each person voted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VII. Elections›PA CONST Art. VII, § 6. Election and registration laws
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VII. Elections › PA CONST Art. VII, § 6. Election and registration laws
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VII, § 6. Election and registration laws (2023)
content:
All laws regulating the holding of elections by the citizens, or for the registration
   of electors, shall be uniform throughout the State, except that laws regulating and
   requiring the registration of electors may be enacted to apply to cities only, provided
   that such laws be uniform for cities of the same class, and except further, that the
   General Assembly shall, by general law, permit the use of voting machines, or other
   mechanical devices for registering or recording and computing the vote, at all elections
   or primaries, in any county, city, borough, incorporated town or township of the Commonwealth,
   at the option of the electors of such county, city, borough, incorporated town or
   township, without being obliged to require the use of such voting machines or mechanical
   devices in any other county, city, borough, incorporated town or township, under such
   regulations with reference thereto as the General Assembly may from time to time prescribe.  The General Assembly may, from time to time, prescribe the number and duties of
   election officers in any political subdivision of the Commonwealth in which voting
   machines or other mechanical devices authorized by this section may be used.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VII. Elections›PA CONST Art. VII, § 13. Contested elections
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VII. Elections › PA CONST Art. VII, § 13. Contested elections
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VII, § 13. Contested elections (2023)
content:
The trial and determination of contested elections of electors of President and Vice-President,
   members of the General Assembly, and of all public officers, whether State, judicial,
   municipal or local, and contests involving questions submitted to the electors at
   any election shall be by the courts of law, or by one or more of the law judges thereof.  The General Assembly shall, by general law, designate the courts and judges by whom
   the several classes of election contests shall be tried, and regulate the manner of
   trial and all matters incident thereto;  but no such law assigning jurisdiction, or
   regulating its exercise, shall apply to any contest arising out of an election held
   before its passage.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VII. Elections›PA CONST Art. VII, § 12. Disqualifications for service as election officer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VII. Elections › PA CONST Art. VII, § 12. Disqualifications for service as election officer
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VII, § 12. Disqualifications for service as election officer (2023)
content:
No person shall be qualified to serve as an election officer who shall hold, or shall
   within two months have held any office, appointment or employment in or under the
   government of the United States, or of this State, or of any city, or county, or of
   any municipal board, commission or trust in any city, save only notaries public and
   persons in the national guard or in a reserve component of the armed forces of the
   United States;  nor shall any election officer be eligible to any civil office to
   be filled at an election at which he shall serve, save only to such subordinate municipal
   or local offices, below the grade of city or county offices, as shall be designated
   by general law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VIII. Taxation and Finance›PA CONST Art. VIII, § 3. Reciprocal exemptions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VIII. Taxation and Finance › PA CONST Art. VIII, § 3. Reciprocal exemptions
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VIII, § 3. Reciprocal exemptions (2023)
content:
Taxation laws may grant exemptions or rebates to residents, or estates of residents,
   of other States which grant similar exemptions or rebates to residents, or estates
   of residents, of Pennsylvania.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VIII. Taxation and Finance›PA CONST Art. VIII, § 4. Public utilities
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VIII. Taxation and Finance › PA CONST Art. VIII, § 4. Public utilities
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VIII, § 4. Public utilities (2023)
content:
The real property of public utilities is subject to real estate taxes imposed by local
   taxing authorities.  Payment to the Commonwealth of gross receipts taxes or other special taxes in replacement
   of gross receipts taxes by a public utility and the distribution by the Commonwealth
   to the local taxing authorities of the amount as herein provided shall, however, be
   in lieu of local taxes upon its real property which is used or useful in furnishing
   its public utility service.  The amount raised annually by such gross receipts or other special taxes shall not
   be less than the gross amount of real estate taxes which the local taxing authorities
   could have imposed upon such real property but for the exemption herein provided.  This gross amount shall be determined in the manner provided by law.  An amount equivalent to such real estate taxes shall be distributed annually among
   all local taxing authorities in the proportion which the total tax receipts of each
   local taxing authority bear to the total tax receipts of all local taxing authorities,
   or in such other equitable proportions as may be provided by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VIII. Taxation and Finance›PA CONST Art. VIII, § 1. Uniformity of taxation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VIII. Taxation and Finance › PA CONST Art. VIII, § 1. Uniformity of taxation
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VIII, § 1. Uniformity of taxation (2023)
content:
All taxes shall be uniform, upon the same class of subjects, within the territorial
   limits of the authority levying the tax, and shall be levied and collected under general
   laws.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VII. Elections›PA CONST Art. VII, § 14. Absentee voting
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VII. Elections › PA CONST Art. VII, § 14. Absentee voting
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VII, § 14. Absentee voting (2023)
content:
(a) The Legislature shall, by general law, provide a manner in which, and the time
      and place at which, qualified electors who may, on the occurrence of any election,
      be absent from the municipality of their residence, because their duties, occupation
      or business require them to be elsewhere or who, on the occurrence of any election,
      are unable to attend at their proper polling places because of illness or physical
      disability or who will not attend a polling place because of the observance of a religious
      holiday or who cannot vote because of election day duties, in the case of a county
      employee, may vote, and for the return and canvass of their votes in the election
      district in which they respectively reside.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VIII. Taxation and Finance›PA CONST Art. VIII, § 7. Commonwealth indebtedness
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VIII. Taxation and Finance › PA CONST Art. VIII, § 7. Commonwealth indebtedness
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VIII, § 7. Commonwealth indebtedness (2023)
content:
(a) No debt shall be incurred by or on behalf of the Commonwealth except by law and
      in accordance with the provisions of this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VIII. Taxation and Finance›PA CONST Art. VIII, § 2. Exemptions and special provisions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VIII. Taxation and Finance › PA CONST Art. VIII, § 2. Exemptions and special provisions
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VIII, § 2. Exemptions and special provisions (2023)
content: (a) The General Assembly may by law exempt from taxation:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VIII. Taxation and Finance›PA CONST Art. VIII, § 5. Exemption from taxation restricted
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VIII. Taxation and Finance › PA CONST Art. VIII, § 5. Exemption from taxation restricted
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VIII, § 5. Exemption from taxation restricted (2023)
content:
All laws exempting property from taxation, other than the property above enumerated,
   shall be void.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VIII. Taxation and Finance›PA CONST Art. VIII, § 9. Municipal debt not to be assumed by Commonwealth
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VIII. Taxation and Finance › PA CONST Art. VIII, § 9. Municipal debt not to be assumed by Commonwealth
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VIII, § 9. Municipal debt not to be assumed by Commonwealth (2023)
content:
The Commonwealth shall not assume the debt, or any part thereof, of any county, city,
   borough, incorporated town, township or any similar general purpose unit of government
   unless such debt shall have been incurred to enable the Commonwealth to suppress insurrection
   or to assist the Commonwealth in the discharge of any portion of its present indebtedness.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VIII. Taxation and Finance›PA CONST Art. VIII, § 13. Appropriations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VIII. Taxation and Finance › PA CONST Art. VIII, § 13. Appropriations
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VIII, § 13. Appropriations (2023)
content:
(a) Operating budget appropriations made by the General Assembly shall not exceed
      the actual and estimated revenues and surplus available in the same fiscal year.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VIII. Taxation and Finance›PA CONST Art. VIII, § 10. Audit
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VIII. Taxation and Finance › PA CONST Art. VIII, § 10. Audit
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VIII, § 10. Audit (2023)
content:
The financial affairs of any entity funded or financially aided by the Commonwealth,
   and all departments, boards, commissions, agencies, instrumentalities, authorities
   and institutions of the Commonwealth, shall be subject to audits made in accordance
   with generally accepted auditing standards.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VIII. Taxation and Finance›PA CONST Art. VIII, § 11. Gasoline taxes and motor license fees restricted
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VIII. Taxation and Finance › PA CONST Art. VIII, § 11. Gasoline taxes and motor license fees restricted
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VIII, § 11. Gasoline taxes and motor license fees restricted (2023)
content:
(a) All proceeds from gasoline and other motor fuel excise taxes, motor vehicle registration
      fees and license taxes, operators' license fees and other excise taxes imposed on
      products used in motor transportation after providing therefrom for (a) cost of administration
      and collection, (b) payment of obligations incurred in the construction and reconstruction
      of public highways and bridges shall be appropriated by the General Assembly to agencies
      of the State or political subdivisions thereof;  and used solely for construction,
      reconstruction, maintenance and repair of and safety on public highways and bridges
      and costs and expenses incident thereto, and for the payment of obligations incurred
      for such purposes, and shall not be diverted by transfer or otherwise to any other
      purpose, except that loans may be made by the State from the proceeds of such taxes
      and fees for a single period not exceeding eight months, but no such loan shall be
      made within the period of one year from any preceding loan, and every loan made in
      any fiscal year shall be repayable within one month after the beginning of the next
      fiscal year.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VIII. Taxation and Finance›PA CONST Art. VIII, § 16. Land and Water Conservation and Reclamation Fund
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VIII. Taxation and Finance › PA CONST Art. VIII, § 16. Land and Water Conservation and Reclamation Fund
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VIII, § 16. Land and Water Conservation and Reclamation Fund (2023)
content:
In addition to the purposes stated in article eight, section seven of this Constitution,
   the Commonwealth may be authorized by law to create a debt and issue bonds in the
   amount of five hundred million dollars ($500,000,000) for a Land and Water Conservation
   and Reclamation Fund to be used for the conservation and reclamation of land and water
   resources of the Commonwealth, including the elimination of acid mine drainage, sewage,
   and other pollution from the streams of the Commonwealth, the provision of State financial
   assistance to political subdivisions and municipal authorities of the Commonwealth
   of Pennsylvania for the construction of sewage treatment plants, the restoration of
   abandoned strip-mined areas, the control and extinguishment of surface and underground
   mine fires, the alleviation and prevention of subsidence resulting from mining operations,
   and the acquisition of additional lands and the reclamation and development of park
   and recreational lands acquired pursuant to the authority of article nine, section
   twenty-four1of this Constitution, subject to such conditions and liabilities as the General Assembly
   may prescribe.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VIII. Taxation and Finance›PA CONST Art. VIII, § 8. Commonwealth credit not to be pledged
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VIII. Taxation and Finance › PA CONST Art. VIII, § 8. Commonwealth credit not to be pledged
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VIII, § 8. Commonwealth credit not to be pledged (2023)
content:
The credit of the Commonwealth shall not be pledged or loaned to any individual, company,
   corporation or association nor shall the Commonwealth become a joint owner or stockholder
   in any company, corporation or association.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VIII. Taxation and Finance›PA CONST Art. VIII, § 6. Taxation of corporations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VIII. Taxation and Finance › PA CONST Art. VIII, § 6. Taxation of corporations
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VIII, § 6. Taxation of corporations (2023)
content:
The power to tax corporations and corporate property shall not be surrendered or suspended
   by any contract or grant to which the Commonwealth shall be a party.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IX. Local Government›PA CONST Art. IX, § 1. Local government
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IX. Local Government › PA CONST Art. IX, § 1. Local government
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IX, § 1. Local government (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall provide by general law for local government within the
   Commonwealth.  Such general law shall be uniform as to all classes of local government regarding
   procedural matters.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VIII. Taxation and Finance›PA CONST Art. VIII, § 17. Special emergency legislation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VIII. Taxation and Finance › PA CONST Art. VIII, § 17. Special emergency legislation
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VIII, § 17. Special emergency legislation (2023)
content:
(a) Notwithstanding any provisions of this Constitution to the contrary, the General
      Assembly shall have the authority to enact laws providing for tax rebates, credits,
      exemptions, grants-in-aid, State supplementations, or otherwise provide special provisions
      for individuals, corporations, associations or nonprofit institutions, including nonpublic
      schools (whether sectarian or nonsectarian) in order to alleviate the danger, damage,
      suffering or hardship faced by such individuals, corporations, associations, institutions
      or nonpublic schools as a result of Great Storms or Floods of September 1971, of June
      1972, or of 1974, or of 1975 or of 1976.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VIII. Taxation and Finance›PA CONST Art. VIII, § 12. Governor's budgets and financial plan
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VIII. Taxation and Finance › PA CONST Art. VIII, § 12. Governor's budgets and financial plan
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VIII, § 12. Governor's budgets and financial plan (2023)
content: Annually, at the times set by law, the Governor shall submit to the General Assembly:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IX. Local Government›PA CONST Art. IX, § 2. Home rule
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IX. Local Government › PA CONST Art. IX, § 2. Home rule
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IX, § 2. Home rule (2023)
content:
Municipalities shall have the right and power to frame and adopt home rule charters.  Adoption, amendment or repeal of a home rule charter shall be by referendum.  The General Assembly shall provide the procedure by which a home rule charter may
   be framed and its adoption, amendment or repeal presented to the electors.  If the General Assembly does not so provide, a home rule charter or a procedure
   for framing and presenting a home rule charter may be presented to the electors by
   initiative or by the governing body of the municipality.  A municipality which has a home rule charter may exercise any power or perform any
   function not denied by this Constitution, by its home rule charter or by the General
   Assembly at any time.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VIII. Taxation and Finance›PA CONST Art. VIII, § 15. Project “70”
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VIII. Taxation and Finance › PA CONST Art. VIII, § 15. Project “70”
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VIII, § 15. Project “70” (2023)
content:
In addition to the purposes stated in article eight, section seven of this Constitution,
   the Commonwealth may be authorized by law to create debt and to issue bonds to the
   amount of seventy million dollars ($70,000,000) for the acquisition of land for State
   parks, reservoirs and other conservation and recreation and historical preservation
   purposes and for participation by the Commonwealth with political subdivisions in
   the acquisition of land for parks, reservoirs and other conservation and recreation
   and historical preservation purposes, subject to such conditions and limitations as
   the General Assembly may prescribe.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article VIII. Taxation and Finance›PA CONST Art. VIII, § 14. Surplus
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article VIII. Taxation and Finance › PA CONST Art. VIII, § 14. Surplus
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. VIII, § 14. Surplus (2023)
content:
All surplus of operating funds at the end of the fiscal year shall be appropriated
   during the ensuing fiscal year by the General Assembly.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IX. Local Government›PA CONST Art. IX, § 5. Intergovernmental cooperation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IX. Local Government › PA CONST Art. IX, § 5. Intergovernmental cooperation
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IX, § 5. Intergovernmental cooperation (2023)
content:
A municipality by act of its governing body may, or upon being required by initiative
   and referendum in the area affected shall, cooperate or agree in the exercise of any
   function, power or responsibility with, or delegate or transfer any function, power
   or responsibility to, one or more other governmental units including other municipalities
   or districts, the Federal government, any other state or its governmental units, or
   any newly created governmental unit.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IX. Local Government›PA CONST Art. IX, § 8. Consolidation, merger or boundary change
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IX. Local Government › PA CONST Art. IX, § 8. Consolidation, merger or boundary change
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IX, § 8. Consolidation, merger or boundary change (2023)
content:
Uniform Legislation.--The General Assembly shall, within two years following the adoption of this article,
   enact uniform legislation establishing the procedure for consolidation, merger or
   change of the boundaries of municipalities.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IX. Local Government›PA CONST Art. IX, § 3. Optional plans
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IX. Local Government › PA CONST Art. IX, § 3. Optional plans
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IX, § 3. Optional plans (2023)
content:
Municipalities shall have the right and power to adopt optional forms of government
   as provided by law.  The General Assembly shall provide optional forms of government for all municipalities.  An optional form of government shall be presented to the electors by initiative,
   by the governing body of the municipality, or by the General Assembly.  Adoption or repeal of an optional form of government shall be by referendum.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IX. Local Government›PA CONST Art. IX, § 6. Area government
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IX. Local Government › PA CONST Art. IX, § 6. Area government
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IX, § 6. Area government (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall provide for the establishment and dissolution of government
   of areas involving two or more municipalities or parts thereof.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IX. Local Government›PA CONST Art. IX, § 4. County government
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IX. Local Government › PA CONST Art. IX, § 4. County government
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IX, § 4. County government (2023)
content:
County officers shall consist of commissioners, controllers or auditors, district
   attorneys, public defenders, treasurers, sheriffs, registers of wills, recorders of
   deeds, prothonotaries, clerks of the courts, and such others as may from time to time
   be provided by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IX. Local Government›PA CONST Art. IX, § 10. Local government debt
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IX. Local Government › PA CONST Art. IX, § 10. Local government debt
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IX, § 10. Local government debt (2023)
content:
Subject only to the restrictions imposed by this section, the General Assembly shall
   prescribe the debt limits of all units of local government including municipalities
   and school districts.  For such purposes, the debt limit base shall be a percentage of the total revenue,
   as defined by the General Assembly, of the unit of local government computed over
   a specific period immediately preceding the year of borrowing.  The debt limit to be prescribed in every such case shall exclude all indebtedness
   (1) for any project to the extent that it is self-liquidating or self-supporting or
   which has heretofore been defined as self-liquidating or self-supporting, or (2) which
   has been approved by referendum held in such manner as shall be provided by law.  The provisions of this paragraph shall not apply to the City or County of Philadelphia.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IX. Local Government›PA CONST Art. IX, § 7. Area-wide powers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IX. Local Government › PA CONST Art. IX, § 7. Area-wide powers
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IX, § 7. Area-wide powers (2023)
content:
The General Assembly may grant powers to area governments or to municipalities within
   a given geographical area in which there exists intergovernmental cooperation or area
   government and designate the classes of municipalities subject to such legislation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IX. Local Government›PA CONST Art. IX, § 9. Appropriation for public purposes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IX. Local Government › PA CONST Art. IX, § 9. Appropriation for public purposes
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IX, § 9. Appropriation for public purposes (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall not authorize any municipality or incorporated district
   to become a stockholder in any company, association or corporation, or to obtain or
   appropriate money for, or to loan its credit to, any corporation, association, institution
   or individual.  The General Assembly may provide standards by which municipalities or school districts
   may give financial assistance or lease property to public service, industrial or commercial
   enterprises if it shall find that such assistance or leasing is necessary to the health,
   safety or welfare of the Commonwealth or any municipality or school district.  Existing authority of any municipality or incorporated district to obtain or appropriate
   money for, or to loan its credit to, any corporation, association, institution or
   individual, is preserved.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IX. Local Government›PA CONST Art. IX, § 12. Philadelphia debt
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IX. Local Government › PA CONST Art. IX, § 12. Philadelphia debt
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IX, § 12. Philadelphia debt (2023)
content:
The debt of the City of Philadelphia may be increased in such amount that the total
   debt of said city shall not exceed thirteen and one-half percent of the average of
   the annual assessed valuations of the taxable realty therein, during the ten years
   immediately preceding the year in which such increase is made, but said city shall
   not increase its indebtedness to an amount exceeding three percent upon such average
   assessed valuation of realty, without the consent of the electors thereof at a public
   election held in such manner as shall be provided by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IX. Local Government›PA CONST Art. IX, § 11. Local reapportionment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IX. Local Government › PA CONST Art. IX, § 11. Local reapportionment
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IX, § 11. Local reapportionment (2023)
content:
Within the year following that in which the Federal decennial census is officially
   reported as required by Federal law, and at such other times as the governing body
   of any municipality shall deem necessary, each municipality having a governing body
   not entirely elected at large shall be reapportioned, by its governing body or as
   shall otherwise be provided by uniform law, into districts which shall be composed
   of compact and contiguous territory as nearly equal in population as practicable,
   for the purpose of describing the districts for those not elected at large.

content: As used in this article, the following words shall have the following meanings:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article X. Private Corporations›PA CONST Art. X, § 2. Certain charters to be subject to the Constitution
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article X. Private Corporations › PA CONST Art. X, § 2. Certain charters to be subject to the Constitution
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. X, § 2. Certain charters to be subject to the Constitution (2023)
content:
Private corporations which have accepted or accept the Constitution of this Commonwealth
   or the benefits of any law passed by the General Assembly after 1873 governing the
   affairs of corporations shall hold their charters subject to the provisions of the
   Constitution of this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article IX. Local Government›PA CONST Art. IX, § 13. Abolition of county offices in Philadelphia
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article IX. Local Government › PA CONST Art. IX, § 13. Abolition of county offices in Philadelphia
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. IX, § 13. Abolition of county offices in Philadelphia (2023)
content:
(a) In Philadelphia all county offices are hereby abolished, and the city shall henceforth
      perform all functions of county government within its area through officers selected
      in such manner as may be provided by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article X. Private Corporations›PA CONST Art. X, § 3. Revocation, amendment and repeal of charters and corporation laws
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article X. Private Corporations › PA CONST Art. X, § 3. Revocation, amendment and repeal of charters and corporation laws
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. X, § 3. Revocation, amendment and repeal of charters and corporation laws (2023)
content:
All charters of private corporations and all present and future common or statutory
   law with respect to the formation or regulation of private corporations or prescribing
   powers, rights, duties or liabilities of private corporations or their officers, directors
   or shareholders may be revoked, amended or repealed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article X. Private Corporations›PA CONST Art. X, § 4. Compensation for property taken by corporations under right of eminent domain
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article X. Private Corporations › PA CONST Art. X, § 4. Compensation for property taken by corporations under right of eminent domain
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. X, § 4. Compensation for property taken by corporations under right of eminent domain (2023)
content:
Municipal and other corporations invested with the privilege of taking private property
   for public use shall make just compensation for property taken, injured or destroyed
   by the construction or enlargement of their works, highways or improvements and compensation
   shall be paid or secured before the taking, injury or destruction.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Article XI. Amendments›PA CONST Art. XI, § 1. Proposal of amendments by the General Assembly and their adoption
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article XI. Amendments › PA CONST Art. XI, § 1. Proposal of amendments by the General Assembly and their adoption
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. XI, § 1. Proposal of amendments by the General Assembly and their adoption (2023)
content:
Amendments to this Constitution may be proposed in the Senate or House of Representatives;
   and if the same shall be agreed to by a majority of the members elected to each House,
   such proposed amendment or amendments shall be entered on their journals with the
   yeas and nays taken thereon, and the Secretary of the Commonwealth shall cause the
   same to be published three months before the next general election, in at least two
   newspapers in every county in which such newspapers shall be published;  and if, in
   the General Assembly next afterwards chosen, such proposed amendment or amendments
   shall be agreed to by a majority of the members elected to each House, the Secretary
   of the Commonwealth shall cause the same again to be published in the manner aforesaid;
   and such proposed amendment or amendments shall be submitted to the qualified electors
   of the State in such manner, and at such time at least three months after being so
   agreed to by the two Houses, as the General Assembly shall prescribe;  and, if such
   amendment or amendments shall be approved by a majority of those voting thereon, such
   amendment or amendments shall become a part of the Constitution;  but no amendment
   or amendments shall be submitted oftener than once in five years.  When two or more amendments shall be submitted they shall be voted upon separately.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Article X. Private Corporations › PA CONST Art. X, § 1. Certain unused charters void
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Art. X, § 1. Certain unused charters void (2023)
content:
The charters and privileges granted prior to 1874 to private corporations which had
   not been organized in good faith and commenced business prior to 1874 shall be void.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 3. Election of Senators
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 3. Election of Senators
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 3. Election of Senators (2023)
content:
At the general election in the years one thousand eight hundred and seventy-four and
   one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five, Senators shall be elected in all districts
   where there shall be vacancies.  Those elected in the year one thousand eight hundred and seventy-four shall serve
   for two years, and those elected in the year one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five
   shall serve for one year.  Senators now elected and those whose terms are unexpired shall represent the districts
   in which they reside until the end of the terms for which they were elected.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 1. When to take effect
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 1. When to take effect (2023)
content:
This Constitution shall take effect on the first day of January, in the year one thousand
   eight hundred and seventy-four, for all purposes not otherwise provided for therein.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 6. Election of Lieutenant Governor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 6. Election of Lieutenant Governor
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 6. Election of Lieutenant Governor (2023)
content:
At the general election in the year one thousand eight hundred and seventy-four, a
   Lieutenant Governor shall be elected according to the provisions of this Constitution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 4. Election of Senators (continued)
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 4. Election of Senators (continued)
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 4. Election of Senators (continued) (2023)
content:
At the general election in the year one thousand eight hundred and seventy-six, Senators
   shall be elected from even numbered districts to serve for two years, and from odd
   numbered districts to serve for four years.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 7. Secretary of Internal Affairs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 7. Secretary of Internal Affairs
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 7. Secretary of Internal Affairs (2023)
content:
The Secretary of Internal Affairs shall be elected at the first general election after
   the adoption of this Constitution;  and when the said officer shall be duly elected
   and qualified, the office of Surveyor General shall be abolished.  The Surveyor General in office at the time of the adoption of this Constitution
   shall continue in office until the expiration of the term for which he was elected.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 5. Election of Governor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 5. Election of Governor
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 5. Election of Governor (2023)
content:
The first election of Governor under this Constitution shall be at the general election
   in the year one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five, when a Governor shall be
   elected for three years;  and the term of the Governor elected in the year one thousand
   eight hundred and seventy-eight and of those thereafter elected shall be for four
   years, according to the provisions of this Constitution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 9. Eligibility of present officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 9. Eligibility of present officers
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 9. Eligibility of present officers (2023)
content:
Nothing contained in this Constitution shall be construed to render any person now
   holding any State office for a first official term ineligible for re-election at the
   end of such term.
