path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 8. Superintendent of Public Instruction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 8. Superintendent of Public Instruction
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 8. Superintendent of Public Instruction (2023)
content:
When the Superintendent of Public Instruction shall be duly qualified the office of
   Superintendent of Common Schools shall cease.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 11. Courts of record
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 11. Courts of record
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 11. Courts of record (2023)
content:
All courts of record and all existing courts which are not specified in this Constitution
   shall continue in existence until the first day of December, in the year one thousand
   eight hundred and seventy-five, without abridgment of their present jurisdiction,
   but no longer.  The court of first criminal jurisdiction for the counties of Schuylkill, Lebanon
   and Dauphin is hereby abolished, and all causes and proceedings pending therein in
   the county of Schuylkill shall be tried and disposed of in the courts of oyer and
   terminer and quarter sessions of the peace of said county.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, Preamble
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, Preamble
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, Preamble (2023)
content:
That no inconvenience may arise from the changes in the Constitution of the Commonwealth,
   and in order to carry the same into complete operation, it is hereby declared, that:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 17. Compensation of judges
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 17. Compensation of judges
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 17. Compensation of judges (2023)
content:
The General Assembly, at the first session after the adoption of this Constitution,
   shall fix and determine the compensation of the judges of the Supreme Court and of
   the judges of the several judicial districts of the Commonwealth;  and the provisions
   of the fifteenth section of the article on Legislation shall not be deemed inconsistent
   herewith.  Nothing contained in this Constitution shall be held to reduce the compensation
   now paid to any law judge of this Commonwealth now in commission.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 2. Former laws remain in force
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 2. Former laws remain in force
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 2. Former laws remain in force (2023)
content:
All laws in force in this Commonwealth at the time of the adoption of this Constitution
   not inconsistent therewith, and all rights, actions, prosecutions and contracts shall
   continue as if this Constitution had not been adopted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 15. Judges in commission
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 15. Judges in commission
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 15. Judges in commission (2023)
content:
Judges learned in the law of any court of record holding commissions in force at the
   adoption of this Constitution shall hold their respective offices until the expiration
   of the terms for which they were commissioned, and until their successors shall be
   duly qualified.  The Governor shall commission the president judge of the court of first criminal
   jurisdiction for the counties of Schuylkill, Lebanon and Dauphin as a judge of the
   court of common pleas of Schuylkill county, for the unexpired term of his office.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 10. Judges of Supreme Court
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 10. Judges of Supreme Court
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 10. Judges of Supreme Court (2023)
content:
The judges of the Supreme Court in office when this Constitution shall take effect
   shall continue until their commissions severally expire.  Two judges in addition to the number now composing the said court shall be elected
   at the first general election after the adoption of this Constitution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 12. Register's courts abolished
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 12. Register's courts abolished
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 12. Register's courts abolished (2023)
content:
The register's courts now in existence shall be abolished on the first day of January
   next succeeding the adoption of this Constitution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 16. President judges; casting lots; associate judges
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 16. President judges; casting lots; associate judges
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 16. President judges; casting lots; associate judges (2023)
content:
After the expiration of the term of any president judge of any court of common pleas,
   in commission at the adoption of this Constitution, the judge of such court learned
   in the law and oldest in commission shall be the president judge thereof;  and when
   two or more judges are elected at the same time in any judicial district they shall
   decide by lot which shall be president judge;  but when the president judge of a court
   shall be re-elected he shall continue to be president judge of that court.  Associate judges not learned in the law, elected after the adoption of this Constitution,
   shall be commissioned to hold their offices for the term of five years from the first
   day of January next after their election.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 13. Judicial districts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 13. Judicial districts
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 13. Judicial districts (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall, at the next session after the adoption of this Constitution,
   designate the several judicial districts as required by this Constitution.  The judges in commission when such designation shall be made shall continue during
   their unexpired terms judges of the new districts in which they reside;  but, when
   there shall be two judges residing in the same district, the president judge shall
   elect to which district he shall be assigned, and the additional law judge shall be
   assigned to the other district.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 21. Causes pending in Philadelphia; transfer of records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 21. Causes pending in Philadelphia; transfer of records
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 21. Causes pending in Philadelphia; transfer of records (2023)
content:
The causes and proceedings pending in the court ofnisi prius,court of common pleas, and district court in Philadelphia shall be tried and disposed
   of in the court of common pleas.  The records and dockets of said courts shall be transferred to the prothonotary's
   office of said county.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 20. When re-organization of courts to take effect
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 20. When re-organization of courts to take effect
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 20. When re-organization of courts to take effect (2023)
content:
The organization of the courts of common pleas under this Constitution for the counties
   of Philadelphia and Allegheny shall take effect on the first Monday of January, one
   thousand eight hundred and seventy-five, and existing courts in said counties shall
   continue with their present powers and jurisdiction until that date, but no new suits
   shall be instituted in the courts ofnisi priusafter the adoption of this Constitution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 22. Causes pending in Allegheny county
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 22. Causes pending in Allegheny county
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 22. Causes pending in Allegheny county (2023)
content:
The causes and proceedings pending in the court of common pleas in the county of Allegheny
   shall be tried and disposed of in the court number one;  and the causes and proceedings
   pending in the district court shall be tried and disposed of in the court number two.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 18. Courts of Philadelphia and Allegheny counties; organization in Philadelphia
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 18. Courts of Philadelphia and Allegheny counties; organization in Philadelphia
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 18. Courts of Philadelphia and Allegheny counties; organization in Philadelphia (2023)
content:
The courts of common pleas in the counties of Philadelphia and Allegheny shall be
   composed of the present judges of the district court and court of common pleas of
   said counties until their offices shall severally end, and of such other judges as
   may from time to time be selected.  For the purpose of first organization in Philadelphia the judges of the court number
   one shall be Judges Allison, Pierce and Paxson;  of the court number two, Judges Hare,
   Mitchell and one other judge to be elected;  of the court number three, Judges Ludlow,
   Finletter and Lynd;  and of the court number four, Judges Thayer, Briggs and one other
   judge to be elected.  The judge first named shall be the president judge of said courts respectively,
   and thereafter the president judge shall be the judge oldest in commission;  but any
   president judge, re-elected in the same court or district, shall continue to be president
   judge thereof.  The additional judges for courts numbers two and four shall be voted for and elected
   at the first general election after the adoption of this Constitution, in the same
   manner as the two additional judges of the Supreme Court, and they shall decide by
   lot to which court they shall belong.  Their term of office shall commence on the first Monday of January, in the year
   one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 14. Decennial adjustment of judicial districts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 14. Decennial adjustment of judicial districts
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 14. Decennial adjustment of judicial districts (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall, at the next succeeding session after each decennial census
   and not oftener, designate the several judicial districts as required by this Constitution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 24. Aldermen
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 24. Aldermen
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 24. Aldermen (2023)
content:
In cities containing over fifty thousand inhabitants, except Philadelphia, all aldermen
   in office at the time of the adoption of this Constitution shall continue in office
   until the expiration of their commissions, and at the election for city and ward officers
   in the year one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five one alderman shall be elected
   in each ward as provided in this Constitution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 25. Magistrates in Philadelphia
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 25. Magistrates in Philadelphia
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 25. Magistrates in Philadelphia (2023)
content:
In Philadelphia magistrates in lieu of aldermen shall be chosen, as required in this
   Constitution, at the election in said city for city and ward officers in the year
   one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five;  their term of office shall commence
   on the first Monday of April succeeding their election.  The terms of office of aldermen in said city holding or entitled to commissions
   at the time of the adoption of this Constitution shall not be affected thereby.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 28. County commissioners and auditors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 28. County commissioners and auditors
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 28. County commissioners and auditors (2023)
content:
The terms of office of county commissioners and county auditors, chosen prior to the
   year one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five, which shall not have expired before
   the first Monday of January in the year one thousand eight hundred and seventy-six,
   shall expire on that day.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 26. Term of present officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 26. Term of present officers
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 26. Term of present officers (2023)
content:
All persons in office in this Commonwealth at the time of the adoption of this Constitution,
   and at the first election under it, shall hold their respective offices until the
   term for which they have been elected or appointed shall expire, and until their successors
   shall be duly qualified, unless otherwise provided in this Constitution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 23. Prothonotary of Philadelphia county
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 23. Prothonotary of Philadelphia county
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 23. Prothonotary of Philadelphia county (2023)
content:
The prothonotary of the court of common pleas of Philadelphia shall be first appointed
   by the judges of said court on the first Monday of December, in the year one thousand
   eight hundred and seventy-five, and the present prothonotary of the district court
   in said county shall be the prothonotary of the said court of common pleas until said
   date when his commission shall expire, and the present clerk of the court of oyer
   and terminer and quarter sessions of the peace in Philadelphia shall be the clerk
   of such court until the expiration of his present commission on the first Monday of
   December, in the year one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 31. Enforcing legislation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 31. Enforcing legislation
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 31. Enforcing legislation (2023)
content:
The General Assembly at its first session, or as soon as may be after the adoption
   of this Constitution, shall pass such laws as may be necessary to carry the same into
   full force and effect.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 27. Oath of office
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 27. Oath of office
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 27. Oath of office (2023)
content:
The seventh article of this Constitution prescribing an oath of office shall take
   effect on and after the first day of January, one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 30. Renewal of oath of office
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 30. Renewal of oath of office
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 30. Renewal of oath of office (2023)
content:
All State and judicial officers heretofore elected, sworn, affirmed, or in office
   when this Constitution shall take effect, shall severally, within one month after
   such adoption, take and subscribe an oath, or affirmation, to support this Constitution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 19. Organization of courts in Allegheny county
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 19. Organization of courts in Allegheny county
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 19. Organization of courts in Allegheny county (2023)
content:
In the county of Allegheny, for the purpose of first organization under this Constitution,
   the judges of the court of common pleas, at the time of the adoption of this Constitution,
   shall be the judges of the court number one, and the judges of the district court,
   at the same date, shall be the judges of the common pleas number two.  The president judges of the common pleas and district court shall be president judge
   of said courts number one and two, respectively, until their offices shall end;  and
   thereafter the judge oldest in commission shall be president judge;  but any president
   judge re-elected in the same court, or district, shall continue to be president judge
   thereof.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 33. City commissioners of Philadelphia
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 33. City commissioners of Philadelphia
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 33. City commissioners of Philadelphia (2023)
content:
The words “county commissioners,” wherever used in this Constitution and in any ordinance accompanying the same, shall
   be held to include the commissioners for the city of Philadelphia.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 29. Compensation of present officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 29. Compensation of present officers
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 29. Compensation of present officers (2023)
content:
All State, county, city, ward, borough and township officers in office at the time
   of the adoption of this Constitution, whose compensation is not provided for by salaries
   alone, shall continue to receive the compensation allowed them by law until the expiration
   of their respective terms of office.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 2 (Amendments of November 2, 1909)›PA CONST Schedule 2, § 1. Adjustments of terms of public officers to amendments of 1909
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 2 (Amendments of November 2, 1909) › PA CONST Schedule 2, § 1. Adjustments of terms of public officers to amendments of 1909
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 2, § 1. Adjustments of terms of public officers to amendments of 1909 (2023)
content:
That no inconvenience may arise from the change in the Constitution of the Commonwealth,
   and in order to carry the same into complete operation, it is hereby declared that--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania›Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874)›PA CONST Schedule 1, § 32. An ordinance declared valid
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Constitution of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania › Schedule No. 1 (Adopted with the Constitution of 1874) › PA CONST Schedule 1, § 32. An ordinance declared valid
citation: PA Stat § PA CONST Schedule 1, § 32. An ordinance declared valid (2023)
content:
The ordinance passed by this Convention, entitled “An ordinance for submitting the
   amended Constitution of Pennsylvania to a vote of the electors thereof,” shall be
   held to be valid for all the purposes thereof.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes›Chapter 3. Format of the Consolidated Statutes›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 303. Cross references between provisions of the Consolidated Statutes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes › Chapter 3. Format of the Consolidated Statutes › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 303. Cross references between provisions of the Consolidated Statutes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 303. Cross references between provisions of the Consolidated Statutes (2023)
content:
When reference is made in this act to a provision contained in any other section or
   sections of the same title such provision shall be identified without specifying the
   number of the title in which it appears.  When reference is made in this act to a provision contained in any section or sections
   of this act appearing in a different title the short form of citation specified in
   section 102 of this title (relating to citation of Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes)
   shall be used.  A cross reference description based on the section heading or headings of the provisions
   cited shall be inserted immediately following the first occurrence of the citation
   in the section and following any reoccurrence of the citation which is preceded in
   the same section or relevant part thereof by a citation to a different section of
   this act.  Where required for clarity in the case of cross references to subsections or other
   parts of a section, the cross reference description shall be based on the subject
   matter of the subsection or other part thereof referred to.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes›Chapter 3. Format of the Consolidated Statutes›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 304. References to other statutes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes › Chapter 3. Format of the Consolidated Statutes › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 304. References to other statutes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 304. References to other statutes (2023)
content:
(a) Acts of the General Assembly shall be referred to generically in this act as statutes
      and, unless the context clearly indicates otherwise, such term when used in this act
      shall be deemed to be also a general reference to the provisions of this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes›Chapter 1. Short Title, Form of Citation and Effective Date›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 101. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes › Chapter 1. Short Title, Form of Citation and Effective Date › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 101. Short title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 101. Short title (2023)
content: This act shall be known and may be cited as the “Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes›Chapter 3. Format of the Consolidated Statutes›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 305. Re-use of section numbers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes › Chapter 3. Format of the Consolidated Statutes › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 305. Re-use of section numbers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 305. Re-use of section numbers (2023)
content:
A section number shall not be re-used for a different subject, except in a bill to
   revise a part, article, chapter or other major subdivision of this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes›Chapter 1. Short Title, Form of Citation and Effective Date›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 102. Citation of Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes › Chapter 1. Short Title, Form of Citation and Effective Date › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 102. Citation of Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 102. Citation of Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes (2023)
content:
The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes may be cited by title and section number.  Without prejudice to any other form of citation, a citation to any section of this
   act in the following form shall, except as provided in section 303 of this title (relating
   to cross references between provisions of the Consolidated Statutes), be adequate
   for all purposes:  “1 Pa.C.S. § 102.”

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes › Chapter 5. Official Publication of the Consolidated Statutes › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 502. Preparation and contents
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 502. Preparation and contents (2023)
content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes›Chapter 3. Format of the Consolidated Statutes›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 301. Arrangement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes › Chapter 3. Format of the Consolidated Statutes › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 301. Arrangement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 301. Arrangement (2023)
content:
(a) This act consists of titles subdivided into parts, articles, chapters and such
      other major subdivisions as may be required for clarity of expression and uniformity
      of style.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes›Chapter 3. Format of the Consolidated Statutes›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 306. Bills to amend the Consolidated Statutes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes › Chapter 3. Format of the Consolidated Statutes › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 306. Bills to amend the Consolidated Statutes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 306. Bills to amend the Consolidated Statutes (2023)
content:
(a) Bills to amend this act shall be drafted to conform with the structure of the
      Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, as provided in this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes›Chapter 5. Official Publication of the Consolidated Statutes›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 503. Official status of publication
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes › Chapter 5. Official Publication of the Consolidated Statutes › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 503. Official status of publication
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 503. Official status of publication (2023)
content:
The publication prepared by the bureau pursuant to this chapter shall constitute an
   official publication of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes and shall be legal
   evidence of the laws contained therein including the Constitution and laws incorporated
   therein pursuant to section 502(a)(4) of this title (relating to preparation and contents).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes›Chapter 3. Format of the Consolidated Statutes›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 302. Section headings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes › Chapter 3. Format of the Consolidated Statutes › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 302. Section headings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 302. Section headings (2023)
content:
Each section of this act shall be given a brief descriptive heading immediately preceding
   the body of the section.  The headings of sections may be referred to as catchlines.  In printing this act and its amendments the Director of the Legislative Reference
   Bureau shall substitute a symbol for the word “Section” preceding  the digits of a
   section number in each catchline.  Subsections may also have headings for convenience.  Subsection headings shall not be set out on separate lines.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes›Chapter 5. Official Publication of the Consolidated Statutes›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 501. Publication and distribution
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes › Chapter 5. Official Publication of the Consolidated Statutes › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 501. Publication and distribution
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 501. Publication and distribution (2023)
content:
(a) The Legislative Reference Bureau may compile, edit, publish, print, supplement
      and revise or contract directly or through the Legislative Printing Clerk for the
      compilation, editing, publishing, printing, supplementation or revision of an official
      publication of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes and amendments thereto.  It shall be the duty of the Department of Property and Supplies,1upon request of the bureau, to arrange for the prompt distribution of the official
      publication and the supplements thereto and revisions thereof in accordance with the
      provisions of this chapter.  This publication shall be in addition to the publication of advance copies of statutes
      and the Laws of Pennsylvania except that the bureau, when authorized by concurrent
      resolution of the General Assembly, may reduce the number of such statutes and laws
      published and printed and provide for the manner of their distribution and a fee to
      be charged for certain distributions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes›Chapter 1. Short Title, Form of Citation and Effective Date›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 103. Effective date
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part I. The Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes › Chapter 1. Short Title, Form of Citation and Effective Date › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 103. Effective date
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 103. Effective date (2023)
content: This act shall take effect immediately.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions›Chapter 9. Constitutional Provisions›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 902. Conduct of election
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions › Chapter 9. Constitutional Provisions › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 902. Conduct of election
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 902. Conduct of election (2023)
content:
The manner in which proposed amendments to the Constitution of Pennsylvania shall
   be submitted to the qualified electors of the Commonwealth and the manner and effect
   of the certification of the returns of the election thereon shall, unless the General
   Assembly shall prescribe otherwise with respect to any particular proposed amendment,
   be as provided in the Pennsylvania Election Code.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions›Chapter 9. Constitutional Provisions›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 901. Legislation to show changes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions › Chapter 9. Constitutional Provisions › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 901. Legislation to show changes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 901. Legislation to show changes (2023)
content:
Bills or joint resolutions introduced in the General Assembly proposing amendments
   to the Constitution of Pennsylvania shall be printed in such a manner as to indicate
   the words to be added to or deleted from the Constitution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions›Chapter 9. Constitutional Provisions›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 906. Short titles of Constitutions of 1874 and 1968
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions › Chapter 9. Constitutional Provisions › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 906. Short titles of Constitutions of 1874 and 1968
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 906. Short titles of Constitutions of 1874 and 1968 (2023)
content:
(a) Constitution of 1874.--The Constitution of Pennsylvania, as adopted by referendum of December 16, 1873,
      shall be known and may be cited as the “Constitution of 1874.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions›Chapter 9. Constitutional Provisions›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 905. Section headings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions › Chapter 9. Constitutional Provisions › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 905. Section headings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 905. Section headings (2023)
content:
The Director of the Legislative Reference Bureau, with the approval of the Department
   of Justice, shall prepare and promulgate an appropriate heading for any section of
   the Constitution of Pennsylvania which was heretofore or may hereafter be adopted
   without a section heading.  Any section heading promulgated pursuant to this section shall be published in the
   next available volume of the Laws of Pennsylvania.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions›Chapter 9. Constitutional Provisions›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 903. Governor to proclaim result of election
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions › Chapter 9. Constitutional Provisions › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 903. Governor to proclaim result of election
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 903. Governor to proclaim result of election (2023)
content:
The officer of this Commonwealth to whom election returns are required by law to be
   certified shall, whenever a proposed amendment to the Constitution of Pennsylvania
   has been on the ballot at any election, certify the result of the election thereon
   to the Governor immediately upon receiving the official returns from all counties
   of the Commonwealth, and the Governor shall thereupon issue his proclamation indicating
   whether or not the proposed amendment has been adopted by a majority of the electors
   voting thereon.  The proclamation shall be published in the next available volume of the Laws of
   Pennsylvania.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions›Chapter 9. Constitutional Provisions›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 904. Governor to proclaim corrected numbering
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions › Chapter 9. Constitutional Provisions › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 904. Governor to proclaim corrected numbering
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 904. Governor to proclaim corrected numbering (2023)
content:
Whenever an amendment of an article or of a section of the Constitution of Pennsylvania
   is adopted without specifying an article or section number, or whenever any amendment
   is adopted bearing a number which conflicts with the number of another article or
   section of the Constitution, the Governor may by proclamation specify a number for
   the article or section having no number, or change the number of any article or section
   which bears a number which conflicts with the number of another article or section
   of the Constitution, or renumber the articles of the Constitution or the sections
   of an article.  The proclamation shall be published in the next available volume of the Laws of
   Pennsylvania.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions›Chapter 11. Statutory Provisions›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1105. Editing statutes for printing
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions › Chapter 11. Statutory Provisions › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1105. Editing statutes for printing
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1105. Editing statutes for printing (2023)
content:
(a) Correction of errors.--Where any statute shall have been finally enacted and it shall be ascertained that
      such statute is technically defective in form, or contains misspelled words or typographical
      errors, or the plural or singular number, or the past, present or future tense appears
      where another should be used, or where a word clearly intended to be inserted has
      been omitted, or where a word clearly should have been omitted, or where a word is
      correctly spelled but it clearly appears that another word was intended, the Director
      of the Legislative Reference Bureau, in editing such statute, shall have authority,
      with the approval of the President Pro Tempore of the Senate, the Speaker of the House
      of Representatives, and the Department of Justice, to correct the original copy of
      such statute, as filed in the Department of State, if such correction will not in
      any manner affect or change the meaning, intent or substance of such statute.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part V. Statutory Construction›Chapter 15. General Provisions›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1501. Short title of part
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part V. Statutory Construction › Chapter 15. General Provisions › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1501. Short title of part
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1501. Short title of part (2023)
content:
This part shall be known, and may be cited as, the “Statutory Construction Act of
   1972.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions›Chapter 11. Statutory Provisions›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1101. Enacting clause and unofficial provisions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions › Chapter 11. Statutory Provisions › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1101. Enacting clause and unofficial provisions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1101. Enacting clause and unofficial provisions (2023)
content:
(a) All statutes shall begin in the following style:  “The General Assembly of the
      Commonwealth of Pennsylvania hereby enacts as follows:”.  Such enacting clause shall be placed immediately after the preamble or the table
      of contents of the statute, or if there be neither preamble nor table of contents,
      then immediately after the title.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions›Chapter 11. Statutory Provisions›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1103. Preparation of statutes for printing
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions › Chapter 11. Statutory Provisions › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1103. Preparation of statutes for printing
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1103. Preparation of statutes for printing (2023)
content:
The Director of the Legislative Reference Bureau shall, as soon as any bill becomes
   a law, prepare the same for printing, cause the same to be printed immediately, and
   collate with and correct the proof sheets by the original rolls.  He shall also have the statutes printed and indexed in book form as the Laws of
   Pennsylvania as early as possible succeeding each regular session of the General Assembly,
   for distribution in accordance with law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions›Chapter 11. Statutory Provisions›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1102. Publication of notice of application for local or special legislation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions › Chapter 11. Statutory Provisions › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1102. Publication of notice of application for local or special legislation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1102. Publication of notice of application for local or special legislation (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--No local or special bill to enact a local or special statute shall be passed by the
      General Assembly, unless notice of the intention to apply therefor shall be published,
      once a week for four successive weeks, in not less than two newspapers of general
      circulation, and also in the legal journal, if any, published in the county or in
      each of the several counties where the matter or thing affected may be.  Where the matter or thing affected is in a municipality, publication shall be made
      in two newspapers of general circulation published in such municipality, if any, and,
      if none, then in two newspapers published in the county, and, in either event, also
      in the legal journal, if any, published in the county.  Where only one newspaper of general circulation is published in a county or in a
      municipality, publication in such one newspaper and in the legal journal, if any,
      shall be deemed sufficient.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions›Chapter 11. Statutory Provisions›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1104. Printing of amendatory statutes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions › Chapter 11. Statutory Provisions › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1104. Printing of amendatory statutes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1104. Printing of amendatory statutes (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The Director of the Legislative Reference Bureau shall, in printing amendatory statutes,
      cause to be printed the section or part of the statute only as reenacted.  Except as provided in subsection (b) of this section, in the section or part of
      the law reenacted, the Director shall cause to be printed between brackets, the words,
      phrases, or provisions of the existing statute, if any, which have been stricken out
      or eliminated by the adoption of the amendment, and he shall cause to be printed in
      italics or with underscoring all new words, phrases or provisions, if any, which have
      been inserted into or added to the statute by the passage of such amendment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part V. Statutory Construction›Chapter 15. General Provisions›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1504. Statutory remedy preferred over common law
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part V. Statutory Construction › Chapter 15. General Provisions › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1504. Statutory remedy preferred over common law
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1504. Statutory remedy preferred over common law (2023)
content:
In all cases where a remedy is provided or a duty is enjoined or anything is directed
   to be done by any statute, the directions of the statute shall be strictly pursued,
   and no penalty shall be inflicted, or anything done agreeably to the common law, in
   such cases, further than shall be necessary for carrying such statute into effect.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions›Chapter 11. Statutory Provisions›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1106. Prothonotaries to keep files of advance copies of statutes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part III. Adoption and Publication of Constitutional and Statutory Provisions › Chapter 11. Statutory Provisions › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1106. Prothonotaries to keep files of advance copies of statutes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1106. Prothonotaries to keep files of advance copies of statutes (2023)
content:
The prothonotaries of the several counties shall file and keep in their offices, in
   such manner that they shall be accessible to the public during the office hours of
   the prothonotaries, advance copies of the statutes enacted at each session of the
   General Assembly, as such advance copies are furnished to them in accordance with
   law, until the statutes of such session as printed in the Laws of Pennsylvania are
   generally available.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part V. Statutory Construction›Chapter 15. General Provisions›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1503. Applicability of colonial law
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part V. Statutory Construction › Chapter 15. General Provisions › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1503. Applicability of colonial law
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1503. Applicability of colonial law (2023)
content:
(a) English law.--The common law and such of the statutes of England as were in force in the Province
      of Pennsylvania on May 14, 1776 and which were properly adapted to the circumstances
      of the inhabitants of this Commonwealth shall be deemed to have been in force in this
      Commonwealth from and after February 10, 1777.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part V. Statutory Construction›Chapter 17. Effective Date of Statutes›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1704. Statutes enacted at a special session
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part V. Statutory Construction › Chapter 17. Effective Date of Statutes › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1704. Statutes enacted at a special session
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1704. Statutes enacted at a special session (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Statutes enacted finally at a special or extraordinary session of the General Assembly
      shall, except as otherwise provided in this section, be governed as to the time when
      they shall be effective by the rules of construction specified in this chapter for
      statutes enacted finally at regular sessions of the General Assembly.

content:
Statutes affecting the budget of any political subdivision enacted finally at any

   of the statute:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part V. Statutory Construction›Chapter 17. Effective Date of Statutes›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1701. Statutes generally

content:

      session of the General Assembly not containing a specified effective date shall be
      effective on the date specified by that one of the following rules of construction
      in effect on the date of final enactment of the statute:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part V. Statutory Construction›Chapter 19. Rules of Construction›Subchapter A. Construction of Words and Phrases›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1902. Number; gender; tense
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part V. Statutory Construction › Chapter 19. Rules of Construction › Subchapter A. Construction of Words and Phrases › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1902. Number; gender; tense
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1902. Number; gender; tense (2023)
content: The singular shall include the plural, and the plural, the singular.  Words used in the masculine gender shall include the feminine and neuter.  Words used in the past or present tense shall include the future.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part V. Statutory Construction›Chapter 17. Effective Date of Statutes›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1702. Statutes making appropriations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part V. Statutory Construction › Chapter 17. Effective Date of Statutes › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1702. Statutes making appropriations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1702. Statutes making appropriations (2023)
content:
Appropriation statutes, or statutes having appropriation items enacted finally at
   any regular session of the General Assembly, shall be effective on the date specified
   by that one of the following rules of construction in effect on the date of final
   enactment of the statute:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part V. Statutory Construction›Chapter 19. Rules of Construction›Subchapter A. Construction of Words and Phrases›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1901. Rules of interpretation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part V. Statutory Construction › Chapter 19. Rules of Construction › Subchapter A. Construction of Words and Phrases › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1901. Rules of interpretation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1901. Rules of interpretation (2023)
content:
In the construction of the statutes of this Commonwealth, the rules set forth in this
   chapter shall be observed, unless the application of such rules would result in a
   construction inconsistent with the manifest intent of the General Assembly.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part V. Statutory Construction›Chapter 19. Rules of Construction›Subchapter A. Construction of Words and Phrases›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1906. Bonds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part V. Statutory Construction › Chapter 19. Rules of Construction › Subchapter A. Construction of Words and Phrases › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1906. Bonds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1906. Bonds (2023)
content:
A statute requiring a bond or undertaking with sureties to be given by any person,
   shall be construed to permit in lieu thereof a bond of indemnity or surety bond for
   the amount of such bond or undertaking, given by any indemnity or surety company authorized
   to do business in this Commonwealth, and approved by the proper authority.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions›Part V. Statutory Construction›Chapter 19. Rules of Construction›Subchapter A. Construction of Words and Phrases›PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1904. Numerals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 1 Pa.C.S.A. General Provisions › Part V. Statutory Construction › Chapter 19. Rules of Construction › Subchapter A. Construction of Words and Phrases › PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1904. Numerals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 1 Pa.C.S.A. § 1904. Numerals (2023)
content: The Roman numerals and the Arabic numerals shall be deemed parts of the English language.
