path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 11. Capital Surplus, Expense Fund and Capital Securities›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1104. Expense fund
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 11. Capital Surplus, Expense Fund and Capital Securities › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1104. Expense fund
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1104. Expense fund (2023)
content:
The expense fund required under section 1010(b)1of this act shall be created out of the portion of amounts paid for shares of common
   stock which is in excess of one hundred fifty percent of the par value of such shares.  Such expense fund may be charged for expenses incurred by the institution in connection
   with its incorporation and operation and any balance in such fund at any time after
   the expiration of one year from the date of the issuance to the institution of a certificate
   of authorization to do business may be credited to undivided profits.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 11. Capital Surplus, Expense Fund and Capital Securities›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1101. Application of chapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 11. Capital Surplus, Expense Fund and Capital Securities › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1101. Application of chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1101. Application of chapter (2023)
content:
This chapter shall apply to, and the word “institution” in the chapter shall mean, a bank, a bank and trust company, a trust company and
   a stock savings bank.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 10. Incorporation›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1011. Organization meetings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 10. Incorporation › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1011. Organization meetings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1011. Organization meetings (2023)
content:
(a) After the filing of the articles in the Department of State, the first meeting
      of the shareholders shall be held within this Commonwealth at the call of the shareholders
      who were the incorporators, or a majority of them, for the purpose of adopting such
      by-laws as this act and the articles require to be adopted by the shareholders and
      for such other purposes as shall be stated in the notice of the meeting.  The shareholders who call the meeting shall give to each shareholder at least five
      days’ written notice of the time and place of the meeting.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 10. Incorporation›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1008. Issuance of certificate of incorporation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 10. Incorporation › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1008. Issuance of certificate of incorporation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1008. Issuance of certificate of incorporation (2023)
content:
If all the taxes, fees and charges required by law shall have been paid and if the
   name of the proposed institution continues to be reserved or is available on the records
   of the Department of State, the receipt of the articles by the Department of State
   with the written approval of the Department of Banking, shall constitute filing of
   the articles with the Department of State as of the date and time of receipt or as
   of any later date and time specified by the Department of Banking.  The Department of State shall immediately issue to the incorporators a certificate
   of incorporation, as of the date and time of filing, with the approved articles attached
   thereto and shall make and retain a copy of such certificate and articles.

content:
(a) Until receipt of a certificate of authorization issued by the department, an institution
      shall not accept deposits, incur indebtedness or transact any business except such
      business as is incident to its organization or to the obtaining of subscriptions and
      payment for its shares and other securities--subject to the penalty provisions of
      this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 10. Incorporation›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1012. Organization as a limited liability company
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 10. Incorporation › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1012. Organization as a limited liability company
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1012. Organization as a limited liability company (2023)
content:
(a) General rule--Subject to any conditions or restrictions as determined by the department, a bank,
      bank and trust company, trust company or savings bank may be organized as a limited
      liability company pursuant to 15 Pa.C.S. Ch. 89 (relating to limited liability companies)
      in order to conduct the business of a bank, bank and trust company, trust company
      or savings bank subject to this act.

      of the institution shall begin and, except in the case of a mutual savings bank, those
      persons who subscribed for shares prior to such filing of the articles, or their assignees,
      shall be shareholders in the institution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1204. Payment of subscriptions and default in payment of subscriptions for shares
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1204. Payment of subscriptions and default in payment of subscriptions for shares
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1204. Payment of subscriptions and default in payment of subscriptions for shares (2023)
content:
The provisions of the Business Corporation Law applicable to payment of subscriptions
   for shares of stock and default in payment of such subscriptions shall apply to the
   payment of subscriptions for shares of an institution and the rights of the institution
   in the event of default in payment of subscriptions for shares, except that references
   in those provisions to a “corporation” shall mean an institution as defined for the
   purpose of this chapter and references to the “registered office” of a corporation
   shall mean the principal office of the institution and except that any advertisement
   provided for under those sections shall comply with the requirements for advertisements
   under section 1091of this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1208. Preemptive rights of shareholders

content:
(a) Unless otherwise provided in its articles, an institution may issue shares, option
      rights or securities having conversion or option rights without first offering them
      to shareholders of any class.

content:
(a) Contents--The shares of an institution shall be represented by share certificates which shall

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1212. Voting rights of shareholders
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1212. Voting rights of shareholders
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1212. Voting rights of shareholders (2023)
content:
(a) Right to vote--Except as otherwise provided in the articles or in this act, every shareholder of
      record shall have the right at every shareholders' meeting to one vote for each share
      standing in his name on the books of the institution.  A shareholder may vote in person or by proxy and shall not sell his vote or execute
      a proxy for any sum of money or anything of value.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1207. Liability of subscribers and shareholders
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1207. Liability of subscribers and shareholders
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1207. Liability of subscribers and shareholders (2023)
content:
A subscriber to, or holder of, shares of an institution shall have no liability with
   respect to such shares other than the obligation of complying with the terms of the
   subscription for such shares which shall be the same as the obligation on a share
   subscription governed by the Business Corporation Law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1211. Quorum of and action by shareholders
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1211. Quorum of and action by shareholders
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1211. Quorum of and action by shareholders (2023)
content:
(a) Requirement--A shareholders' meeting duly called shall not be organized for the transaction of
      business unless a quorum is present.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1213. Election of directors; cumulative voting
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1213. Election of directors; cumulative voting
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1213. Election of directors; cumulative voting (2023)
content:
(a) Elections of directors need not be by ballot, except as otherwise provided in
      the by-laws or upon demand made by a shareholder at the election and before the voting
      begins.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1215. Voting by joint holders of shares
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1215. Voting by joint holders of shares
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1215. Voting by joint holders of shares (2023)
content:
(a) Shares which are held jointly or as tenants in common by two or more persons,
      as fiduciaries or otherwise, shall be deemed to be represented for the purpose of
      determining a quorum if one or more such persons are present in person or by proxy.  Except as provided in subsection (b) of this section, the vote of all such shares
      shall be the vote cast by such person or a majority of such persons but if such persons
      are equally divided upon the manner of voting, the vote of the shares held by them
      shall be divided equally among such persons, without prejudice to the rights of such
      joint owners or the beneficial owners thereof among themselves.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1209. Meetings of shareholders
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1209. Meetings of shareholders
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1209. Meetings of shareholders (2023)
content:
(a) Place--Meetings of the shareholders of an institution shall be held at such place within
      the Commonwealth as shall be fixed by the by-laws or by the board of directors pursuant
      to the by-laws or, if none is so fixed, at the principal place of business of the
      institution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1214. Voting by fiduciaries and pledgees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1214. Voting by fiduciaries and pledgees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1214. Voting by fiduciaries and pledgees (2023)
content:
(a) Shares standing in the name of a fiduciary may be voted either in person or by
      proxy of the fiduciary.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1210. Notice of meetings of shareholders
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1210. Notice of meetings of shareholders
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1210. Notice of meetings of shareholders (2023)
content:
Written notice of each meeting of shareholders shall be given to each shareholder
   of record entitled to vote at the meeting at least five days prior to the date thereof,
   unless a longer period of notice is required by the articles, by-laws or other provisions
   of this act.  Notice of an adjourned meeting and of the business to be transacted at such meeting
   may be given by announcement at the meeting at which the adjournment is taken unless
   otherwise provided in the articles or by-laws.

content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1219. Voting trusts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1219. Voting trusts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1219. Voting trusts (2023)
content:
(a) Agreement--Two or more shareholders of an institution may, upon the terms and conditions stated
      in an agreement in writing, transfer their shares to one or more voting trustees other
      than the institution for the purpose of vesting in the transferee or transferees voting
      or other rights in respect of such shares for a period not in excess of ten years.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 13. Dividends and Distributions to Shareholders; Redemption or Acquisition of Preferred Shares›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1306. Redemption and acquisition of redeemable shares; statement of reduction of authorized shares
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 13. Dividends and Distributions to Shareholders; Redemption or Acquisition of Preferred Shares › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1306. Redemption and acquisition of redeemable shares; statement of reduction of authorized shares
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1306. Redemption and acquisition of redeemable shares; statement of reduction of authorized shares (2023)
content:
(a) Unless otherwise provided in its articles, an institution may by resolution of
      its board of directors and with the prior approval of the department redeem or otherwise
      acquire shares subject to redemption if immediately after the redemption or other
      acquisition surplus would be at least equal to the amount of capital.  In determining whether or not to give its approval under this subsection (a), the
      department shall give primary consideration to the question whether or not, after
      the cancellation of the shares, the capital accounts of the institution would be adequate
      to support its anticipated deposit volume.  The provisions of this section do not restrict or otherwise affect the power of
      an institution with prior approval of the department to purchase (subject to the requirements
      of this act as to capital and surplus), hold and own its shares other than shares
      subject to redemption.

      shall at least five days before each meeting of shareholders make a list of the shareholders
      entitled to vote at the meeting, arranged in alphabetical order with the address of

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1217. Determination of shareholders of record
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1217. Determination of shareholders of record

(a) The board of directors of an institution may, except as otherwise provided in
      its by-laws, fix a date for the determination of the shareholders entitled to receive
      notice of and to vote at any meeting or to receive any dividend, distribution or allotment
      of rights or a date for any change, conversion or exchange of shares by:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1222. Rights of dissenting shareholders
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1222. Rights of dissenting shareholders
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1222. Rights of dissenting shareholders (2023)
content:
If a shareholder of an institution shall object to a proposed plan of action of the
   institution authorized under a section of this act and such section provides that
   the shareholder shall be entitled to the rights and remedies of a dissenting shareholder,
   the rights and remedies of such shareholder shall be governed by the provisions of
   the Business Corporation Law1applicable to dissenting shareholders and shall be subject to the limitations on
   such rights and remedies under those provisions.  Shares acquired by an institution as a result of the exercise of such rights by
   a dissenting shareholder may be held and disposed of as treasury shares or, in the
   case of a merger or consolidation, as otherwise provided in the plan of merger or
   consolidation.

content:
(a) A judge or three judges of election, and an alternate or alternates to act in
      the event of a vacancy, may be appointed:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1221. Informal action by shareholders
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 12. Shares and Shareholders › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1221. Informal action by shareholders
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1221. Informal action by shareholders (2023)
content:
Any action which may be taken at a meeting of shareholders may, unless otherwise provided
   in the articles or by-laws, be taken without a meeting if a consent or consents in
   writing setting forth the action so taken shall be signed by all of the shareholders
   who would be entitled to vote on such action at a meeting and shall be filed with
   the secretary of the institution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 13. Dividends and Distributions to Shareholders; Redemption or Acquisition of Preferred Shares›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1304. Liability for unlawful dividends and distributions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 13. Dividends and Distributions to Shareholders; Redemption or Acquisition of Preferred Shares › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1304. Liability for unlawful dividends and distributions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1304. Liability for unlawful dividends and distributions (2023)
content:
(a) Prohibition--The directors of an institution shall not declare dividends, or authorize or ratify
      the distribution of any part of its assets to shareholders by purchase of its shares
      or otherwise, except as authorized by this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 13. Dividends and Distributions to Shareholders; Redemption or Acquisition of Preferred Shares›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1302. Cash dividends
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 13. Dividends and Distributions to Shareholders; Redemption or Acquisition of Preferred Shares › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1302. Cash dividends
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1302. Cash dividends (2023)
content:
(a) Authorized dividends--The board of directors of an institution may, from time to time, declare, and the
      institution may pay, dividends on its outstanding shares subject to the restrictions
      of this act and to the restrictions, if any, in its articles.  Dividends may be declared and paid out of accumulated net earnings of the institution
      or accumulated net earnings acquired as a result of a merger and transferred to surplus,
      if used within seven years of the date of merger, and may be paid in cash or property
      other than its own shares.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 14. Directors or Trustees; Officers, Employees and Attorneys›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1401. Application of chapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 14. Directors or Trustees; Officers, Employees and Attorneys › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1401. Application of chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1401. Application of chapter (2023)
content: This chapter shall apply to, and the word “institution” in this chapter shall mean, an incorporated institution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 13. Dividends and Distributions to Shareholders; Redemption or Acquisition of Preferred Shares›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1301. Application of chapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 13. Dividends and Distributions to Shareholders; Redemption or Acquisition of Preferred Shares › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1301. Application of chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1301. Application of chapter (2023)
content:
This chapter shall apply to, and the word “institution” in this chapter shall mean, a bank, a bank and trust company, a trust company and
   a stock savings bank.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 13. Dividends and Distributions to Shareholders; Redemption or Acquisition of Preferred Shares›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1303. Distributions of shares of institution
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 13. Dividends and Distributions to Shareholders; Redemption or Acquisition of Preferred Shares › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1303. Distributions of shares of institution
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1303. Distributions of shares of institution (2023)
content:
(a) Authorized distributions--The board of directors of an institution may distribute pro rata to holders of any
      class of its shares from time to time treasury shares and authorized but unissued
      shares of the institution, subject to the restrictions of this act and to the restrictions,
      if any, in its articles.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 13. Dividends and Distributions to Shareholders; Redemption or Acquisition of Preferred Shares›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1305. Distribution upon reduction of capital
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 13. Dividends and Distributions to Shareholders; Redemption or Acquisition of Preferred Shares › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1305. Distribution upon reduction of capital
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1305. Distribution upon reduction of capital (2023)
content:
(a) Upon the decrease of capital of an institution pursuant to an amendment of its
      articles to reduce its authorized capital, the board of directors may, with the approval
      of the department and subject to the restrictions, if any, of its articles, distribute
      to the shareholders of the institution an amount in cash equal to all or part of the
      amount of the decrease in capital together with a like amount of surplus, if immediately
      after such distribution the institution would have the capital required by this act
      and would have surplus in an amount at least equal to its capital.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 14. Directors or Trustees; Officers, Employees and Attorneys›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1402. Board of directors or trustees; honorary and advisory positions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 14. Directors or Trustees; Officers, Employees and Attorneys › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1402. Board of directors or trustees; honorary and advisory positions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1402. Board of directors or trustees; honorary and advisory positions (2023)
content:
(a) Authority--The business and affairs of an institution shall be managed by a board of trustees
      in the case of a savings bank and by a board of directors in the case of any other
      institution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 14. Directors or Trustees; Officers, Employees and Attorneys›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1406. Oaths of directors or trustees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 14. Directors or Trustees; Officers, Employees and Attorneys › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1406. Oaths of directors or trustees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1406. Oaths of directors or trustees (2023)
content:
(a) Each director or trustee shall before assuming office take an oath or affirmation
      that he will diligently and honestly perform his duties in the administration of the
      affairs of the institution, that he will not permit a wilful violation of law by the
      institution and that he meets the eligibility requirements of this act and of the
      articles and by-laws.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 14. Directors or Trustees; Officers, Employees and Attorneys›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1403. Number, qualifications and eligibility of directors or trustees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 14. Directors or Trustees; Officers, Employees and Attorneys › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1403. Number, qualifications and eligibility of directors or trustees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1403. Number, qualifications and eligibility of directors or trustees (2023)
content:
(a) Number--The by-laws may fix the number of trustees of a savings bank at not less than five.  The by-laws of any other institution may fix the number of directors at not less
      than five or more than twenty-five and may provide that the board may, within such
      limitation, increase the number of directors by not more than two in any one year.

content: Except as otherwise provided in this act or in the articles or by-laws:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 14. Directors or Trustees; Officers, Employees and Attorneys›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1404. Term of office of directors or trustees; vacancies; classification of directors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 14. Directors or Trustees; Officers, Employees and Attorneys › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1404. Term of office of directors or trustees; vacancies; classification of directors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1404. Term of office of directors or trustees; vacancies; classification of directors (2023)
content:
(a) Term of office--Each trustee of a mutual savings bank shall, except as otherwise specifically provided
      in its articles, hold office until he resigns, is removed or becomes disqualified
      and each director of any other institution shall hold office until he resigns, is
      removed, becomes disqualified or until his successor shall have been duly elected
      and qualified.  Directors shall be elected by the shareholders for a term of one year except as
      otherwise provided in this chapter or in the articles or the by-laws.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 14. Directors or Trustees; Officers, Employees and Attorneys›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1409. Officers; share purchase and option plans
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 14. Directors or Trustees; Officers, Employees and Attorneys › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1409. Officers; share purchase and option plans
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1409. Officers; share purchase and option plans (2023)
content:
(a) Number--An institution shall have a president, a secretary and a cashier or treasurer and
      such other officers as it may authorize.  The by-laws may provide that the same individual may hold any two or more offices
      except both the offices of president and of cashier or treasurer.  The president shall be a member of the board of directors or trustees.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 14. Directors or Trustees; Officers, Employees and Attorneys›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1410. Bonds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 14. Directors or Trustees; Officers, Employees and Attorneys › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1410. Bonds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1410. Bonds (2023)
content:
Each officer and employe and any director or trustee who is authorized to handle money
   or negotiable assets on behalf of the institution shall be bonded and the institution
   may pay the cost of such bond.  The form, amount and surety of such bonds shall be such as is approved by the board
   of directors or trustees but the department may require an additional amount or new
   or additional surety.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1413. Prohibitions applicable to directors, trustees, officers, employes and attorneys (2023)
content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 14. Directors or Trustees; Officers, Employees and Attorneys›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1414. Preferential rates of interest
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 14. Directors or Trustees; Officers, Employees and Attorneys › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1414. Preferential rates of interest
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1414. Preferential rates of interest (2023)
content:
(a) Preferences prohibited--Notwithstanding the provisions of section 3061and except as provided by subsection (c), an institution shall not pay to any director,
      trustee, executive officer or attorney a higher rate of interest on deposits than
      the rate paid to any other depositor on similar deposits and shall not grant to any
      such individual a lower rate of interest on a loan, or a lower rate of charge on an
      agreement for the payment of money, than the rate granted to other customers under
      similar circumstances.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 14. Directors or Trustees; Officers, Employees and Attorneys › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1407. Audits and reports by directors or trustees; accountants; internal auditors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1407. Audits and reports by directors or trustees; accountants; internal auditors (2023)
content:
(a) Annual audit--Except as provided in subsection (c) of this section, the board of directors or trustees
      shall at least once each year have made, by certified public accountants selected
      by the institution and satisfactory to the department, an audit of the books and affairs
      of the institution including such matters as may be required by the department and
      including, in the case of a bank and trust company, a savings bank or a trust company,
      accounts held in a fiduciary or other representative capacity.  The department may by regulation establish minimum standards for audits and reports
      under this subsection (a).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 14. Directors or Trustees; Officers, Employees and Attorneys›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1418. Standard of care and justifiable reliance

   duties.

      merger or consolidation will result in an institution subject to this act who objects
      to the plan shall be entitled to the rights and remedies of a dissenting shareholder
      provided under, and subject to compliance with, the provisions of section 12221of this act.

content:

   and, in the case of a change of name, if the proposed new name of the institution
   continues to be reserved or is available on the records of the Department of State,
   the receipt of the articles of amendment by the Department of State with the written
   approval of the Department of Banking shall constitute filing of the articles of amendment

   of amendment as of the date and time of filing with the approved articles of amendment

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 16. Mergers, Consolidations and Certain Other Fundamental Transactions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1602. Authority to merge or consolidate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1602. Authority to merge or consolidate (2023)
content:
(a) Upon compliance with the requirements of this chapter one or more institutions
      and one or more national banks, Federal savings banks and interstate banks, without
      regard to whether any such interstate bank maintains branches in this Commonwealth
      at the time of a merger or consolidation, may merge or consolidate into a national
      bank or Federal savings bank and, with the approval by the department, may merge with
      or into an institution or consolidate into a new institution or merge a nonbank subsidiary
      into an institution, provided that the institution can engage in activities conducted
      by the subsidiary as principal, except that a trust company may enter into a merger
      or consolidation only with another trust company, a bank and trust company, a national
      bank or a Federal savings bank which has fiduciary powers or a stock savings bank

content:
(a) Rights and remedies--Unless (i) the bylaws, by amendment adopted within ninety days of the date of enactment
      of this section and not subsequently rescinded by an amendment of the articles, or

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 16. Mergers, Consolidations and Certain Other Fundamental Transactions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1605. Procedure after approval by the department; issuance of certificate of merger or consolidation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 16. Mergers, Consolidations and Certain Other Fundamental Transactions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1605. Procedure after approval by the department; issuance of certificate of merger or consolidation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1605. Procedure after approval by the department; issuance of certificate of merger or consolidation (2023)
content:
(a) If the laws of the United States require the approval of the merger or consolidation
      by any Federal agency, the department shall, after its approval, retain the articles
      of merger or consolidation until it receives notice of the decision of such agency.  If such agency shall refuse to give its approval, the department shall notify the
      parties to the plan that the department's approval has been rescinded for that reason.  If such agency gives its approval, the Department of Banking shall immediately deliver
      the articles of merger or consolidation with its written approval to the Department
      of State for filing as of a date and time specified by the Department of Banking and
      shall notify the parties to the plan.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 16. Mergers, Consolidations and Certain Other Fundamental Transactions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1608. Succession to fiduciary accounts and appointments; application for appointment of new fiduciary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1608. Succession to fiduciary accounts and appointments; application for appointment of new fiduciary (2023)
content:
(a) Fiduciary accounts--If a party to a plan of merger or consolidation was authorized to act in a fiduciary
      capacity and if the resulting institution, resulting national bank or resulting interstate
      bank is similarly authorized, the resulting institution, resulting national bank or
      resulting interstate bank shall be automatically substituted by reason of the merger
      or consolidation as fiduciary of all accounts held in that capacity by such party
      to the plan, without further action and without any order or decree of any court or
      public officer, and shall have all the rights and be subject to all the obligations
      of such party as fiduciary.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 17. Conversions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1710. Rights of dissenting shareholders of converting national bank or interstate bank
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 17. Conversions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1710. Rights of dissenting shareholders of converting national bank or interstate bank
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1710. Rights of dissenting shareholders of converting national bank or interstate bank (2023)
content:
If a shareholder of a national bank or interstate bank which converts into an institution
   shall object to the plan of conversion and shall comply with the requirements of applicable
   laws of the United States or the laws of the jurisdiction under which the interstate
   bank exists, the resulting institution shall be liable for the value of his shares
   as determined in accordance with such laws of the United States or the laws of the
   jurisdiction under which the interstate bank exists.  If the laws of the United States do not provide rights of dissenting shareholders
   or requirements for the exercise of such rights and the valuation of shares, such
   shareholder shall be entitled to the rights and remedies of a dissenting shareholder
   under, and subject to compliance with, the provisions of section 12221of this act.

content:

   name of the resulting institution continues to be reserved or is available on the
   records of the Department of State, the receipt of the articles of conversion by the
   Department of State with the written approval of the Department of Banking shall constitute
   filing of the articles of conversion as of the date and time of receipt or as of any

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1902. Continuation of and changes in existing private banks (2023)
content:

      in conducting the business of a private bank may continue to do so but no new private
      bank shall hereafter be established.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 19. Private Banks › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1904. Issuance of certificate of authorization or rejection of application
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1904. Issuance of certificate of authorization or rejection of application (2023)
content:
(a) Issuance of certificate--The department shall, immediately upon receipt of the application of a private bank,
      conduct such investigation as it may deem necessary to ascertain the financial condition
      and responsibility of the private bank, and the reliability of any new partner or
      partners being admitted.  If it shall find that the provisions of this act have been complied with, that the
      financial condition and responsibility of the private bank is such as to warrant a
      continuance of the business and that it approves any new partner or partners, it shall
      retain and file one of the duplicate originals of the application, and shall issue
      a certificate of authorization, empowering the private bank to continue in business.  The other duplicate original and the certificate of authorization shall be sent
      by the department to the private bank.  The certificate shall at all times be conspicuously posted in the place of business
      of the private bank in view of its customers.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 19. Private Banks›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1905. Reserve against deposits
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 19. Private Banks › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1905. Reserve against deposits
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1905. Reserve against deposits (2023)
content:
No certificate of authorization shall be granted to a private bank unless it shall
   have a reserve fund for deposits in an amount at least equal to that required by this
   act for an incorporated bank.  The entire amount of such reserve fund shall be at all times maintained in the manner
   provided by this act for an incorporated bank.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 19. Private Banks›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1906. Segregation of assets
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 19. Private Banks › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1906. Segregation of assets
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1906. Segregation of assets (2023)
content:
All assets of a private bank shall be segregated and kept apart from the property
   and assets of the owner or owners of the private bank in their individual capacities.  All such assets shall be carried in the name of the private bank or in the name
   of a nominee of the private bank.  If its name is the same as that of the individual owner, or, in the case of a partnership,
   of any of the owners thereof, all assets of the private bank shall be carried in such
   name, with the addition of the descriptive words “private bank.”  In such case all deeds, mortgages, assignments, contracts and agreements shall be
   received, taken or entered into in the name of the private bank with the addition
   of the descriptive words “private bank.”

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 20. Provisions Applicable to Department of Banking [Heading Repealed] › PA ST 7 P.S. § 2004. Relationship of institutions and their personnel with officials and employes of department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 2004. Relationship of institutions and their personnel with officials and employes of department (2023)
content:
(a) Loans and Gifts--Notwithstanding the provisions of section 1114-A of the act of May 15, 1933 (P.L.
      565, No. 111),1known as the “Department of Banking Code,” relating to conflicts of interests, and
      except as provided in subsection (d) of this section, an institution or any director,
      trustee, officer, employe or attorney thereof shall not grant or give to the Secretary
      of Banking, any official or employe of the department, any deputy receiver or any
      employe of the Secretary of Banking as receiver, none of whom shall receive, any sum
      of money or any property as a gift or loan or otherwise, directly or indirectly--subject
      to the penalty provisions of this act.  This subsection shall not apply to loans to employes of the Department of Banking
      who function in a clerical or nondecision making capacity with regard to institutions,
      including but not limited to clerks, typists and stenographers.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 21. Penalties and Criminal Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 2102. Penalties and criminal provisions applicable to directors, trustees, officers, employes and attorneys of institutions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 2102. Penalties and criminal provisions applicable to directors, trustees, officers, employes and attorneys of institutions (2023)
content:
(a) Violations of sections 1413, 1416 and 1912--A director, trustee, officer, employe or attorney of an institution who wilfully violates
      any of the provisions of sections 1413, 1416 or 1912 of this act1shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall upon conviction thereof be subject to
      imprisonment for a period not exceeding one year, or a fine not exceeding one thousand
      dollars ($1,000), or both;  and shall be subject to a further fine of a sum equal
      to:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 19. Private Banks›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1910. Directors, officers, employes and attorneys of private banks
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 19. Private Banks › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1910. Directors, officers, employes and attorneys of private banks
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1910. Directors, officers, employes and attorneys of private banks (2023)
content:
(a) Board--The business and affairs of a private bank may be managed by a board of directors.  The partnership agreement or the by-laws of such private bank may grant the board
      of directors such powers, prescribe such procedures, and impose such restrictions
      and limitations upon the board as the partners in the private bank may agree upon
      with respect to all matters that are dealt with as to incorporated institutions by
      chapter 14 of the act1or which are normally provided for by the articles or by-laws of an incorporated
      institution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 19. Private Banks›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1907. Exclusion from financial records of loans to owners of private bank and certain investments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 19. Private Banks › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1907. Exclusion from financial records of loans to owners of private bank and certain investments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1907. Exclusion from financial records of loans to owners of private bank and certain investments (2023)
content:
No loan made by a private bank, directly or indirectly, to the owner or owners thereof,
   or to any person with whom the owner or any of the owners of such private bank is
   associated as partner or member of an unincorporated association, or to any corporation
   twenty-five percent or more of the capital of which is owned legally or equitably
   by the owners of the private bank, and no investment made in any business conducted
   by any such partnership, unincorporated association or corporation shall be included
   as an asset upon the books or other records or in any statement of the financial condition
   of the private bank, except to the extent of the value of a mortgage upon real property
   which complies with the requirements of this act or the market value of collateral
   which secures such loan.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 19. Private Banks›PA ST 7 P.S. § 1913. Conversion of private bank into incorporated institution
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 19. Private Banks › PA ST 7 P.S. § 1913. Conversion of private bank into incorporated institution
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 1913. Conversion of private bank into incorporated institution (2023)
content:
(a) Authority--A private bank may convert into a bank or a bank and trust company upon adoption of
      a plan of conversion by its owner or owners and approval of the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 21. Penalties and Criminal Provisions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 2103. Penalties applicable to institutions for violation of section 705
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 21. Penalties and Criminal Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 2103. Penalties applicable to institutions for violation of section 705
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 2103. Penalties applicable to institutions for violation of section 705 (2023)
content:
An institution which fails to give written notice to the department of a deficiency
   in its reserve fund as required by section 7051shall pay to the department a penalty of fifty dollars ($50) for each day that it
   does not give such notice after the time fixed by section 705 for the giving of such
   notice.  The department may in its discretion relieve any institution from the payment of
   such penalty, in whole or in part, upon a showing to the department of good cause
   for the failure of the institution to give such notice.  If an institution fails to pay a penalty from which it has not been thus relieved,
   the Department of Banking may through the Department of Justice maintain an action
   at law to recover it.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967›Article I. General Provisions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-1. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967 › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-1. Short title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-1. Short title (2023)
content: This act shall be known, and may be cited, as the “Savings Association Code of 1967.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967›Article I. General Provisions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-6. Certificates and certified copies of documents to be received in evidence
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967 › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-6. Certificates and certified copies of documents to be received in evidence
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-6. Certificates and certified copies of documents to be received in evidence (2023)
content:
All certificates issued by the Department of Banking and by the Department of State
   and all copies of articles, papers and other documents filed in either department
   and certified by the Secretary of the Department of Banking or by the Secretary of
   the Commonwealth shall be taken and received by all courts, public offices, and official
   bodies as prima facie evidence of the facts therein stated.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 21. Penalties and Criminal Provisions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 2105. Penalties applicable to persons for violation of section 112
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 21. Penalties and Criminal Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 2105. Penalties applicable to persons for violation of section 112
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 2105. Penalties applicable to persons for violation of section 112 (2023)
content:
(a) Criminal liability--Any person who acquires or proposes to acquire shares of an institution or of a corporation
      which controls an institution in violation of section 1121or who violates subsection (g) thereof shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall
      upon conviction thereof be subject, in the case of an individual, to imprisonment
      for a period not exceeding five years, or a fine not exceeding five thousand dollars
      ($5,000), or both, and, in the case of any other person, to a fine not exceeding fifty
      thousand dollars ($50,000).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 21. Penalties and Criminal Provisions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 2104. Penalties applicable to persons subject to this act
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 21. Penalties and Criminal Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 2104. Penalties applicable to persons subject to this act
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 2104. Penalties applicable to persons subject to this act (2023)
content:
(a) Violations of sections 105, 106--Any person who wilfully engages in the business of receiving deposits or money for
      transmission, or who wilfully establishes a place of business for such purpose, in
      violation of section 1051and any person whom such person represents, and any corporation which wilfully acts
      in a fiduciary capacity in violation of section 106,2shall be guilty of a felony and shall upon conviction thereof be subject, in the
      case of an individual, to imprisonment for a period not exceeding two years, or a
      fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars ($10,000) per violation, or both, and, in
      the case of any other person, to a fine not exceeding five hundred thousand dollars
      ($500,000).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 22. Effective Date, Repealers and Transition Provisions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 2201. Effective date
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 22. Effective Date, Repealers and Transition Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 2201. Effective date
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 2201. Effective date (2023)
content:
This act shall take effect at 12:01 A.M. on the first Sunday of the month which is
   the second month after the month in which this act is approved.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967 › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-2. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-2. Definitions (2023)
content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 50. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 5005. Savings banks with capital stock to issue certificates thereof for transfer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 50. Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 5005. Savings banks with capital stock to issue certificates thereof for transfer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 5005. Savings banks with capital stock to issue certificates thereof for transfer (2023)
content:
All savings banks having a capital stock are hereby authorized and required to issue
   certificates of their said stock, to all the stockholders, properly signed by the
   president, secretary or treasurer of said savings bank, which certificates transferred
   by the party holding the same, or his duly authorized attorney, in the presence of
   the president, secretary or treasurer, shall be a valid and legal transfer of the
   said stock.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 50. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 5004. Investment of deposits in obligations issued by federal banks
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 50. Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 5004. Investment of deposits in obligations issued by federal banks
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 5004. Investment of deposits in obligations issued by federal banks (2023)
content:
From and after the passage of this act, trustees or directors of savings banks, savings
   institutions, and provident institutions, chartered under general or special acts
   of Assembly of this Commonwealth, may, notwithstanding any provisions of their charter,
   or of any act of Assembly under which they may have been incorporated, invest the
   moneys deposited in said savings banks, savings institutions, and provident institutions
   in debentures, bonds or other obligations issued by Federal Land Banks or by Federal
   Intermediate Credit Banks under the authority of the Federal Farm Loan Act and its
   amendments and supplements,1or by Banks for Cooperatives under authority of the Federal Farm Credit Act of 1933
   and its amendments and supplements,2or by Federal Home Loan Banks under authority of the Federal Home Loan Bank Act and
   its amendments and supplements.3

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 50. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 5003. Payment of bank tax
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 50. Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 5003. Payment of bank tax
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 5003. Payment of bank tax (2023)
content:
The bank tax imposed by the laws of this Commonwealth, shall be paid by such bank,
   up to the date of its becoming such association, in proportion to the time since the
   next preceding payment therefor.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-3. Declaration of purposes; standard for exercise of power and discretion by department (2023)
content:
(a) The General Assembly declares as its purposes in adopting this act to provide
      for:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 22. Effective Date, Repealers and Transition Provisions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 2204. Transition provisions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 22. Effective Date, Repealers and Transition Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 2204. Transition provisions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 2204. Transition provisions (2023)
content:
(a) Transactions and proceedings commenced under or pursuant to statutes repealed
      by this act shall be terminated, completed or enforced pursuant to the provisions
      of such statutes which for such purpose shall remain in full force and effect as to
      such transactions and proceedings.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 22. Effective Date, Repealers and Transition Provisions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 2202. Specific repealers

content:
Except as provided in section 2204,1the following acts and parts of acts and all amendments thereof are hereby repealed
   to the extent specified:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967›Article I. General Provisions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-5. Emergency powers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967 › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-5. Emergency powers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-5. Emergency powers (2023)
content:
In the event a nuclear attack or other disaster results in the declaration of an emergency
   an association may during the continuance of such emergency, without regard to any
   restriction or limitation of this act, take any action to preserve the assets of the
   association and to continue or resume its business, including any action to obtain
   the benefit of, or participate in, emergency action authorized by the Federal government.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967›Article I. General Provisions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-7. Advertisement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967 › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-7. Advertisement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-7. Advertisement (2023)
content:
(a) Every advertisement required by this act shall be published, except as otherwise
      provided in this act, once in a newspaper of general circulation and once in a legal
      newspaper.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Banking Code of 1965›Chapter 22. Effective Date, Repealers and Transition Provisions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 2203. General repealer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Banking Code of 1965 › Chapter 22. Effective Date, Repealers and Transition Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 2203. General repealer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 2203. General repealer (2023)
content: Except as provided in section 2204,1all acts and parts of acts inconsistent with this act are hereby repealed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967›Article I. General Provisions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-8. Notices
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967 › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-8. Notices
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-8. Notices (2023)
content:
(a) Written notice required to be given to any person under the provisions of this
      act or under the articles or bylaws of an association may be given to such person,
      either personally or by sending a copy thereof through the mail, or by telegram, charges
      prepaid, to his address appearing on the books of the association, or supplied by
      him to the association for the purpose of notice.  If the notice is sent by mail or by telegraph, it shall be deemed to have been given
      to the person entitled thereto when deposited in the United States mail or with a
      telegraph office for transmission to such person.  If such notice is of a meeting, it shall specify the place, date and hour of the
      meeting, and, in the case of a special meeting of members, the general nature of the
      business to be transacted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967›Article I. General Provisions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-9. Execution of instruments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967 › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-9. Execution of instruments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-9. Execution of instruments (2023)
content:
Without regard to any other form of execution provided in the bylaws, an instrument
   in writing, or any assignment or endorsement thereof, executed or entered into between
   an association and any person and signed by the president or vice-president and by
   the secretary or treasurer of the association, shall be held to have been properly
   executed by and in behalf of the association.  Except as otherwise required by statute, the affixation of the corporate seal shall
   not be necessary to the valid execution, assignment or endorsement by an association
   of any instrument in writing.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967›Article I. General Provisions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-11. Retention of records and admissibility of copies in evidence
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967 › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-11. Retention of records and admissibility of copies in evidence
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-11. Retention of records and admissibility of copies in evidence (2023)
content:
(a) Every association shall preserve in such form and manner that they may be readily
      produced upon proper demand, all of its records of original or final entries for a
      period of seven years from the date of making the last entry thereon, except that
      coupons accompanying deposits in a club account, such as a Christmas club or a vacation
      club, need not be so retained for more than two years from the date of closing of
      such account.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967›Article II. Incorporation and Organization›PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-28. Effect of filing of articles in Department of State and of certificate of incorporation

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967›Article I. General Provisions›PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-10. Books, records and accounts of associations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967 › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-10. Books, records and accounts of associations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-10. Books, records and accounts of associations (2023)
content:
(a) An association may maintain its books of account on a cash, accrual, or modified
      accrual basis, as determined by the board of directors.

content: (a) An association shall not repledge any property held by it in pledge or as collateral.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967 › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-13. Statutory amendment of existing charters

   heretofore granted shall be deemed to be amended to the extent necessary to give effect

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967›Article II. Incorporation and Organization›PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-23. Articles of incorporation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967 › Article II. Incorporation and Organization › PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-23. Articles of incorporation

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-22. Prohibition of promoters' fees (2023)
content:
(a) A savings association shall not pay any fee, compensation or commission for the
      promotion or organization of an association or for any part of the money collected
      from members, except legal fees and other usual and ordinary expenses necessary for
      its organization.  Any incorporator, officer, director or employe paying or receiving any such fee,
      compensation or commission shall be subject to the penalty provisions of this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967›Article IV. Offices›PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-51. Authorized offices

content:
(a) An association may not maintain any office for the conduct of its business other
      than:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967›Article II. Incorporation and Organization›PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-25. Advertisement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967 › Article II. Incorporation and Organization › PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-25. Advertisement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-25. Advertisement (2023)
content:
(a) The incorporators shall advertise their intention to deliver, or the delivery
      of, articles of incorporation with the department once in each newspaper in which
      such advertisement is required to be made and published in accordance with section
      107.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967›Article IV. Offices›PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-53. Authorization of new branches
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967 › Article IV. Offices › PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-53. Authorization of new branches
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-53. Authorization of new branches (2023)
content:
(a) Upon a merger, consolidation or conversion of a Federal savings and loan association
      into a State association the resulting association may with the prior written approval
      of the department maintain as branches, in addition to its principal place of business,
      every office which was maintained prior to the merger or consolidation by the parties
      thereto or prior to the conversion by the Federal savings and loan association and
      which is located within Pennsylvania.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967›Article II. Incorporation and Organization›PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-30. Organization meetings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967 › Article II. Incorporation and Organization › PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-30. Organization meetings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-30. Organization meetings (2023)
content:
(a) After the filing of the articles in the Department of State the first meeting
      of the members shall be held within this Commonwealth at the call of the incorporators,
      or the majority of them, for the purpose of adopting such bylaws as this act and the
      articles require to be adopted by the members, and for such other purposes as shall
      be stated in the notice of the meeting.  The incorporators, at the call of the meeting, shall give to each member at least
      five days' written notice of the time and place of the meeting.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-52. Change of location of office (2023)
content: (a) Deleted by 1982, April 9, P.L. 334, No. 94, § 5, imd. effective.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967 › Article III. Names › PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-42. Change of name of an association
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-42. Change of name of an association (2023)
content:
(a) If an association makes any change in its name the new name shall comply with
      the provisions of section 301.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967›Article II. Incorporation and Organization›PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-31. Adoption and contents of bylaws
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967 › Article II. Incorporation and Organization › PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-31. Adoption and contents of bylaws
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-31. Adoption and contents of bylaws (2023)
content:
(a) The members shall have the power to make, alter, amend and repeal the bylaws of
      an association, but such authority may be expressly vested by the articles or by the
      bylaws in the board of directors (except as to bylaws fixing the qualification, classification,
      or terms of office of directors), subject to the power of the members to change such
      action.  Unless the articles or bylaws otherwise provide, the powers hereby conferred shall
      be exercised by a majority vote of the directors or by the majority vote of members
      of the association present in person or by proxy at any regular or special meeting.  No notice shall be required to members for any regular meeting where such bylaw
      changes are to be considered.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967›Article II. Incorporation and Organization›PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-29. Certificate of authorization to do business
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967 › Article II. Incorporation and Organization › PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-29. Certificate of authorization to do business
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-29. Certificate of authorization to do business (2023)
content:
(a) Until receipt of a certificate of authorization issued by the department an association
      shall not open savings accounts for its members, incur indebtedness or transact any
      business except such business as is incident to its organization or to the obtaining
      of subscriptions.  Any officer or director violating this prohibition shall be subject to the penalty
      provisions of this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967›Article IV. Offices›PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-55. Branches acquired from the receiver of a closed association
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967 › Article IV. Offices › PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-55. Branches acquired from the receiver of a closed association
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-55. Branches acquired from the receiver of a closed association (2023)
content:
Any association whose principal place of business is located in Pennsylvania may maintain
   as a branch any office which it acquires from the secretary, or public body of the
   United States, as receiver, in conjunction with an assumption of deposit liabilities
   of a closed association whether in connection with a purchase of assets, through a
   merger or consolidation or otherwise, without regard to the location of the principal
   place of business of the acquiring association.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking›Miscellaneous Laws›Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967›Article II. Incorporation and Organization›PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-27. Issuance of certificate of incorporation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 7 P.S. Banks and Banking › Miscellaneous Laws › Chapter 51A. Savings Association Code of 1967 › Article II. Incorporation and Organization › PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-27. Issuance of certificate of incorporation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 7 P.S. § 6020-27. Issuance of certificate of incorporation (2023)
content:
If all the taxes, fees and charges required by law shall have been paid and if the
   name of the proposed association continues to be reserved or is available on the records
   of the Department of State the receipt of the articles by the Department of State
   with the written approval of the department shall constitute filing of the articles
   with the Department of State as of the date and time of receipt or as of any later
   date and time specified by the department and the Department of State shall immediately
   issue to the incorporators a certificate of incorporation as of the date and time
   of filing with the approved articles attached thereto and shall make and retain a
   copy of such certificate and articles.
