citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7601. Lost, stolen or destroyed documents of title (2023)
content:
(a) Court orders.--If a document of title is lost, stolen or destroyed, a court may order delivery of
      the goods or issuance of a substitute document, and the bailee may, without liability
      to any person, comply with the order.  If the document was negotiable, a court may not order delivery of the goods or issuance
      of a substitute document without the claimant's posting security unless it finds that
      any person that may suffer loss as a result of nonsurrender of possession or control
      of the document is adequately protected against the loss.  If the document was nonnegotiable, the court may require security.  The court may also order payment of the bailee's reasonable costs and attorney fees
      in any action under this subsection.

Warehouse Receipts and Bills of Lading: Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7602. Judicial process against goods covered by negotiable document of title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 76. Warehouse Receipts and Bills of Lading: Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7602. Judicial process against goods covered by negotiable document of title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7602. Judicial process against goods covered by negotiable document of title (2023)
content:
Unless a document of title was originally issued upon delivery of the goods by a person
   that did not have power to dispose of them, a lien does not attach by virtue of any
   judicial process to goods in the possession of a bailee for which a negotiable document
   of title is outstanding unless possession or control of the document is first surrendered
   to the bailee or the document's negotiation is enjoined.  The bailee may not be compelled to deliver the goods pursuant to process until possession
   or control of the document is surrendered to the bailee or to the court.  A purchaser of the document for value without notice of the process or injunction
   takes free of the lien imposed by judicial process.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 76. Warehouse Receipts and Bills of Lading: Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7603. Conflicting claims; interpleader
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7603. Conflicting claims; interpleader (2023)
content:
If more than one person claims title to or possession of the goods, the bailee is
   excused from delivery until the bailee has a reasonable time to ascertain the validity
   of the adverse claims or to commence an action for interpleader.  The bailee may assert an interpleader either in defending an action for nondelivery
   of the goods or by original action.

   for value of the financial asset.  A securities intermediary that acquires a security entitlement to a financial asset
   from another securities intermediary acquires the security entitlement for value if
   the securities intermediary acquiring the security entitlement establishes a security
   entitlement to the financial asset in favor of an entitlement holder.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 82. Issue and Issuer › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8203. Staleness as notice of defect or defense
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8203. Staleness as notice of defect or defense (2023)
content:
After an act or event, other than a call that has been revoked, creating a right to
   immediate performance of the principal obligation represented by a certificated security
   or setting a date on or after which the security is to be presented or surrendered
   for redemption or exchange, a purchaser is charged with notice of any defect in its

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 82. Issue and Issuer›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8202. Issuer's responsibility and defenses; notice of defect or defense
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 82. Issue and Issuer › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8202. Issuer's responsibility and defenses; notice of defect or defense
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8202. Issuer's responsibility and defenses; notice of defect or defense (2023)
content:
(a) Terms included in certificated security.--Even against a purchaser for value and without notice, the terms of a certificated
      security include terms stated on the certificate and terms made part of the security
      by reference on the certificate to another instrument, indenture or document or to
      a constitution, statute, ordinance, rule, regulation, order or the like, to the extent
      the terms referred to do not conflict with terms stated on the certificate.  A reference under this subsection does not of itself charge a purchaser for value
      with notice of a defect going to the validity of the security, even if the certificate
      expressly states that a person accepting it admits notice.  The terms of an uncertificated security include those stated in any instrument,
      indenture or document or in a constitution, statute, ordinance, rule, regulation,
      order or the like, pursuant to which the security is issued.

content:

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 82. Issue and Issuer › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8205. Effect of unauthorized signature on security certificate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8205. Effect of unauthorized signature on security certificate (2023)
content:
An unauthorized signature placed on a security certificate before or in the course
   of issue is ineffective, but the signature is effective in favor of a purchaser for
   value of the certificated security if the purchaser is without notice of the lack

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 82. Issue and Issuer›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8207. Rights and duties of issuer with respect to registered owners
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 82. Issue and Issuer › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8207. Rights and duties of issuer with respect to registered owners
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8207. Rights and duties of issuer with respect to registered owners (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Before due presentment for registration of transfer of a certificated security in
      registered form or of an instruction requesting registration of transfer of an uncertificated
      security, the issuer or indenture trustee may treat the registered owner as the person
      exclusively entitled to vote, receive notifications and otherwise exercise all the
      rights and powers of an owner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 82. Issue and Issuer›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8209. Issuer's lien
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 82. Issue and Issuer › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8209. Issuer's lien
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8209. Issuer's lien (2023)
content:
A lien in favor of an issuer upon a certificated security is valid against a purchaser
   only if the right of the issuer to the lien is noted conspicuously on the security
   certificate.

content:
(a) When owner entitled to new security.--If an owner of a certificated security, whether in registered or bearer form, claims

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 82. Issue and Issuer›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8210. Overissue
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 82. Issue and Issuer › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8210. Overissue
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8210. Overissue (2023)
content:
(a) Definition of “overissue”.--In this section,“overissue”means the issue of securities in excess of the amount the issuer has corporate power
      to issue, but an overissue does not occur if appropriate action has cured the overissue.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 83. Transfer of Certificated and Uncertificated Securities›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8303. Protected purchaser

content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 83. Transfer of Certificated and Uncertificated Securities›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8304. Indorsement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 83. Transfer of Certificated and Uncertificated Securities › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8304. Indorsement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8304. Indorsement (2023)
content:
(a) Blank and special indorsement.--An indorsement may be in blank or special.  An indorsement in blank includes an indorsement to bearer.  A special indorsement specifies to whom a security is to be transferred or who has
      power to transfer it.  A holder may convert a blank indorsement to a special indorsement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 84. Registration›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8401. Duty of issuer to register transfer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 84. Registration › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8401. Duty of issuer to register transfer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8401. Duty of issuer to register transfer (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If a certificated security in registered form is presented to an issuer with a request
      to register transfer or an instruction is presented to an issuer with a request to
      register transfer of an uncertificated security, the issuer shall register the transfer
      as requested if:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 84. Registration›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8403. Demand that issuer not register transfer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 84. Registration › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8403. Demand that issuer not register transfer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8403. Demand that issuer not register transfer (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A person who is an appropriate person to make an indorsement or originate an instruction
      may demand that the issuer not register transfer of a security by communicating to
      the issuer a notification that identifies the registered owner and the issue of which
      the security is a part and provides an address for communications directed to the
      person making the demand.  The demand is effective only if it is received by the issuer at a time and in a
      manner affording the issuer reasonable opportunity to act on it.

content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 83. Transfer of Certificated and Uncertificated Securities›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8305. Instruction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 83. Transfer of Certificated and Uncertificated Securities › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8305. Instruction

content:
(a) Instruction originated by appropriate person.--If an instruction has been originated by an appropriate person but is incomplete in
      any other respect, any person may complete it as authorized and the issuer may rely
      on it as completed, even though it has been completed incorrectly.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 83. Transfer of Certificated and Uncertificated Securities›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8307. Purchaser's right to requisites for registration of transfer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 83. Transfer of Certificated and Uncertificated Securities › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8307. Purchaser's right to requisites for registration of transfer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8307. Purchaser's right to requisites for registration of transfer (2023)
content:
Unless otherwise agreed, the transferor of a security on due demand shall supply the
   purchaser with proof of authority to transfer or with any other requisite necessary
   to obtain registration of the transfer of the security, but, if the transfer is not
   for value, a transferor need not comply unless the purchaser pays the necessary expenses.  If the transferor fails within a reasonable time to comply with the demand, the
   purchaser may reject or rescind the transfer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 84. Registration›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8404. Wrongful registration
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 84. Registration › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8404. Wrongful registration

content:

      of lost, destroyed or wrongfully taken security certificate), an issuer is liable
      for wrongful registration of transfer if the issuer has registered a transfer of a
      security to a person not entitled to it and the transfer was registered:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 84. Registration›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8406. Obligation to notify issuer of lost, destroyed or wrongfully taken security certificate
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 84. Registration › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8406. Obligation to notify issuer of lost, destroyed or wrongfully taken security certificate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8406. Obligation to notify issuer of lost, destroyed or wrongfully taken security certificate (2023)
content:
If a security certificate has been lost, apparently destroyed or wrongfully taken
   and the owner fails to notify the issuer of that fact within a reasonable time after
   the owner has notice of it and the issuer registers a transfer of the security before
   receiving notification, the owner may not assert against the issuer a claim for registering
   the transfer under section 8404 (relating to wrongful registration) or a claim to
   a new security certificate under section 8405 (relating to replacement of lost, destroyed
   or wrongfully taken security certificate).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 84. Registration›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8407. Authenticating trustee, transfer agent and registrar
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 84. Registration › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8407. Authenticating trustee, transfer agent and registrar
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8407. Authenticating trustee, transfer agent and registrar (2023)
content:
A person acting as authenticating trustee, transfer agent, registrar or other agent
   for an issuer in the registration of a transfer of its securities, in the issue of
   new security certificates or uncertificated securities or in the cancellation of surrendered
   security certificates has the same obligation to the holder or owner of a certificated
   or uncertificated security with regard to the particular functions performed as the
   issuer has in regard to those functions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 85. Security Entitlements›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8504. Duty of securities intermediary to maintain financial asset
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 85. Security Entitlements › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8504. Duty of securities intermediary to maintain financial asset
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8504. Duty of securities intermediary to maintain financial asset (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A securities intermediary shall promptly obtain and thereafter maintain a financial
      asset in a quantity corresponding to the aggregate of all security entitlements it
      has established in favor of its entitlement holders with respect to that financial
      asset.  The securities intermediary may maintain those financial assets directly or through
      one or more other securities intermediaries.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 85. Security Entitlements›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8501. Securities account; acquisition of security entitlement from securities intermediary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 85. Security Entitlements › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8501. Securities account; acquisition of security entitlement from securities intermediary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8501. Securities account; acquisition of security entitlement from securities intermediary (2023)
content:
(a) Definition of “securities account”.--“Securities account”means an account to which a financial asset is or may be credited in accordance with
      an agreement under which the person maintaining the account undertakes to treat the
      person for whom the account is maintained as entitled to exercise the rights that
      comprise the financial asset.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 85. Security Entitlements›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8506. Duty of securities intermediary to exercise rights as directed by entitlement holder
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 85. Security Entitlements › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8506. Duty of securities intermediary to exercise rights as directed by entitlement holder
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8506. Duty of securities intermediary to exercise rights as directed by entitlement holder (2023)
content:
A securities intermediary shall exercise rights with respect to a financial asset
   if directed to do so by an entitlement holder.  A securities intermediary satisfies the duty if:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 85. Security Entitlements›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8502. Assertion of adverse claim against entitlement holder
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 85. Security Entitlements › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8502. Assertion of adverse claim against entitlement holder
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8502. Assertion of adverse claim against entitlement holder (2023)
content:
An action based on an adverse claim to a financial asset, whether framed in conversion,
   replevin, constructive trust, equitable lien or other theory, may not be asserted
   against a person who acquires a security entitlement under section 8501 (relating
   to securities account;  acquisition of security entitlement from securities intermediary)
   for value and without notice of the adverse claim.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 85. Security Entitlements›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8503. Property interest of entitlement holder in financial asset held by securities intermediary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 85. Security Entitlements › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8503. Property interest of entitlement holder in financial asset held by securities intermediary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8503. Property interest of entitlement holder in financial asset held by securities intermediary (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--To the extent necessary for a securities intermediary to satisfy all security entitlements
      with respect to a particular financial asset, all interests in that financial asset
      held by the securities intermediary are held by the securities intermediary for the
      entitlement holders, are not property of the securities intermediary and are not subject
      to claims of creditors of the securities intermediary, except as otherwise provided
      in section 8511 (relating to priority among security interests and entitlement holders).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 85. Security Entitlements›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8511. Priority among security interests and entitlement holders
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 85. Security Entitlements › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8511. Priority among security interests and entitlement holders
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8511. Priority among security interests and entitlement holders (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided in subsections (b) and (c), if a securities intermediary
      does not have sufficient interests in a particular financial asset to satisfy both
      its obligations to entitlement holders who have security entitlements to that financial
      asset and its obligation to a creditor of the securities intermediary who has a security
      interest in that financial asset, the claims of entitlement holders other than the
      creditor have priority over the claim of the creditor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 91. General Provisions›Subchapter A. Short Title, Definitions and General Concepts›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9101. Short title of division
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 91. General Provisions › Subchapter A. Short Title, Definitions and General Concepts › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9101. Short title of division
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9101. Short title of division (2023)
content:
This division shall be known and may be cited as the Uniform Commercial Code, Division
   9, Secured Transactions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 85. Security Entitlements›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8509. Specification of duties of securities intermediary by other statute or regulation; manner of performance of duties of securities intermediary and exercise of rights of entitlement holder
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 85. Security Entitlements › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8509. Specification of duties of securities intermediary by other statute or regulation; manner of performance of duties of securities intermediary and exercise of rights of entitlement holder
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8509. Specification of duties of securities intermediary by other statute or regulation; manner of performance of duties of securities intermediary and exercise of rights of entitlement holder (2023)
content:
(a) Compliance with statute, etc., satisfies duty.--If the substance of a duty imposed upon a securities intermediary by sections 8504
      (relating to duty of securities intermediary to maintain financial asset) through
      8508 (relating to duty of securities intermediary to change entitlement holder's position
      to other form of security holding) is the subject of another statute, regulation or
      rule, compliance with that statute, regulation or rule satisfies the duty.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 85. Security Entitlements›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8507. Duty of securities intermediary to comply with entitlement order
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 85. Security Entitlements › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8507. Duty of securities intermediary to comply with entitlement order
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8507. Duty of securities intermediary to comply with entitlement order (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A securities intermediary shall comply with an entitlement order if the entitlement
      order is originated by the appropriate person, the securities intermediary has had
      reasonable opportunity to assure itself that the entitlement order is genuine and
      authorized and the securities intermediary has had reasonable opportunity to comply
      with the entitlement order.  A securities intermediary satisfies the duty if:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 85. Security Entitlements›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8505. Duty of securities intermediary with respect to payments and distributions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 85. Security Entitlements › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8505. Duty of securities intermediary with respect to payments and distributions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8505. Duty of securities intermediary with respect to payments and distributions (2023)
content:
(a) Duty of securities intermediary to obtain payment or distribution.--A securities intermediary shall take action to obtain a payment or distribution made
      by the issuer of a financial asset.  A securities intermediary satisfies the duty if:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 85. Security Entitlements›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8508. Duty of securities intermediary to change entitlement holder's position to other form of security holding
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 85. Security Entitlements › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8508. Duty of securities intermediary to change entitlement holder's position to other form of security holding
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8508. Duty of securities intermediary to change entitlement holder's position to other form of security holding (2023)
content:
A securities intermediary shall act at the direction of an entitlement holder to change
   a security entitlement into another available form of holding for which the entitlement

content:

content:
(a) General rule;  location of debtor.--Except as otherwise provided in this section, while a debtor is located in a jurisdiction,
      the local law of that jurisdiction governs perfection, the effect of perfection or
      nonperfection and the priority of a security interest in collateral.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9303. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in goods covered by certificate of title (2023)
content:
(a) Applicability of section.--This section applies to goods covered by a certificate of title even if there is no
      other relationship between the jurisdiction under whose certificate of title the goods
      are covered and the goods or the debtor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter B. Perfection›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9313. When possession by or delivery to secured party perfects security interest without filing
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority › Subchapter B. Perfection › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9313. When possession by or delivery to secured party perfects security interest without filing
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9313. When possession by or delivery to secured party perfects security interest without filing (2023)
content:
(a) Perfection by possession or delivery.--Except as otherwise provided in subsection (b), a secured party may perfect a security
      interest in goods, instruments, negotiable tangible documents or money by taking possession
      of the collateral.  A secured party may perfect a security interest in certificated securities by taking
      delivery under section 8301 (relating to delivery).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9302. Law governing perfection and priority of agricultural liens

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9302. Law governing perfection and priority of agricultural liens (2023)
content:
While farm products are located in a jurisdiction, the local law of that jurisdiction
   governs perfection, the effect of perfection or nonperfection and the priority of
   an agricultural lien on the farm products.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9304. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in deposit accounts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority › Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9304. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in deposit accounts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9304. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in deposit accounts (2023)
content:
(a) Law of bank's jurisdiction governs.--The local law of a bank's jurisdiction governs perfection, the effect of perfection
      or nonperfection and the priority of a security interest in a deposit account maintained
      with that bank even if the transaction does not bear any relation to the bank's jurisdiction.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9306.1. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in chattel paper

Law Governing Perfection and Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9306.1. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in chattel paper
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9306.1. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in chattel paper (2023)
content:
(a) Chattel paper evidenced by authoritative electronic copy.--Except as provided in subsection (d), if chattel paper is evidenced only by an authoritative
      electronic copy of the chattel paper or is evidenced by an authoritative electronic
      copy and an authoritative tangible copy, the local law of the chattel paper's jurisdiction
      governs perfection, the effect of perfection or nonperfection and the priority of
      a security interest in the chattel paper, even if the transaction does not bear any
      relation to the chattel paper's jurisdiction.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9306. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in letter-of-credit rights

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9306. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in letter-of-credit rights (2023)
content:
(a) Governing law;  issuer's or nominated person's jurisdiction.--Subject to subsection (c), the local law of the issuer's jurisdiction or a nominated
      person's jurisdiction governs perfection, the effect of perfection or nonperfection
      and the priority of a security interest in a letter-of-credit right if the issuer's
      jurisdiction or nominated person's jurisdiction is a state.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9307. Location of debtor (2023)
content: (a) Place of business.--As used in this section, the term“place of business”means a place where a debtor conducts its affairs.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority › Subchapter B. Perfection › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9308. When security interest or agricultural lien is perfected; continuity of perfection
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9308. When security interest or agricultural lien is perfected; continuity of perfection (2023)
content:
(a) Perfection of security interest.--Except as otherwise provided in this section and section 9309 (relating to security
      interest perfected upon attachment), a security interest is perfected if it has attached
      and all of the applicable requirements for perfection in sections 9310 (relating to
      when filing required to perfect security interest or agricultural lien;  security
      interests and agricultural liens to which filing provisions do not apply) through
      9316 (relating to effect of change in governing law) have been satisfied.  A security interest is perfected when it attaches if the applicable requirements
      are satisfied before the security interest attaches.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9312. Perfection of security interests in chattel paper, controllable accounts, controllable electronic records, controllable payment intangibles, deposit accounts, documents, goods covered by documents, instruments, investment property, letter-of-credit rights and money; perfection by permissive filing; temporary perfection without filing or transfer of possession (2023)
content:
(a) Perfection by filing permitted.--A security interest in chattel paper, controllable accounts, controllable electronic
      records, controllable payment intangibles, instruments, investment property or negotiable
      documents may be perfected by filing.

content:

Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in controllable accounts, controllable electronic records and controllable payment intangibles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority › Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9306.2. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in controllable accounts, controllable electronic records and controllable payment intangibles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9306.2. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in controllable accounts, controllable electronic records and controllable payment intangibles (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as provided in subsection (b), the local law of the controllable electronic
      record's jurisdiction specified in section 12107(c) and (d) (relating to governing
      law) governs perfection, the effect of perfection or nonperfection and the priority
      of a security interest in a controllable electronic record and a security interest
      in a controllable account or controllable payment intangible evidenced by the controllable
      electronic record.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter B. Perfection›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9310. citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9310. When filing required to perfect security interest or agricultural lien; security interests and agricultural liens to which filing provisions do not apply (2023)
content:
(a) General rule:  perfection by filing.--Except as otherwise provided in subsection (b) and section 9312(b) (relating to perfection
      of security interests in chattel paper, controllable accounts, controllable electronic
      records, controllable payment intangibles, deposit accounts, documents, goods covered
      by documents, instruments, investment property, letter-of-credit rights and money;
      perfection by permissive filing;  temporary perfection without filing or transfer
      of possession), a financing statement must be filed to perfect all security interests
      and agricultural liens.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter B. Perfection›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9314. Perfection by control

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9314. Perfection by control (2023)
content:
(a) Perfection by control.--A security interest in controllable accounts, controllable electronic records, controllable
      payment intangibles, deposit accounts, electronic documents, investment property or
      letter-of-credit rights may be perfected by control of the collateral under section
      7106 (relating to control of electronic document of title), 9104 (relating to control
      of deposit account), 9106 (relating to control of investment property), 9107 (relating
      to control of letter-of-credit right) or 9107.1 (relating to control of controllable
      electronic record, controllable account or controllable payment intangible).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter B. Perfection›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9314.1. Perfection by possession and control of chattel paper
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority › Subchapter B. Perfection › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9314.1. Perfection by possession and control of chattel paper
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9314.1. Perfection by possession and control of chattel paper (2023)
content:
(a) Perfection by possession and control.--A secured party may perfect a security interest in chattel paper by taking possession
      of each authoritative tangible copy of the record evidencing the chattel paper and
      obtaining control of each authoritative electronic copy of the electronic record evidencing
      the chattel paper.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority › Subchapter C. Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9318. No interest retained in right to payment which is sold; rights and title of seller of account or chattel paper with respect to creditors and purchasers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9318. No interest retained in right to payment which is sold; rights and title of seller of account or chattel paper with respect to creditors and purchasers (2023)
content:
(a) Seller retains no interest.--A debtor that has sold an account, chattel paper, payment intangible or promissory
      note does not retain a legal or equitable interest in the collateral sold.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter C. Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9320. Buyer of goods
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority › Subchapter C. Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9320. Buyer of goods
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9320. Buyer of goods (2023)
content:
(a) Buyer in ordinary course of business.--Except as otherwise provided in subsection (e), a buyer in ordinary course of business,
      other than a person buying farm products from a person engaged in farming operations,
      takes free of a security interest created by the buyer's seller, even if the security
      interest is perfected and the buyer knows of its existence.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter C. Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9319. Rights and title of consignee with respect to creditors and purchasers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority › Subchapter C. Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9319. Rights and title of consignee with respect to creditors and purchasers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9319. Rights and title of consignee with respect to creditors and purchasers (2023)
content:
(a) Consignee has consignor's rights.--Except as otherwise provided in subsection (b), for purposes of determining the rights
      of creditors of and purchasers for value of goods from a consignee, while the goods
      are in the possession of the consignee, the consignee is deemed to have rights and
      title to the goods identical to those the consignor had or had power to transfer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter C. Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9324. Priority of purchase-money security interests
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority › Subchapter C. Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9324. Priority of purchase-money security interests
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9324. Priority of purchase-money security interests (2023)
content:
(a) General rule:  purchase-money priority.--Except as otherwise provided in subsection (g), a perfected purchase-money security
      interest in goods other than inventory or livestock has priority over a conflicting
      security interest in the same goods, and, except as otherwise provided in section
      9327 (relating to priority of security interests in deposit account), a perfected
      security interest in its identifiable proceeds also has priority if the purchase-money
      security interest is perfected when the debtor receives possession of the collateral
      or within 20 days thereafter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter C. Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9321. Licensee of general intangible and lessee of goods in ordinary course of business
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority › Subchapter C. Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9321. Licensee of general intangible and lessee of goods in ordinary course of business
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9321. Licensee of general intangible and lessee of goods in ordinary course of business (2023)
content:
(a) Licensee in ordinary course of business.--As used in this section, the term“licensee in ordinary course of business”means a person that becomes a licensee of a general intangible in good faith, without
      knowledge that the license violates the rights of another person in the general intangible,
      and in the ordinary course from a person in the business of licensing general intangibles
      of that kind.  A person becomes a licensee in the ordinary course if the license to the person
      comports with the usual or customary practices in the kind of business in which the
      licensor is engaged or with the licensor's own usual or customary practices.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority › Subchapter C. Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9326.1. Priority of security interest in controllable account, controllable electronic record and controllable payment intangible
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9326.1. Priority of security interest in controllable account, controllable electronic record and controllable payment intangible (2023)
content:
A security interest in a controllable account, controllable electronic record or controllable
   payment intangible held by a secured party having control of the account, electronic
   record or payment intangible has priority over a conflicting security interest held
   by a secured party that does not have control.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter C. Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9326. Priority of security interests created by new debtor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority › Subchapter C. Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9326. Priority of security interests created by new debtor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9326. Priority of security interests created by new debtor (2023)
content:
(a) Subordination of security interest created by new debtor.--Subject to subsection (b), a security interest that is created by a new debtor in
      collateral in which the new debtor has or acquires rights and is perfected solely
      by a filed financing statement which would be ineffective to perfect the security
      interest but for the application of section 9316(i)(1) (relating to effect of change
      in governing law) or 9508 (relating to effectiveness of financing statement if new
      debtor becomes bound by security agreement) is subordinate to a security interest
      in the same collateral which is perfected other than by such a filed financing statement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter C. Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9330. Priority of purchaser of chattel paper or instrument

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9301. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9301. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9301. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests (2023)
content:
(a) General rule;  location of debtor.--Except as otherwise provided in this section, while a debtor is located in a jurisdiction,
      the local law of that jurisdiction governs perfection, the effect of perfection or
      nonperfection and the priority of a security interest in collateral.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter C. Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9332. Transfer of money; transfer of funds from deposit account
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority › Subchapter C. Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9332. Transfer of money; transfer of funds from deposit account
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9332. Transfer of money; transfer of funds from deposit account (2023)
content:
(a) Transferee of money.--A transferee of money takes the money free of a security interest if the transferee
      receives possession of the money without acting in collusion with the debtor in violating
      the rights of the secured party.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9302. Law governing perfection and priority of agricultural liens
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9302. Law governing perfection and priority of agricultural liens
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9302. Law governing perfection and priority of agricultural liens (2023)
content:
While farm products are located in a jurisdiction, the local law of that jurisdiction
   governs perfection, the effect of perfection or nonperfection and the priority of
   an agricultural lien on the farm products.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9303. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in goods covered by certificate of title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9303. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in goods covered by certificate of title (2023)
content:
(a) Applicability of section.--This section applies to goods covered by a certificate of title even if there is no
      other relationship between the jurisdiction under whose certificate of title the goods
      are covered and the goods or the debtor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9306. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in letter-of-credit rights
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9306. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in letter-of-credit rights
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9306. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in letter-of-credit rights (2023)
content:
(a) Governing law;  issuer's or nominated person's jurisdiction.--Subject to subsection (c), the local law of the issuer's jurisdiction or a nominated
      person's jurisdiction governs perfection, the effect of perfection or nonperfection
      and the priority of a security interest in a letter-of-credit right if the issuer's
      jurisdiction or nominated person's jurisdiction is a state.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9304. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in deposit accounts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9304. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in deposit accounts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9304. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in deposit accounts (2023)
content:
(a) Law of bank's jurisdiction governs.--The local law of a bank's jurisdiction governs perfection, the effect of perfection
      or nonperfection and the priority of a security interest in a deposit account maintained
      with that bank even if the transaction does not bear any relation to the bank's jurisdiction.

content: (a) Governing law;  general rules.--Except as otherwise provided in subsection (c), the following rules apply:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter C. Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9334. Priority of security interests in fixtures and crops
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority › Subchapter C. Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9334. Priority of security interests in fixtures and crops
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9334. Priority of security interests in fixtures and crops (2023)
content:
(a) Security interest in fixtures under this division.--A security interest under this division may be created in goods which are fixtures
      or may continue in goods which become fixtures.  A security interest does not exist under this division in ordinary building materials
      incorporated into an improvement on land.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter C. Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9331. Priority of rights of purchasers of controllable accounts, controllable electronic records, controllable payment intangibles, documents, instruments and securities under other divisions; priority of interests in financial assets and security entitlements and protection against assertion of claim under Divisions 8 and 12
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority › Subchapter C. Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9331. Priority of rights of purchasers of controllable accounts, controllable electronic records, controllable payment intangibles, documents, instruments and securities under other divisions; priority of interests in financial assets and security entitlements and protection against assertion of claim under Divisions 8 and 12
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9331. Priority of rights of purchasers of controllable accounts, controllable electronic records, controllable payment intangibles, documents, instruments and securities under other divisions; priority of interests in financial assets and security entitlements and protection against assertion of claim under Divisions 8 and 12 (2023)
content:
(a) Rights under Divisions 3, 7, 8 and 12 not limited.--This division does not limit the rights of a holder in due course of a negotiable
      instrument, a holder to which a negotiable document of title has been duly negotiated,
      a protected purchaser of a security or a qualifying purchaser of a controllable account,
      controllable electronic record or controllable payment intangible.  These holders or purchasers take priority over an earlier security interest, even
      if perfected, to the extent provided in Divisions 3 (relating to negotiable instruments),
      7 (relating to warehouse receipts, bills of lading and other documents of title),
      8 (relating to investment securities) and 12 (relating to controllable electronic
      records).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9306.1. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in chattel paper
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9306.1. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in chattel paper
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9306.1. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in chattel paper (2023)
content:
(a) Chattel paper evidenced by authoritative electronic copy.--Except as provided in subsection (d), if chattel paper is evidenced only by an authoritative
      electronic copy of the chattel paper or is evidenced by an authoritative electronic
      copy and an authoritative tangible copy, the local law of the chattel paper's jurisdiction
      governs perfection, the effect of perfection or nonperfection and the priority of
      a security interest in the chattel paper, even if the transaction does not bear any
      relation to the chattel paper's jurisdiction.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter C. Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9335. Accessions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority › Subchapter C. Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9335. Accessions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9335. Accessions (2023)
content:
(a) Creation of security interest in accession.--A security interest may be created in an accession and continues in collateral which
      becomes an accession.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9306.2. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in controllable accounts, controllable electronic records and controllable payment intangibles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9306.2. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in controllable accounts, controllable electronic records and controllable payment intangibles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9306.2. Law governing perfection and priority of security interests in controllable accounts, controllable electronic records and controllable payment intangibles (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as provided in subsection (b), the local law of the controllable electronic
      record's jurisdiction specified in section 12107(c) and (d) (relating to governing
      law) governs perfection, the effect of perfection or nonperfection and the priority
      of a security interest in a controllable electronic record and a security interest
      in a controllable account or controllable payment intangible evidenced by the controllable
      electronic record.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9307. Location of debtor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Subchapter A. Law Governing Perfection and Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9307. Location of debtor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9307. Location of debtor (2023)
content: (a) Place of business.--As used in this section, the term“place of business”means a place where a debtor conducts its affairs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter C. Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9339. Priority subject to subordination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority › Subchapter C. Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9339. Priority subject to subordination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9339. Priority subject to subordination (2023)
content:
This division does not preclude subordination by agreement by a person entitled to
   priority.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter C. Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9337. Priority of security interests in goods covered by certificate of title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority › Subchapter C. Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9337. Priority of security interests in goods covered by certificate of title

content:
If, while a security interest in goods is perfected by any method under the law of
   another jurisdiction, the Commonwealth issues a certificate of title which does not
   show that the goods are subject to the security interest or contain a statement that
   they may be subject to security interests not shown on the certificate:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter C. Priority›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9338. Priority of security interest or agricultural lien perfected by filed financing statement providing certain incorrect information
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority › Subchapter C. Priority › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9338. Priority of security interest or agricultural lien perfected by filed financing statement providing certain incorrect information
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9338. Priority of security interest or agricultural lien perfected by filed financing statement providing certain incorrect information (2023)
content:
If a security interest or agricultural lien is perfected by a filed financing statement
   providing information described in section 9516(b)(5) (relating to what constitutes
   filing;  effectiveness of filing) which is incorrect at the time the financing statement
   is filed:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 93. Perfection and Priority›Subchapter D. Rights of Bank›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9342. Bank's right to refuse to enter into or disclose existence of control agreement

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9342. Bank's right to refuse to enter into or disclose existence of control agreement (2023)
content:
This division does not require a bank to enter into an agreement of the kind described
   in section 9104(a)(2) (relating to requirements for control) even if its customer
   so requests or directs.  A bank which has entered into such an agreement is not required to confirm the existence
   of the agreement to another person unless requested to do so by its customer.

      interest in property, even if the transaction, lien or interest was entered into,
      created or acquired before the effective date of this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 91. Transitional Provisions›Chapter 911. Transitional Provisions for 2022 Amendments›Subchapter B. General Transitional Provision›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 91121. Savings clause

   interests flowing from the transaction remain valid thereafter and may be terminated,
   completed, consummated or enforced as required or permitted by law other than this
   title or, if applicable, this title, as though this section had not taken effect.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 91. Transitional Provisions›Chapter 911. Transitional Provisions for 2022 Amendments›Subchapter C. Transitional Provisions for Divisions 9 and 12›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 91134. Effectiveness of actions taken before effective date

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 91134. Effectiveness of actions taken before effective date (2023)
content:
(a) Pre-effective-date action;  attachment and perfection before adjustment date.--If action, other than the filing of a financing statement, is taken before the effective
      date of this section and the action would have resulted in perfection of the security
      interest had the security interest become enforceable before the effective date of
      this section, the action is effective to perfect a security interest that attaches
      under the act adding this chapter before the adjustment date.  An attached security interest becomes unperfected on the adjustment date unless
      the security interest becomes a perfected security interest under the act adding this
      chapter before the adjustment date.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 P.S. Constables›Chapter 6. Compensation and Fees›PA ST 13 P.S. § 74. Return of subpoenas; limitation on mileage cost
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 P.S. Constables › Chapter 6. Compensation and Fees › PA ST 13 P.S. § 74. Return of subpoenas; limitation on mileage cost
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 P.S. § 74. Return of subpoenas; limitation on mileage cost (2023)
content:
Whenever the officer or individual who has served subpoenas issued by the district
   attorney for any term of court shall make return thereof as required by law, he shall
   be required to return all subpoenas, received within a reasonable time prior to such
   return day, at one and the same time;  and in making such return of subpoenas he shall
   receive mileage only for trips actually and necessarily made in returning such subpoenas
   and not mileage on each separate subpoena returned.  In order to carry into effect the provisions of this section, the district attorney
   in issuing subpoenas shall, so far as conveniently may be, mail or cause to be delivered
   subpoenas going to the same officer or individual for a term of court at one and the
   same time.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 P.S. Constables›Chapter 4. Duties and Liabilities›PA ST 13 P.S. § 46. Actions for violation of ordinances; practice
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 P.S. Constables › Chapter 4. Duties and Liabilities › PA ST 13 P.S. § 46. Actions for violation of ordinances; practice
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 P.S. § 46. Actions for violation of ordinances; practice (2023)
content:
All actions, prosecutions, complaints and proceedings for the violation of borough
   ordinances, and for the collection of fines and penalties imposed thereby, may be
   commenced by warrant or by summons at the discretion of the chief burgess or justice
   of the peace1before whom the complaint is made or the proceedings begun, but no warrant shall
   be issued except upon complaint, on oath or affirmation, specifying the ordinance
   for the violation of which the same is issued, and all proceedings shall be directed
   to and be served by any policeman or constable of said borough, who shall execute
   the same anywhere within the borough, or in the county of which it is a part, or elsewhere
   in the state, as may be provided by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 P.S. Constables›Chapter 4. Duties and Liabilities›PA ST 13 P.S. § 40. Peace officers; powers and duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 P.S. Constables › Chapter 4. Duties and Liabilities › PA ST 13 P.S. § 40. Peace officers; powers and duties

Constables, county detectives, sheriffs, deputy sheriffs, waterways patrolmen and

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 P.S. Constables›Chapter 6. Compensation and Fees›PA ST 13 P.S. § 75. Approval of bills for services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 P.S. Constables › Chapter 6. Compensation and Fees › PA ST 13 P.S. § 75. Approval of bills for services

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 15 Pa.C.S.A. Corporations and Unincorporated Associations›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 1. General Provisions›Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 103. Subordination of title to regulatory laws
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 15 Pa.C.S.A. Corporations and Unincorporated Associations › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 1. General Provisions › Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 103. Subordination of title to regulatory laws
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 103. Subordination of title to regulatory laws (2023)
content:
(a) Regulatory laws unaffected.--This title is not intended to authorize any corporation or other association to do
      any act prohibited by any statute regulating the business of the association or by
      any rule or regulation validly promulgated thereunder by any department, board or
      commission of this Commonwealth.  Except as otherwise provided by the statutes and prescribed by the rules and regulations
      promulgated thereunder applicable to the business of the association, the issuance
      by the Department of State of any certificate evidencing the incorporation of a corporation
      or the filing of an instrument with respect to or the organization or qualification
      of an association under this title or any amendment to its articles or certificate
      or other change in its status or other action under this title shall not be effective
      to exempt the association from any of the requirements of those statutes or rules
      and regulations.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 15 Pa.C.S.A. Corporations and Unincorporated Associations›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 1. General Provisions›Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 104. Equitable remedies

content:
Except to the extent otherwise provided in this title in cases where a statutory remedy
   is provided by this title, the court shall have the powers of a court of equity or
   chancery insofar as those powers relate to the supervision and control of corporations
   and other associations.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 15 Pa.C.S.A. Corporations and Unincorporated Associations›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 1. General Provisions›Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 106. Effect of filing papers required to be filed
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 15 Pa.C.S.A. Corporations and Unincorporated Associations › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 1. General Provisions › Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 106. Effect of filing papers required to be filed

content:

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 110. Supplementary general principles of law applicable (2023)
content:
Unless displaced by the particular provisions of this title, the principles of law
   and equity, including, but not limited to, the law relating to principal and agent,
   estoppel, waiver, fraud, misrepresentation, duress, coercion, mistake, bankruptcy
   or other validating or invalidating cause, shall supplement its provisions.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 114. Defense of usury (2023)
content:
A domestic association other than a business corporation shall be subject to section
   1510 (relating to certain specifically authorized debt terms) with respect to obligations,
   as defined in that section, governed by the laws of this Commonwealth or affecting
   real property situated in this Commonwealth, to the same extent as if the domestic
   association were a domestic business corporation.

      file the document, certify that the document has been filed by endorsing upon the

content:
(a) General rule.--The function of the Department of State under this title is to act in a manner comparable
      to the offices of recorder of deeds under former provisions of law as an office of
      public record wherein articles and other papers relating to association affairs may
      be filed to establish the permanent and definitive text thereof and to afford all
      persons the opportunity of acquiring knowledge of the contents thereof.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 15 Pa.C.S.A. Corporations and Unincorporated Associations › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 1. General Provisions › Subchapter B. Functions and Powers of Department of State › PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 137. Court to pass upon rejection of documents by Department of State
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 137. Court to pass upon rejection of documents by Department of State (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Whenever the Department of State rejects a document delivered for filing under this
      title, the original document or a copy thereof and any papers relating thereto may
      be delivered to the prothonotary or clerk of the court vested by or pursuant to Title
      42 (relating to judiciary and judicial procedure) with jurisdiction of appeals from
      the department.  Immediately the prothonotary or clerk shall transmit the papers to the court without
      formality or expense to the person who delivered the original document to the department.  The question of the eligibility of the document for filing by the department shall
      thereupon, at the earliest possible time, be heard by a judge of the court, without
      jury, in the court or in chambers.  The finding of the court, or any judge thereof, that the document is eligible for
      filing by the department shall be final and the department shall act in accordance
      therewith.  The true intent of this section is to secure for applicants an immediate hearing
      in court and a determination by the court without delay or expense to the applicants.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 140. Custody and management of orphan corporate and business records (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Any orphan corporate and business record under the custody or control of a county,
      including the City and County of Philadelphia, may become a Commonwealth record in
      the manner provided in this section.  The Department of State, with the concurrence of the county records committee existing
      under the act of August 14, 1963 (P.L. 839, No. 407),1may provide for the transfer on a progressive and phased basis to the custody and
      management of the department of any or all orphan corporate and business records.  To the extent feasible, such records shall be integrated with records of the department
      relating to the same type of matters or transactions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 15 Pa.C.S.A. Corporations and Unincorporated Associations›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 103. Subordination of title to regulatory laws
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 15 Pa.C.S.A. Corporations and Unincorporated Associations › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 103. Subordination of title to regulatory laws
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 103. Subordination of title to regulatory laws (2023)
content:
(a) Regulatory laws unaffected.--This title is not intended to authorize any corporation or other association to do
      any act prohibited by any statute regulating the business of the association or by
      any rule or regulation validly promulgated thereunder by any department, board or
      commission of this Commonwealth.  Except as otherwise provided by the statutes and prescribed by the rules and regulations
      promulgated thereunder applicable to the business of the association, the issuance
      by the Department of State of any certificate evidencing the incorporation of a corporation
      or the filing of an instrument with respect to or the organization or qualification
      of an association under this title or any amendment to its articles or certificate
      or other change in its status or other action under this title shall not be effective
      to exempt the association from any of the requirements of those statutes or rules
      and regulations.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 143. Liability for inaccurate information in filing (2023)
content:
If a document that is delivered to the department for filing under this title and
   filed by the department contains inaccurate information at the time of delivery to
   the department, a person that suffers a loss by reliance on the information may recover
   damages for the loss from a person that signed the document or caused another to sign
   it on behalf of the person and knew at the time the document was delivered that the
   information was inaccurate.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 114. Defense of usury (2023)
content:
A domestic association other than a business corporation shall be subject to section
   1510 (relating to certain specifically authorized debt terms) with respect to obligations,
   as defined in that section, governed by the laws of this Commonwealth or affecting

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 15 Pa.C.S.A. Corporations and Unincorporated Associations › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Subchapter B. Functions and Powers of Department of State › PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 132. Functions of Department of State
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 132. Functions of Department of State (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The function of the Department of State under this title is to act in a manner comparable
      to the offices of recorder of deeds under former provisions of law as an office of
      public record wherein articles and other papers relating to association affairs may
      be filed to establish the permanent and definitive text thereof and to afford all
      persons the opportunity of acquiring knowledge of the contents thereof.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 15 Pa.C.S.A. Corporations and Unincorporated Associations›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Subchapter B. Functions and Powers of Department of State›PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 137. Court to pass upon rejection of documents by Department of State
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 15 Pa.C.S.A. Corporations and Unincorporated Associations › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Subchapter B. Functions and Powers of Department of State › PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 137. Court to pass upon rejection of documents by Department of State
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 15 Pa.C.S.A. § 137. Court to pass upon rejection of documents by Department of State (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Whenever the Department of State rejects a document delivered for filing under this
      title, the original document or a copy thereof and any papers relating thereto may
      be delivered to the prothonotary or clerk of the court vested by or pursuant to Title
      42 (relating to judiciary and judicial procedure) with jurisdiction of appeals from
      the department.  Immediately the prothonotary or clerk shall transmit the papers to the court without
      formality or expense to the person who delivered the original document to the department.  The question of the eligibility of the document for filing by the department shall
      thereupon, at the earliest possible time, be heard by a judge of the court, without
      jury, in the court or in chambers.  The finding of the court, or any judge thereof, that the document is eligible for
      filing by the department shall be final and the department shall act in accordance
      therewith.  The true intent of this section is to secure for applicants an immediate hearing
      in court and a determination by the court without delay or expense to the applicants.
