citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.5. Manner of making appointments (2023)
content:
Every position of employment, unless filled by promotion or reinstatement, shall be
   filled only in the following manner:  The sheriff of the county shall notify the commission
   of any vacancy in the force of deputy sheriffs which is to be filled and shall request
   certification of a list of eligibles.  The commission shall certify to the sheriff all those eligible from the last preceding
   examination held within a period of three years next preceding the date of the request
   for such eligibles.  The sheriff of the county shall thereupon make an appointment from the eligible
   list certified to him.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.12. Present employes exempted
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.12. Present employes exempted
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.12. Present employes exempted (2023)
content:
(a) All members of the force of deputy sheriffs upon the effective date of this act
      shall continue to hold their positions and shall not be required to take any examination
      whatsoever under this act except such as may be required for subsequent promotion.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.8. Promotions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.8. Promotions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.8. Promotions (2023)
content:
Promotions shall be based on merit to be ascertained by examinations to be prescribed
   by the sheriff and the commission.  All questions relative to promotions shall be practical in character and such as
   will fairly test the merit and fitness of persons seeking promotion.  The sheriff of the county shall have the discretion to promote the person or persons
   of his choice from the list of those who have successfully completed the appropriate
   examination and are certified as eligible for promotion by the commission.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.11. Reduction in number of deputy sheriffs; reinstatements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.11. Reduction in number of deputy sheriffs; reinstatements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.11. Reduction in number of deputy sheriffs; reinstatements (2023)
content:
If for reasons of economy or otherwise, it shall be deemed necessary by the sheriff
   of the county to reduce the number of deputy sheriffs then such reduction in numbers
   shall be made in the following manner:  (i) if there are any deputy sheriffs eligible
   for retirement under the terms of any retirement or pension system or law, then such
   reduction in numbers shall be made by retirement, if the party to be retired has served
   in the force of deputy sheriffs for a period of at least twenty-five years and his
   age exceeds the maximum age as defined in the act of October 27, 1955 (P.L. 744, No.
   222),1known as the “Pennsylvania Human Relations Act”,  (ii) if the number of deputy sheriffs
   eligible for retirement is insufficient to effect the reduction in numbers decided
   upon by the sheriff of the county, or if no retirement or pension system or law exists,
   or if there are no deputy sheriffs eligible for retirement or pension, then the reduction
   shall be made by furloughing the last deputy sheriff including the probationers that
   have been appointed to the force and continue in numerical order until the reduction
   decided upon by the sheriff of the county has been affected.  In any case where there has been more than one employe appointed at the same time
   then such furloughing shall be determined by the alphabetical order of the first letter
   of their surname.  In the event the said force of deputy sheriffs shall again be increased in numbers
   then the employes furloughed shall be reinstated in the inverse order of that in which
   they were furloughed before any new appointments shall be made to the deputy sheriffs'
   force.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.10. Reducing in rank; suspension; furloughing; discharging
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.10. Reducing in rank; suspension; furloughing; discharging
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.10. Reducing in rank; suspension; furloughing; discharging (2023)
content:
(a) No deputy sheriff covered by this act shall be reduced in rank, suspended, furloughed
      or discharged, except for the following reasons:  (i) neglect or violation of official
      duty, (ii) violation of a law of this Commonwealth which provides that such violation
      constitutes a misdemeanor or a felony, (iii) inefficiency, except as hereinafter provided,
      wilful disobedience of orders, or conduct unbecoming a police officer, (iv) drinking
      of intoxicating liquor while on duty or the use of which renders him unfit when called
      upon for duty.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.15. Compensation and expenses to deputy sheriff injured or ill
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.15. Compensation and expenses to deputy sheriff injured or ill
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.15. Compensation and expenses to deputy sheriff injured or ill (2023)
content:
After the effective date of this act any member of the force of deputy sheriffs of
   all ranks, including chief deputy, who may be injured or become sick through the performance
   of his duties and by reason thereof is temporarily incapacitated from performing his
   duties, shall be paid by the county his full rate of salary as fixed by the salary
   board until the disability arising therefrom has ceased.  All medical and hospital bills incurred in connection with any such injury or sickness
   shall be paid by the county.  All benefits under the Workmen's Compensation Law which shall be reviewed or collected
   by any such member during the period he has received salary for temporary disability
   shall be paid over to the county and paid into the treasury thereof.  If any such payment or payments shall not be so made by the member of the force,
   the amount so directed to be paid to the county shall be deducted from any salary
   which shall then or thereafter become due and owing to such member.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.9. Physical examinations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.9. Physical examinations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.9. Physical examinations (2023)
content:
All applicants for examination shall undergo a physical examination, which shall be
   conducted under the supervision of a doctor of medicine appointed by the sheriff of
   the county.  No person shall be eligible to take an examination until said doctor certifies to
   the commission that the applicant is free from any bodily or mental defects, deformity
   or disease that might incapacitate him from the discharge of the duties of a deputy
   sheriff.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.13. Discrimination on account of religious or political affiliations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.13. Discrimination on account of religious or political affiliations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.13. Discrimination on account of religious or political affiliations (2023)
content:
No question in any form of application for any examination or in any examination shall
   be so framed as to elicit information concerning the religious or political opinions
   of any applicant, nor shall inquiry be made concerning such opinions or affiliations
   and all such disclosures thereof shall be discountenanced.  No discrimination shall be exercised, threatened or promised by any person in or
   interested in the force of deputy sheriffs against or in favor of an applicant on
   the eligible list for appointment to or promotion in the force because of his religious
   or political opinions or affiliations.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.14. Hours of service; exceptions; vacations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.14. Hours of service; exceptions; vacations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.14. Hours of service; exceptions; vacations (2023)
content:
Every member of the force of deputy sheriffs shall have at least twenty-four consecutive
   hours of rest in each calendar week, except in emergency cases for the suppression
   of riots or tumults or the preservation of the public peace, in times of war, riot,
   conflagration or public celebration or whenever the sheriff deems it necessary to
   maintain good order.  No member shall be required to work more than eight consecutive hours in any twenty-four
   hours except in the aforesaid cases of emergency.  Every member shall be allowed one day's vacation for each month of service for the
   first twelve months of service, and thereafter an annual vacation of not less than
   fourteen days.  He shall also be allowed an annual sick leave of not less than fourteen days.  All such vacation and sick leave shall be without any deduction or diminution of
   salary or compensation as fixed by the salary board.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.17. General repealer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.17. General repealer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.17. General repealer (2023)
content: All acts and parts of acts are repealed in so far as they are inconsistent herewith.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.16. Penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.16. Penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.16. Penalties (2023)
content:
The sheriff of the county or anyone acting for him who shall cause any person to be
   appointed to or promoted in the force of deputy sheriffs contrary to the provisions
   of this act, or who violates any of the provisions of this act, shall be guilty of
   a misdemeanor, and upon conviction, shall be sentenced to pay a fine of not more than
   five hundred dollars ($500) or suffer imprisonment not exceeding one year, or both.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4233. Removal of bodies to morgue
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4233. Removal of bodies to morgue
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4233. Removal of bodies to morgue (2023)
content:
Whenever the body of any deceased person who is unidentified, or which body is unclaimed
   by proper persons, has been found within the county, it shall be removed to the county
   morgue.  The coroner shall, if he deems it necessary, cause any such body to be properly
   embalmed or prepared for preservation for such length of time as he may think proper.  Any such body shall be examined or inspected only by such persons as the coroner
   authorizes in writing or who are admitted in his presence.  No such body shall be removed from any such morgue except upon the certificate of
   the coroner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4232. Duties with respect to county morgues
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4232. Duties with respect to county morgues
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4232. Duties with respect to county morgues (2023)
content:
The coroner of the county shall make general rules and regulations for the government
   and control of county morgues, and shall appoint suitable persons for such morgues
   so established to have charge of the same, and who shall be removable at the pleasure
   of the coroner.  The number of such persons and the salary of each shall be fixed by the salary board.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.18. Effective date
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.18. Effective date
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.18. Effective date (2023)
content: This act shall take effect immediately.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4231. Deputies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4231. Deputies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4231. Deputies (2023)
content:
The coroner shall appoint a chief deputy and may appoint one or more deputies to act
   in his place and stead, as he may deem proper and necessary.  Such deputy or deputies shall have the same powers as the coroner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4234. Ambulance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4234. Ambulance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4234. Ambulance (2023)
content:
In the county, the county commissioners shall furnish and maintain, from the general
   funds of the county, an ambulance for the removal of bodies of deceased persons to
   and from the morgue and for the burial of unclaimed bodies.  The coroner may provide rules and regulations for the use and maintenance of the
   ambulance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4236. Coroner's investigations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4236. Coroner's investigations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4236. Coroner's investigations (2023)
content:
(a) The coroner having a view of the body shall investigate the facts and circumstances
      concerning deaths which appear to have happened within the county, regardless where
      the cause thereof may have occurred, for the purpose of determining whether or not
      an autopsy should be conducted or an inquest thereof shall be had, in the following
      cases:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4237. Autopsy; inquest; records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4237. Autopsy; inquest; records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4237. Autopsy; inquest; records (2023)
content:
(a) If, upon investigation, the coroner shall be unable to determine the cause and
      manner of death, he shall perform or order an autopsy on the body.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4235. Unclaimed property of deceased; sales
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4235. Unclaimed property of deceased; sales
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4235. Unclaimed property of deceased; sales (2023)
content:
(a) The coroner shall safely keep in his charge all personal effects and property
      which appear to have been on or about the person at the time of his death, or being
      found on any decedent whose body is received at the county morgue, and all such effects
      and property which are delivered to him according to law.  The coroner shall hold such property for one year, unless sooner claimed by legal
      representatives of the deceased or otherwise duly and lawfully claimed or disposed
      of.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4235.1. Requests for examinations and reports
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4235.1. Requests for examinations and reports
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4235.1. Requests for examinations and reports (2023)
content:
(a) Requests for examinations or other professional services by other counties or
      persons may be complied with at the discretion of the coroner pursuant to guidelines
      established by the county commissioners.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4238. Sudden deaths defined
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4238. Sudden deaths defined
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4238. Sudden deaths defined (2023)
content:
The coroner shall regard any death as sudden if it occurs without prior medical attendance
   by a person who may lawfully execute a certificate of death in this Commonwealth,
   or if, within twenty-four hours of death, the decedent was discharged from such medical
   attendance or a change of such medical attendance had occurred, or if any such medical
   attendance began within twenty-four hours of death and the medical attendant refuses
   or is unable to certify the cause of death.  Medical attendance includes hospitalization.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4240. Release of coroner's jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4240. Release of coroner's jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4240. Release of coroner's jurisdiction (2023)
content:
Whenever the coroner assumes jurisdiction of a body pursuant to the provisions of
   this subdivision or of any other law, the body shall not be released or removed from
   his jurisdiction except upon his direction and consent, in accordance with law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4201. Unfinished business of outgoing sheriff
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4201. Unfinished business of outgoing sheriff
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4201. Unfinished business of outgoing sheriff (2023)
content:
(a) It shall be the duty of every outgoing sheriff to deliver all unfinished and unexecuted
      writs and process whatsoever to his successor, whose duty it shall be to receive and
      execute the same as if said writs and process had been originally issued and directed
      to him, and to carry out and complete all other official duties of his predecessor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4239. Bodies not to be moved
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4239. Bodies not to be moved
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4239. Bodies not to be moved (2023)
content:
In all cases where the coroner has jurisdiction to investigate the facts and circumstances
   of death, the body and its surroundings shall be left untouched until the coroner
   has had a view thereof or until he shall otherwise direct or authorize, except as
   may be otherwise provided by law, or as circumstances may require.  Bodies upon a public thoroughfare or in other places may be removed so much as is
   necessary for precaution against traffic accidents or other serious consequences which
   might reasonably be anticipated if they were left intact.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4202. Sheriff may act by deputy
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4202. Sheriff may act by deputy
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4202. Sheriff may act by deputy (2023)
content:
Whenever the sheriff is or shall be required by law to act in person under or by virtue
   of any writ or process whatsoever issued by the courts of this Commonwealth, he may
   act either in person or by a regularly appointed deputy sheriff.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4203.1. Chief deputy in counties of the second class
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4203.1. Chief deputy in counties of the second class
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4203.1. Chief deputy in counties of the second class (2023)
content:
In counties of the second class, the sheriff of the county shall appoint in accordance
   with section 1216,1by commission duly recorded in the Department of Real Estate, a chief deputy, whose
   appointment shall be revocable by the sheriff at pleasure on recording in said department
   a signed revocation thereof.  The chief deputy, during his continuance in office, shall have full power and authority
   to perform any duty incumbent upon such sheriff with like effect in law as if such
   official act had been done by the sheriff in person, regardless of the ability or
   temporary disability of such sheriff to act while such sheriff continues in office.  Nothing in this section shall operate to relieve such sheriff or his sureties from
   liability upon their official bond.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4203. Chief deputy
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4203. Chief deputy
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4203. Chief deputy (2023)
content:
The sheriff of the county shall appoint, by commission duly recorded in the office
   for recording deeds, a chief deputy, whose appointment shall be revocable by the sheriff
   at pleasure on recording in said office a signed revocation thereof.  The chief deputy, during his continuance in office, shall have full power and authority
   to perform any duty incumbent upon such sheriff with like effect in law as if such
   official act had been done by the sheriff in person, regardless of the ability or
   temporary disability of such sheriff to act while such sheriff continues in office.  Nothing in this section shall operate to relieve such sheriff or his sureties from
   liability upon their official bond.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4204. Real estate deputy
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4204. Real estate deputy
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4204. Real estate deputy (2023)
content:
The sheriff may have a real estate deputy to take charge of all matters relating to
   sheriff's sales of real estate and distributions of the proceeds thereof, whose appointment
   shall be made and be revocable, as hereinbefore provided for the chief deputy.  Such deputy shall have full power to perform all duties incumbent upon the sheriff,
   in like manner as his chief deputy, with like effect in law as if such official acts
   had been done by the sheriff in person.  Such duties shall include the execution and acknowledgment of sheriff's deeds for
   real estate upon receipt of the purchase price thereof.  Nothing in this act1shall operate to relieve the sheriff or his sureties from liability upon their official
   bonds, but such liability shall continue as heretofore.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4241. Cooperation with district attorney
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4241. Cooperation with district attorney
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4241. Cooperation with district attorney (2023)
content:
In the exercise of his duties as contained in this subdivision, the coroner shall,
   so far as may be practicable, consult and advise with the district attorney.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4205. Deputies and clerks
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4205. Deputies and clerks
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4205. Deputies and clerks (2023)
content:
The sheriff of the county may appoint such deputies and clerks as may be necessary
   to properly transact the business of his office.  He may revoke the appointment of deputies in the same manner as his chief deputy.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4205.1. Deputies and clerks in counties of the second class
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4205.1. Deputies and clerks in counties of the second class
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4205.1. Deputies and clerks in counties of the second class (2023)
content:
In counties of the second class, the sheriff of the county may appoint in accordance
   with section 1216,1such deputies and clerks as may be necessary to properly transact the business of
   his office.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4243. Power of subpoena and attachment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4243. Power of subpoena and attachment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4243. Power of subpoena and attachment (2023)
content:
The coroner shall have power to issue subpoenas to obtain the attendance of any person
   whom it may be necessary to examine as a witness at any inquest, and to compel attendance
   by attachment in like manner and to the same extent as any court of common pleas of
   this Commonwealth may or can do in cases pending before them, and also to compel in
   like manner the production of all papers and other things relative to such inquest.  Such subpoena and attachment shall be served and executed by the sheriff or by the
   coroner himself or his deputy, as the case may require.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4206. Deputy sheriffs; qualifications
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4206. Deputy sheriffs; qualifications
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4206. Deputy sheriffs; qualifications (2023)
content:
A sheriff shall not appoint any person a chief deputy or any other deputy sheriff
   unless the sheriff files with the prothonotary, prior to the appointment of such person,
   the name and photograph of such person, together with an affidavit of such person
   setting forth the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4207. False statements in deputy's affidavit
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4207. False statements in deputy's affidavit
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4207. False statements in deputy's affidavit (2023)
content:
Any false statement contained in any such affidavit shall constitute perjury and shall
   be punishable as such.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4209. Public list of applicants for deputy sheriff
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4209. Public list of applicants for deputy sheriff
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4209. Public list of applicants for deputy sheriff (2023)
content:
The sheriff shall, from time to time, prepare a list of the names of all persons who
   have applied for appointment as deputy sheriff and who meet the qualifications hereinbefore
   prescribed.  Such list shall be posted in a public place for a period of not less than ten days,
   and thereafter shall be filed in the office of the prothonotary.  No deputies shall be appointed by the sheriff whose names do not appear on said
   list.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4208. Filed items public records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4208. Filed items public records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4208. Filed items public records (2023)
content:
The name, photograph and affidavit of any such person so filed with the prothonotary
   shall constitute a public record.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4209.1. Public list of applicants for deputy sheriff in counties of the second class
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4209.1. Public list of applicants for deputy sheriff in counties of the second class
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4209.1. Public list of applicants for deputy sheriff in counties of the second class (2023)
content:
In counties of the second class, the sheriff shall, from time to time, prepare a list
   of the names of all persons who have applied for appointment as deputy sheriff and
   who meet the qualifications hereinbefore prescribed.  Such list shall be posted in a public place for a period of not less than ten (10)
   days and thereafter shall be filed in the Department of Court Records--civil division.  No deputies shall be appointed by the sheriff whose names do not appear on said
   list.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4244. Power to administer oaths
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4244. Power to administer oaths
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4244. Power to administer oaths (2023)
content:
The coroner shall have power to administer oaths and affirmations to all persons brought
   or appearing before him, and any person swearing or affirming falsely on such examination
   shall be guilty of perjury.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4210. Private services, gifts and payments; contracts prohibited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4210. Private services, gifts and payments; contracts prohibited
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4210. Private services, gifts and payments; contracts prohibited (2023)
content:
(a) No sheriff, deputy sheriff, detective or other county police officer whatsoever
      shall perform, directly or indirectly, any official services or official duties for
      any person, association or corporation, or receive, directly or indirectly, any compensation,
      gifts or gratuities from any person, association or corporation, during the period
      of his official services.  Nothing herein contained shall prohibit such officers from serving writs and other
      legal process as authorized by law.  Any compensation payable to any such officer for official duties and services shall
      be paid only out of the public funds, to the amount and in the manner prescribed by
      law.  Gifts, donations and gratuities of any nature whatsoever, made by any person, association
      or corporation to the county or to any official or agent thereof, shall not constitute
      public funds within the meaning of this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4212. Construction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4212. Construction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4212. Construction (2023)
content: Nothing contained in sections 1206 or 1210 of this act1shall be construed:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4211. Penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4211. Penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4211. Penalties (2023)
content:
Any sheriff, deputy sheriff or any other county police officer whatsoever, or any
   other official of the county, or any person, association or corporation violating
   any of the provisions of sections 1206, 1209 or 1210 of this act,1shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction, shall be sentenced to pay
   a fine of not less than one hundred dollars ($100) nor more than five hundred dollars
   ($500), or to undergo imprisonment for not less than ninety (90) days nor more than
   two years, or both.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4242. Certificate of cause of death
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4242. Certificate of cause of death
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4242. Certificate of cause of death (2023)
content:
The coroner shall issue a certificate of cause of death in all cases referred to him
   by the local registrar of vital statistics, pursuant to the provisions of the act,
   approved the twenty-first day of May, one thousand nine hundred forty-three (Pamphlet
   Laws 414), known as the Uniform Vital Statistics Act,1and in all other cases of which he has jurisdiction, if no person duly authorized
   by the said act certifies the cause of death.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4246. Inquests not public
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4246. Inquests not public
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4246. Inquests not public (2023)
content:
The coroner, may in his discretion, admit or exclude members of the public from any
   inquest or part thereof, and admit or exclude any person interested or suspected from
   such inquest or any part thereof.  No person excluded may appear by attorney, but any person required to attend may
   have benefit of counsel at such attendance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4243.1. Inquests; juries
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4243.1. Inquests; juries
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4243.1. Inquests; juries (2023)
content:
(a) The coroner may at his discretion summon a jury of six to be selected from the
      jury panels of the court of common pleas.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4213. Solicitor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4213. Solicitor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4213. Solicitor (2023)
content:
The sheriff may appoint one person learned in the law and admitted to practice in
   the county of this Commonwealth as his solicitor.  Said solicitor shall advise the sheriff upon all legal matters that may be submitted
   to him, and shall conduct any litigation in connection with the sheriff's office,
   when requested so to do by the sheriff.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4215. Sheriff to keep docket
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4215. Sheriff to keep docket
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4215. Sheriff to keep docket (2023)
content:
Every sheriff and every coroner acting as sheriff shall provide and keep in his office
   a book or books in which he shall enter all writs that may come to him and the proceedings
   thereon, and at the expiration of his term of office, such book or books shall be
   deposited in the office of the prothonotary, for the inspection of all persons interested
   therein.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4247. Chief deputy coroner to act as coroner in case of vacancy
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4247. Chief deputy coroner to act as coroner in case of vacancy
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4247. Chief deputy coroner to act as coroner in case of vacancy (2023)
content:
If the coroner shall be legally removed from his office or shall die or resign before
   expiration of the term for which he was commissioned, the chief deputy coroner of
   the county shall execute the office of coroner and perform all things thereunto appertaining
   and receive the compensation provided by law for coroners until another coroner is
   commissioned and notice thereof is given to such chief deputy coroner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4214. Chief deputy sheriff to act as sheriff in case of a vacancy
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4214. Chief deputy sheriff to act as sheriff in case of a vacancy
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4214. Chief deputy sheriff to act as sheriff in case of a vacancy (2023)
content:
If the sheriff shall be legally removed from his office, or shall die before the expiration
   of the term for which he was commissioned, the chief deputy sheriff of the county
   shall execute the office of sheriff and perform all things thereunto appertaining
   and receive the compensation provided by law for sheriffs until another sheriff is
   commissioned and notice thereof is given to such chief deputy sheriff.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.3. Application for examination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.3. Application for examination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.3. Application for examination (2023)
content:
(a) Each person desiring to apply for examination shall file with the commission a
      formal application in which the applicant shall state under oath or affirmation (i)
      his full name and residence or post office address, (ii) his citizenship, place and
      date of birth, (iii) his condition of health and physical capacity for public service,
      (iv) his business or employment and his residence for the past five years, and (v)
      such other information as may be required by the commission's rules and regulations,
      showing the applicant's qualifications for the position for which he is being examined.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.1. Appointment of deputy sheriffs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.1. Appointment of deputy sheriffs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.1. Appointment of deputy sheriffs (2023)
content:
(a) The sheriff of a county of the second class may subject to Article XVIII of the
      Second Class County Code, act of July 28, 1953 (P.L. 723, No. 230)1appoint such deputies as may be necessary to properly transact the business of his
      office:  Provided, however, That hereafter every appointment to and promotion in the
      force of deputy sheriffs of such counties shall be made only according to qualifications
      and fitness to be ascertained by examinations which shall be competitive as provided
      in this act.  The compensation of deputy sheriffs shall be paid by the county.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.4. Rejection of applicant; hearing
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.4. Rejection of applicant; hearing
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.4. Rejection of applicant; hearing (2023)
content:
(a) The commission may refuse to examine, or, if examined, may refuse to certify as
      eligible, after examination, any applicant who is found to lack any of the minimum
      qualifications for examination prescribed in the rules and regulations adopted for
      the position or employment for which he has applied, or who is physically disabled
      and unfit for the performance of the duties of the position to which he seeks employment,
      or who is addicted to the habitual use of intoxicating liquors or narcotic drugs,
      or who has been guilty of any crime involving moral turpitude, or of infamous or notoriously
      disgraceful conduct, or who has been dismissed from public service for delinquency
      or misconduct of office, or who is affiliated with any group whose policies or activities
      are subversive to the form of government set forth in the constitutions and laws of
      the United States and Pennsylvania.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4245. Commitment to county prison
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4245. Commitment to county prison
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4245. Commitment to county prison (2023)
content:
If any person appearing before the coroner for examination shall refuse to take oath
   or affirmation, or after having been sworn or affirmed shall refuse to make answer
   to such questions as shall be put to him by the coroner touching the matters of the
   inquest, such person so refusing may be held for contempt before the court of quarter
   sessions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4216. Sheriff's employes, counties of second class
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4216. Sheriff's employes, counties of second class
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4216. Sheriff's employes, counties of second class (2023)
content:
(a) Appointment and promotion of deputies and other employes in the office of sheriff
      of a county of the second class shall be made in the manner provided by the act of
      May 31, 1974 (P.L. 296, No. 94),1entitled “An act providing for the appointment, promotion, reduction in rank, suspension,
      furlough, discharge and reinstatement of deputy sheriffs in counties of the second
      class;  extending civil service coverage to such deputies;  and providing penalties,”
      except as otherwise provided in this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.5. Manner of making appointments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.5. Manner of making appointments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.5. Manner of making appointments (2023)
content:
Every position of employment, unless filled by promotion or reinstatement, shall be
   filled only in the following manner:  The sheriff of the county shall notify the commission
   of any vacancy in the force of deputy sheriffs which is to be filled and shall request
   certification of a list of eligibles.  The commission shall certify to the sheriff all those eligible from the last preceding
   examination held within a period of three years next preceding the date of the request
   for such eligibles.  The sheriff of the county shall thereupon make an appointment from the eligible
   list certified to him.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4250. Anatomical gifts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4250. Anatomical gifts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4250. Anatomical gifts (2023)
content:
The coroner may order the removal of parts of a decedent's body for donation purposes
   in accordance with 20 Pa.C.S. Ch. 86 (relating to anatomical gifts).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.2. Civil Service Commission
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.2. Civil Service Commission
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.2. Civil Service Commission (2023)
content:
(a) The provisions of this act shall be administered by the Civil Service Commission,
      hereinafter referred to as the commission, created pursuant to section 15031of the Second Class County Code, act of July 28, 1953 (P.L. 723, No. 230).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.6. Probationary period
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.6. Probationary period
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.6. Probationary period (2023)
content:
All appointments to positions in the force of deputy sheriffs shall be for a probationary
   period of nine months.  During that period an appointee may not be promoted nor may he be dismissed except
   for cause as specified in section 10 of this act.1If, at the close of the probationary period, the conduct or fitness of the probationery2has not been satisfactory to the sheriff of the county, the probationer shall be
   notified in writing that he will not receive a permanent appointment.  Thereupon, the appointment shall cease.  Otherwise, his retention shall be equivalent to a permanent appointment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4217. Political activity by sheriff's employes in counties of the second class
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4217. Political activity by sheriff's employes in counties of the second class
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4217. Political activity by sheriff's employes in counties of the second class (2023)
content:
(a) No employe shall use his official authority or influence for the purpose of interfering
      with or affecting the result of an election.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4249. Solicitor to coroner
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4249. Solicitor to coroner
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4249. Solicitor to coroner (2023)
content:
The coroner may appoint one person, learned in the law, as his solicitor.  The solicitor shall advise the coroner upon all legal matters that may be submitted
   to him, and shall conduct any litigation in connection with the coroner's office when
   requested to do so by him.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4248. Vacancies; no fees upon commissions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4248. Vacancies; no fees upon commissions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4248. Vacancies; no fees upon commissions (2023)
content:
If any person elected to the office of coroner shall neglect or refuse, for the space
   of two months next after such election, to assume the duties of said office and to
   comply with the requirements of the acts of Assembly in such cases, the office shall
   be vacant, and it shall be the duty of the Governor, upon the notification of the
   recorder of deeds, to appoint and commission some suitable person to fill such vacancy,
   until the first Monday of January next succeeding the first municipal election which
   shall occur two or more months after the happening of such vacancy.  Such appointee shall be confirmed by the Senate if in session.  No fees shall hereafter be charged on commissions issued to the coroner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(c) Provisions Relating to Sheriffs and Coroners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4260. Not to exercise office until commission granted and recorded; penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (c) Provisions Relating to Sheriffs and Coroners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4260. Not to exercise office until commission granted and recorded; penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4260. Not to exercise office until commission granted and recorded; penalty (2023)
content:
No person elected or appointed to the office of sheriff or coroner shall execute any
   of the duties of such office before a commission shall have been duly granted to him
   by the Governor and recorded in the recorder of deeds office, under a penalty of imprisonment
   for a term not exceeding six months, at the discretion of the court of quarter sessions.  Such person shall nevertheless be liable to any person injured by any acts done
   by him under color of such office.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.13. Discrimination on account of religious or political affiliations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.13. Discrimination on account of religious or political affiliations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.13. Discrimination on account of religious or political affiliations (2023)
content:
No question in any form of application for any examination or in any examination shall
   be so framed as to elicit information concerning the religious or political opinions
   of any applicant, nor shall inquiry be made concerning such opinions or affiliations
   and all such disclosures thereof shall be discountenanced.  No discrimination shall be exercised, threatened or promised by any person in or
   interested in the force of deputy sheriffs against or in favor of an applicant on
   the eligible list for appointment to or promotion in the force because of his religious
   or political opinions or affiliations.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.10. Reducing in rank; suspension; furloughing; discharging
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.10. Reducing in rank; suspension; furloughing; discharging
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.10. Reducing in rank; suspension; furloughing; discharging (2023)
content:
(a) No deputy sheriff covered by this act shall be reduced in rank, suspended, furloughed
      or discharged, except for the following reasons:  (i) neglect or violation of official
      duty, (ii) violation of a law of this Commonwealth which provides that such violation
      constitutes a misdemeanor or a felony, (iii) inefficiency, except as hereinafter provided,
      wilful disobedience of orders, or conduct unbecoming a police officer, (iv) drinking
      of intoxicating liquor while on duty or the use of which renders him unfit when called
      upon for duty.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.14. Hours of service; exceptions; vacations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.14. Hours of service; exceptions; vacations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.14. Hours of service; exceptions; vacations (2023)
content:
Every member of the force of deputy sheriffs shall have at least twenty-four consecutive
   hours of rest in each calendar week, except in emergency cases for the suppression
   of riots or tumults or the preservation of the public peace, in times of war, riot,
   conflagration or public celebration or whenever the sheriff deems it necessary to
   maintain good order.  No member shall be required to work more than eight consecutive hours in any twenty-four
   hours except in the aforesaid cases of emergency.  Every member shall be allowed one day's vacation for each month of service for the
   first twelve months of service, and thereafter an annual vacation of not less than
   fourteen days.  He shall also be allowed an annual sick leave of not less than fourteen days.  All such vacation and sick leave shall be without any deduction or diminution of
   salary or compensation as fixed by the salary board.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.9. Physical examinations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.9. Physical examinations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.9. Physical examinations (2023)
content:
All applicants for examination shall undergo a physical examination, which shall be
   conducted under the supervision of a doctor of medicine appointed by the sheriff of
   the county.  No person shall be eligible to take an examination until said doctor certifies to
   the commission that the applicant is free from any bodily or mental defects, deformity
   or disease that might incapacitate him from the discharge of the duties of a deputy
   sheriff.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.7. Provisional appointments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.7. Provisional appointments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.7. Provisional appointments (2023)
content:
Whenever there are urgent reasons for the filling of a vacancy in any position in
   the force of deputy sheriffs and there are no names on the eligible list for such
   appointment, the sheriff of the county may nominate a person to the commission for
   a noncompetitive examination and if such nominee shall be certified by the commission
   as qualified, after such noncompetitive examination, he may be appointed provisionally
   to fill such vacancy until an examination for such position can be held.  It shall thereupon become the duty of the commission, within three weeks from the
   date of provisional appointment, to hold a competitive examination for such position
   and certify a list of eligibles to the sheriff of the county and a regular appointment
   shall then be made as prescribed in this act.  Nothing herein contained shall prevent the appointment of deputy sheriffs without
   examination to act in emergency cases, for the suppression of riots, breaches of the
   peace, tumults, in times of war, pestilence, conflagration, or public celebration.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.11. Reduction in number of deputy sheriffs; reinstatements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.11. Reduction in number of deputy sheriffs; reinstatements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.11. Reduction in number of deputy sheriffs; reinstatements (2023)
content:
If for reasons of economy or otherwise, it shall be deemed necessary by the sheriff
   of the county to reduce the number of deputy sheriffs then such reduction in numbers
   shall be made in the following manner:  (i) if there are any deputy sheriffs eligible
   for retirement under the terms of any retirement or pension system or law, then such
   reduction in numbers shall be made by retirement, if the party to be retired has served
   in the force of deputy sheriffs for a period of at least twenty-five years and his
   age exceeds the maximum age as defined in the act of October 27, 1955 (P.L. 744, No.
   222),1known as the “Pennsylvania Human Relations Act”,  (ii) if the number of deputy sheriffs
   eligible for retirement is insufficient to effect the reduction in numbers decided
   upon by the sheriff of the county, or if no retirement or pension system or law exists,
   or if there are no deputy sheriffs eligible for retirement or pension, then the reduction
   shall be made by furloughing the last deputy sheriff including the probationers that
   have been appointed to the force and continue in numerical order until the reduction
   decided upon by the sheriff of the county has been affected.  In any case where there has been more than one employe appointed at the same time
   then such furloughing shall be determined by the alphabetical order of the first letter
   of their surname.  In the event the said force of deputy sheriffs shall again be increased in numbers
   then the employes furloughed shall be reinstated in the inverse order of that in which
   they were furloughed before any new appointments shall be made to the deputy sheriffs'
   force.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.8. Promotions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.8. Promotions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.8. Promotions (2023)
content:
Promotions shall be based on merit to be ascertained by examinations to be prescribed
   by the sheriff and the commission.  All questions relative to promotions shall be practical in character and such as
   will fairly test the merit and fitness of persons seeking promotion.  The sheriff of the county shall have the discretion to promote the person or persons
   of his choice from the list of those who have successfully completed the appropriate
   examination and are certified as eligible for promotion by the commission.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.12. Present employes exempted
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.12. Present employes exempted
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.12. Present employes exempted (2023)
content:
(a) All members of the force of deputy sheriffs upon the effective date of this act
      shall continue to hold their positions and shall not be required to take any examination
      whatsoever under this act except such as may be required for subsequent promotion.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.15. Compensation and expenses to deputy sheriff injured or ill
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.15. Compensation and expenses to deputy sheriff injured or ill
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.15. Compensation and expenses to deputy sheriff injured or ill (2023)
content:
After the effective date of this act any member of the force of deputy sheriffs of
   all ranks, including chief deputy, who may be injured or become sick through the performance
   of his duties and by reason thereof is temporarily incapacitated from performing his
   duties, shall be paid by the county his full rate of salary as fixed by the salary
   board until the disability arising therefrom has ceased.  All medical and hospital bills incurred in connection with any such injury or sickness
   shall be paid by the county.  All benefits under the Workmen's Compensation Law which shall be reviewed or collected
   by any such member during the period he has received salary for temporary disability
   shall be paid over to the county and paid into the treasury thereof.  If any such payment or payments shall not be so made by the member of the force,
   the amount so directed to be paid to the county shall be deducted from any salary
   which shall then or thereafter become due and owing to such member.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.17. General repealer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.17. General repealer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.17. General repealer (2023)
content: All acts and parts of acts are repealed in so far as they are inconsistent herewith.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4231. Deputies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4231. Deputies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4231. Deputies (2023)
content:
The coroner shall appoint a chief deputy and may appoint one or more deputies to act
   in his place and stead, as he may deem proper and necessary.  Such deputy or deputies shall have the same powers as the coroner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4234. Ambulance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4234. Ambulance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4234. Ambulance (2023)
content:
In the county, the county commissioners shall furnish and maintain, from the general
   funds of the county, an ambulance for the removal of bodies of deceased persons to
   and from the morgue and for the burial of unclaimed bodies.  The coroner may provide rules and regulations for the use and maintenance of the
   ambulance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4233. Removal of bodies to morgue
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4233. Removal of bodies to morgue
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4233. Removal of bodies to morgue (2023)
content:
Whenever the body of any deceased person who is unidentified, or which body is unclaimed
   by proper persons, has been found within the county, it shall be removed to the county
   morgue.  The coroner shall, if he deems it necessary, cause any such body to be properly
   embalmed or prepared for preservation for such length of time as he may think proper.  Any such body shall be examined or inspected only by such persons as the coroner
   authorizes in writing or who are admitted in his presence.  No such body shall be removed from any such morgue except upon the certificate of
   the coroner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.18. Effective date
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.18. Effective date
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.18. Effective date (2023)
content: This act shall take effect immediately.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(A.1) Deputy Sheriffs›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.16. Penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (A.1) Deputy Sheriffs › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.16. Penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4221.16. Penalties (2023)
content:
The sheriff of the county or anyone acting for him who shall cause any person to be
   appointed to or promoted in the force of deputy sheriffs contrary to the provisions
   of this act, or who violates any of the provisions of this act, shall be guilty of
   a misdemeanor, and upon conviction, shall be sentenced to pay a fine of not more than
   five hundred dollars ($500) or suffer imprisonment not exceeding one year, or both.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4236. Coroner's investigations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4236. Coroner's investigations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4236. Coroner's investigations (2023)
content:
(a) The coroner having a view of the body shall investigate the facts and circumstances
      concerning deaths which appear to have happened within the county, regardless where
      the cause thereof may have occurred, for the purpose of determining whether or not
      an autopsy should be conducted or an inquest thereof shall be had, in the following
      cases:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4237. Autopsy; inquest; records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4237. Autopsy; inquest; records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4237. Autopsy; inquest; records (2023)
content:
(a) If, upon investigation, the coroner shall be unable to determine the cause and
      manner of death, he shall perform or order an autopsy on the body.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4239. Bodies not to be moved
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4239. Bodies not to be moved
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4239. Bodies not to be moved (2023)
content:
In all cases where the coroner has jurisdiction to investigate the facts and circumstances
   of death, the body and its surroundings shall be left untouched until the coroner
   has had a view thereof or until he shall otherwise direct or authorize, except as
   may be otherwise provided by law, or as circumstances may require.  Bodies upon a public thoroughfare or in other places may be removed so much as is
   necessary for precaution against traffic accidents or other serious consequences which
   might reasonably be anticipated if they were left intact.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4238. Sudden deaths defined
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4238. Sudden deaths defined
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4238. Sudden deaths defined (2023)
content:
The coroner shall regard any death as sudden if it occurs without prior medical attendance
   by a person who may lawfully execute a certificate of death in this Commonwealth,
   or if, within twenty-four hours of death, the decedent was discharged from such medical
   attendance or a change of such medical attendance had occurred, or if any such medical
   attendance began within twenty-four hours of death and the medical attendant refuses
   or is unable to certify the cause of death.  Medical attendance includes hospitalization.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4242. Certificate of cause of death
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4242. Certificate of cause of death
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4242. Certificate of cause of death (2023)
content:
The coroner shall issue a certificate of cause of death in all cases referred to him
   by the local registrar of vital statistics, pursuant to the provisions of the act,
   approved the twenty-first day of May, one thousand nine hundred forty-three (Pamphlet
   Laws 414), known as the Uniform Vital Statistics Act,1and in all other cases of which he has jurisdiction, if no person duly authorized
   by the said act certifies the cause of death.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4240. Release of coroner's jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4240. Release of coroner's jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4240. Release of coroner's jurisdiction (2023)
content:
Whenever the coroner assumes jurisdiction of a body pursuant to the provisions of
   this subdivision or of any other law, the body shall not be released or removed from
   his jurisdiction except upon his direction and consent, in accordance with law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4232. Duties with respect to county morgues
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4232. Duties with respect to county morgues
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4232. Duties with respect to county morgues (2023)
content:
The coroner of the county shall make general rules and regulations for the government
   and control of county morgues, and shall appoint suitable persons for such morgues
   so established to have charge of the same, and who shall be removable at the pleasure
   of the coroner.  The number of such persons and the salary of each shall be fixed by the salary board.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4235. Unclaimed property of deceased; sales
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4235. Unclaimed property of deceased; sales
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4235. Unclaimed property of deceased; sales (2023)
content:
(a) The coroner shall safely keep in his charge all personal effects and property
      which appear to have been on or about the person at the time of his death, or being
      found on any decedent whose body is received at the county morgue, and all such effects
      and property which are delivered to him according to law.  The coroner shall hold such property for one year, unless sooner claimed by legal
      representatives of the deceased or otherwise duly and lawfully claimed or disposed
      of.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4247. Chief deputy coroner to act as coroner in case of vacancy
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4247. Chief deputy coroner to act as coroner in case of vacancy
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4247. Chief deputy coroner to act as coroner in case of vacancy (2023)
content:
If the coroner shall be legally removed from his office or shall die or resign before
   expiration of the term for which he was commissioned, the chief deputy coroner of
   the county shall execute the office of coroner and perform all things thereunto appertaining
   and receive the compensation provided by law for coroners until another coroner is
   commissioned and notice thereof is given to such chief deputy coroner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4243.1. Inquests; juries
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4243.1. Inquests; juries
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4243.1. Inquests; juries (2023)
content:
(a) The coroner may at his discretion summon a jury of six to be selected from the
      jury panels of the court of common pleas.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4235.1. Requests for examinations and reports
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (b) Coroner › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4235.1. Requests for examinations and reports
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4235.1. Requests for examinations and reports (2023)
content:
(a) Requests for examinations or other professional services by other counties or
      persons may be complied with at the discretion of the coroner pursuant to guidelines
      established by the county commissioners.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(b) Coroner›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4245. Commitment to county prison
