   to prevent the use thereof by such railroad company or its employes, is guilty of
   a summary offense, and upon conviction thereof, shall be sentenced to pay a fine of
   one hundred dollars ($100).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 P.S. Crimes and Offenses›Chapter 51. Pre-Crimes Code Provisions›Chapter 2. The Penal Code of 1939›Article VIII. Offenses Against Personal Property and Fraudulent Dealing Therewith›PA ST 18 P.S. § 4806.9. Possession of records of criminal usury
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 P.S. Crimes and Offenses › Chapter 51. Pre-Crimes Code Provisions › Chapter 2. The Penal Code of 1939 › Article VIII. Offenses Against Personal Property and Fraudulent Dealing Therewith › PA ST 18 P.S. § 4806.9. Possession of records of criminal usury
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 P.S. § 4806.9. Possession of records of criminal usury (2023)
content:
Whoever, other than a public officer in the performance of his duty as such, maintains,
   causes to be maintained, conspires to maintain, or possesses any writing, paper, book,
   instrument or article used to record criminally usurious transactions, and who knows
   or has reasonable grounds to know that the contents record a criminally usurious transaction,
   is guilty of a felony and, upon conviction thereof, shall be sentenced to pay a fine
   not exceeding two thousand, five hundred dollars ($2,500) or to undergo imprisonment
   not exceeding five (5) years, or both.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 1. Short Title and Definitions›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 101. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 1. Short Title and Definitions › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 101. Short title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 101. Short title (2023)
content:
This title shall be known and may be cited as the “Probate, Estates and Fiduciaries
   Code.”1Each chapter herein shall be known and may be cited by its chapter heading.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 711. Mandatory exercise of jurisdiction through orphans' court division in general
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 711. Mandatory exercise of jurisdiction through orphans' court division in general
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 711. Mandatory exercise of jurisdiction through orphans' court division in general (2023)
content:
Except as provided in section 712 (relating to nonmandatory exercise of jurisdiction
   through the orphans' court division) and section 713 (relating to special provisions
   for Philadelphia County), the jurisdiction of the court of common pleas over the following
   shall be exercised through its orphans' court division:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter C. Venue›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 722. Venue of trust estates
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter C. Venue › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 722. Venue of trust estates
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 722. Venue of trust estates (2023)
content:
When a Pennsylvania court has jurisdiction of any trust, testamentary or inter vivos,
   except as otherwise provided by law, the venue for all purposes shall be in the county
   where at the time being is the situs of the trust.  The situs of the trust shall remain in the county of the court which first assumed
   jurisdiction of the trust, unless and until such court shall order a change of situs
   under the provisions of this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 713. Special provisions for Philadelphia County
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 713. Special provisions for Philadelphia County
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 713. Special provisions for Philadelphia County (2023)
content:
The provisions of section 711 (relating to mandatory exercise of jurisdiction through
   orphans' court division in general), insofar as they relate to adoptions and birth
   records, shall not apply to Philadelphia County.  In Philadelphia County the jurisdiction over adoptions and all proceedings which
   may be necessary to be presented to a court for determination with regard to issues
   concerning recordation of birth and birth records or the alteration, amendment or
   modification of such birth records or the right to obtain a certified copy of the
   same, shall be exercised through the family court division of the court of common
   pleas.  Whenever a resident of Philadelphia is entitled to take an appeal from the action
   of the Department of Health in connection with any matters concerning birth records,
   the appeal shall be taken to the family court division of the court of common pleas
   of Philadelphia.  In all other matters in which a petition is addressed to a court by a resident of
   Philadelphia in connection with matters of birth records, the filing of which petition
   is not in the nature of an appeal but is an original proceeding, the petition shall
   be determined by the family court division of the court of common pleas of Philadelphia.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 3. Ownership of Property; Legal Title and Equitable Estate›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 304. Application of payments made to fiduciaries
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 3. Ownership of Property; Legal Title and Equitable Estate › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 304. Application of payments made to fiduciaries
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 304. Application of payments made to fiduciaries (2023)
content:
A person who, in good faith, pays or transfers to a fiduciary any money or other property,
   which the fiduciary as such is authorized to receive, is not responsible for the proper
   application thereof by the fiduciary, and any right or title acquired from the fiduciary
   in consideration of the payment or transfer is not invalid in consequence of a misapplication
   by the fiduciary.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter C. Venue›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 727. Venue of cemetery companies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter C. Venue › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 727. Venue of cemetery companies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 727. Venue of cemetery companies (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise provided in Title 9 (relating to burial grounds) or prescribed
   by general rules, in exercising the jurisdiction of the court over the property or
   affairs of a domestic or foreign cemetery company in matters relating to burial grounds
   or to property held for the burial of the dead or for the care or adornment of burial
   grounds, the venue shall be in the county where the burial ground, or any part thereof
   is located or, in the absence of any involved burial grounds within this Commonwealth,
   in a county where any property held or controlled by the cemetery company is located.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 3. Ownership of Property; Legal Title and Equitable Estate›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 305. Right to dispose of a decedent's remains
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 3. Ownership of Property; Legal Title and Equitable Estate › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 305. Right to dispose of a decedent's remains
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 305. Right to dispose of a decedent's remains (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as specified in subsection (a.1), the determination of the final disposition
      of a decedent's remains shall be as set forth in this section unless otherwise specifically
      provided by waiver and agreement of the person entitled to make such determination
      under this section, subject to the provisions of a valid will executed by the decedent
      and sections 8611(a) (relating to persons who may execute anatomical gift) and 8654(1)
      (relating to requirement of explicit, specific and separate authorization).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 712. Nonmandatory exercise of jurisdiction through orphans' court division
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 712. Nonmandatory exercise of jurisdiction through orphans' court division
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 712. Nonmandatory exercise of jurisdiction through orphans' court division (2023)
content:
The jurisdiction of the court of common pleas over the following may be exercised
   through either its orphans' court division or other appropriate division:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter C. Venue›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 726. Venue of nonprofit corporations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter C. Venue › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 726. Venue of nonprofit corporations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 726. Venue of nonprofit corporations (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise prescribed by general rules, in exercising the jurisdiction of
   the court over the property or affairs of a domestic or foreign nonprofit corporation,
   the venue shall be in the county where the registered office of the corporation is
   located or deemed to be located for venue purposes or, in the absence of a registered
   office within this Commonwealth, in a county where any property held or controlled
   by the nonprofit corporation is located.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 3. Ownership of Property; Legal Title and Equitable Estate›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 302. Title to real and personal estate of an incapacitated person
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 3. Ownership of Property; Legal Title and Equitable Estate › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 302. Title to real and personal estate of an incapacitated person
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 302. Title to real and personal estate of an incapacitated person (2023)
content:
Legal title to all real estate and personal property of an incapacitated person shall
   remain in him, subject, however, to all the powers granted to his guardian by this
   title and lawfully by a governing instrument and to all orders of the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 3. Ownership of Property; Legal Title and Equitable Estate›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 301. Title to real and personal estate of a decedent
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 3. Ownership of Property; Legal Title and Equitable Estate › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 301. Title to real and personal estate of a decedent
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 301. Title to real and personal estate of a decedent (2023)
content:
(a) Personal estate.--Legal title to all personal estate of a decedent shall pass at his death to his
      personal representative, if any, as of the date of his death.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 3. Ownership of Property; Legal Title and Equitable Estate›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 303. Title to real and personal estate of a minor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 3. Ownership of Property; Legal Title and Equitable Estate › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 303. Title to real and personal estate of a minor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 303. Title to real and personal estate of a minor (2023)
content:
Legal title to all real and personal property of a minor shall remain in him, subject,
   however, to all the powers granted to his guardian by this title and lawfully by a
   governing instrument and to all orders of the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 714. Conflict of laws
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 714. Conflict of laws
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 714. Conflict of laws (2023)
content:
Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to interfere with the rules of law applicable
   to the determination of the question whether Pennsylvania courts have jurisdiction
   of the subject matters enumerated in this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter A. Organization›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 701. Orphans' court divisions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter A. Organization › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 701. Orphans' court divisions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 701. Orphans' court divisions (2023)
content:
Orphans' court divisions shall be organized as provided by Title 42 (relating to judiciary
   and judicial procedure).  Except as otherwise provided or prescribed by law, each orphans' court division
   shall possess the powers vested in the whole court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 1. Short Title and Definitions›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 102. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 1. Short Title and Definitions › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 102. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 102. Definitions (2023)
content:
Subject to additional definitions contained in subsequent provisions of this title
   which are applicable to specific provisions of this title, the following words and
   phrases when used in this title shall have, unless the context clearly indicates otherwise,
   the meanings given to them in this section:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter C. Venue›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 721. Venue of decedents', minors' and incapacitated persons' estates
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter C. Venue › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 721. Venue of decedents', minors' and incapacitated persons' estates
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 721. Venue of decedents', minors' and incapacitated persons' estates (2023)
content:
When a Pennsylvania court has jurisdiction of a decedent's, a minor's, or an incapacitated
   person's estate, except as otherwise provided by law, the venue for all purposes shall
   be as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter F. Masters, Auditors, Examiners, Guardians Ad Litem and Trustees Ad Litem›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 751. Appointment; purpose
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter F. Masters, Auditors, Examiners, Guardians Ad Litem and Trustees Ad Litem › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 751. Appointment; purpose
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 751. Appointment; purpose (2023)
content: The orphans' court division may appoint:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter E. Duties of the Clerk and Sheriff›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 745. Advertisement of accounts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter E. Duties of the Clerk and Sheriff › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 745. Advertisement of accounts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 745. Advertisement of accounts (2023)
content:
(a) Requirement of notice;  contents of notice.--The clerk of the orphans' court division shall give notice by advertisement of the
      time when accounts filed with him will be presented to the division for confirmation,
      stating in the advertisement the names and capacities of the respective accountants.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter F. Masters, Auditors, Examiners, Guardians Ad Litem and Trustees Ad Litem›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 752. Compensation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter F. Masters, Auditors, Examiners, Guardians Ad Litem and Trustees Ad Litem › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 752. Compensation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 752. Compensation (2023)
content:
The compensation of any master, auditor, examiner, guardian ad litem, or trustee ad
   litem, subject to any inconsistent general rule shall be paid from such source as
   the court shall direct.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter F. Masters, Auditors, Examiners, Guardians Ad Litem and Trustees Ad Litem›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 753. Subpoenas
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter F. Masters, Auditors, Examiners, Guardians Ad Litem and Trustees Ad Litem › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 753. Subpoenas
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 753. Subpoenas (2023)
content:
Masters, auditors and examiners shall have the power to issue subpoenas with or without
   a clause of duces tecum to witnesses to appear before them when necessary for the
   performance of any of their duties.  If any person who has been duly subpoenaed fails to obey the subpoena, the master,
   auditor, or examiner issuing the subpoena may report the neglect or refusal to the
   orphans' court division.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 761. Petitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 761. Petitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 761. Petitions (2023)
content:
All applications to the orphans' court division shall be by petition in the form prescribed
   by general rules and shall be attested either by an affidavit or by a verified statement.  In the case of the latter alternative, the statement shall set forth that it is
   subject to the penalties of18 Pa.C.S. § 4904(relating to unsworn falsification to authorities).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 762. Accounts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 762. Accounts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 762. Accounts (2023)
content:
The orphans' court division may decide or dispose of any question relating to the
   administration or distribution of an estate or trust and exercise any of its powers
   in respect thereof upon the filing of an account or in any other appropriate proceeding.  The account may be a complete accounting of the estate or trust or of only the transactions
   which raise the question to be determined.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 764. Citation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 764. Citation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 764. Citation (2023)
content:
Jurisdiction of the person shall be obtained by citation to be awarded by the orphans'
   court division upon application of any party in interest.  The citation shall direct the party named therein to file a complete answer under
   oath to the averments of the petition on or before a day certain, which shall be not
   less than ten days after the service thereof, and to show cause as the decree of the
   division shall provide.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 766. Proof of service
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 766. Proof of service
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 766. Proof of service (2023)
content:
Proof of service shall be by affidavit of the person or the return of the sheriff
   making service, and shall set forth the same information as a sheriff's return in
   an action of assumpsit.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 767. Parties in interest
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 767. Parties in interest
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 767. Parties in interest (2023)
content:
In any proceeding where the orphans' court division considers that the interests of
   any taxing authority, including the United States, any state and any political subdivision
   thereof, may be adversely affected directly or indirectly by a decision of such division
   because of the effect of such decision on assets subject to tax or for any other reason,
   the division shall have the power on its own motion or on the application of any party
   in interest, including the taxing authority, and upon such notice as it may direct,
   to authorize the taxing authority through its proper officer to appear as a party
   in interest, and if such an appearance is entered, the taxing authority shall be considered
   to be a party in interest aggrieved by any decision adversely affecting its interests.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 765. Service of citation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 765. Service of citation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 765. Service of citation (2023)
content:
A citation to obtain jurisdiction of a person may be served by an adult person, or
   by the sheriff of the county wherein the citation issued, or by deputization of the
   sheriff of the county where the service may be had in any county of the Commonwealth,
   in the same manner as a writ of summons in an action of assumpsit.  When no other time is specially fixed by the orphans' court division, the order
   awarding the citation shall be void unless the citation is issued within six months.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 901. Register's jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 901. Register's jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 901. Register's jurisdiction (2023)
content:
Within the county for which he has been elected or appointed, the register shall have
   jurisdiction of the probate of wills, the grant of letters to a personal representative,
   and any other matter as provided by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 776. Testimony in proceedings removed from register
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 776. Testimony in proceedings removed from register
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 776. Testimony in proceedings removed from register (2023)
content:
On appeal from the register, or in a proceeding removed from the register, the orphans'
   court division may find, upon the testimony taken before the register, that a substantial
   dispute of fact exists and grant a jury trial.  When upon the testimony taken before the register a jury trial is not granted, the
   division shall hear the testimony de novo unless all parties appearing in the proceeding
   agree that the case be heard on the testimony taken before the register.  In any event, the division may require witnesses already examined and other witnesses
   to appear before it.  The division, in its discretion, may impanel a jury at any stage of the proceedings.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 775. Perpetuation of testimony and court records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 775. Perpetuation of testimony and court records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 775. Perpetuation of testimony and court records (2023)
content:
The orphans' court division, by general rule or special order, may prescribe the practice
   relating to the perpetuation of testimony and to the perpetuation of lost or destroyed
   court records.  When proved, such court records shall have the same legal effect as original records
   would have had.  Notice of proceedings for the perpetuation of testimony and for the perpetuation
   of lost or destroyed court records shall be given in such manner as the division shall
   direct.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 768. Manner of service; proof
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 768. Manner of service; proof
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 768. Manner of service; proof (2023)
content:
Notice of any proceeding in an orphans' court division may be given within or outside
   the Commonwealth by personal service, by registered mail, by publication, or otherwise,
   as the division shall direct by general rule or special order.  Notice may be in the form of a citation served as provided in this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 778. Procedure for jury trials
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 778. Procedure for jury trials
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 778. Procedure for jury trials (2023)
content:
(a) Jury.--Jury trials in any case begun before or certified or appealed to an orphans' court
      division shall be tried in the division.  The division shall draw a jury and preside at the trial of the issue and shall have
      all the powers of a judge in trials by jury in cases at law.  The panel of jurors drawn for service in other divisions of the court shall be available
      for such service in the orphans' court division when required, and in judicial districts
      where there is a separate orphans' court division, the court of common pleas shall,
      by appropriate rules, provide for and regulate the manner in which the jurors shall
      be made available and sent to the orphans' court division when required for the trial
      of issues therein.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 777. Right to jury trial; discretion of orphans' court division
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 777. Right to jury trial; discretion of orphans' court division
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 777. Right to jury trial; discretion of orphans' court division (2023)
content:
(a) Title to property.--When a substantial dispute of fact shall arise concerning the decedent's title to
      property, real or personal, any party in interest shall be entitled to a trial of
      such issue by a jury.  The verdict of the jury shall have the same effect as the verdict of a jury in a
      case at law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 779. Nonsuits
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 779. Nonsuits
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 779. Nonsuits (2023)
content:
(a) In general.--The orphans' court division may enter a nonsuit under the same circumstances, subject
      to review in the same manner and with the same effect as in an action at law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 784. Procedure on execution on personal property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 784. Procedure on execution on personal property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 784. Procedure on execution on personal property (2023)
content:
Writs of execution on personal property shall be allowed by the orphans' court division
   and directed to and executed by the sheriff of the proper county.  The proceedings thereon shall be the same as on execution on personal property issued
   out of the division of the court having jurisdiction over actions at law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 774. Depositions and discovery
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 774. Depositions and discovery
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 774. Depositions and discovery (2023)
content:
The orphans' court division, by general rule or special order, may prescribe the practice
   relating to depositions, discovery, and the production of documents.  To the extent not provided for by general rule or special order, the practice relating
   to such matters shall conform to the practice in the division of the court having
   jurisdiction over actions at law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 781. Methods of enforcement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 781. Methods of enforcement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 781. Methods of enforcement (2023)
content:
Compliance with an order or decree of an orphans' court division may be enforced by
   attachment of the person;  sequestration of real or personal property;  execution
   on personal property;  attachment execution;  or execution on real estate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 783. Procedure on sequestration of real or personal property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 783. Procedure on sequestration of real or personal property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 783. Procedure on sequestration of real or personal property (2023)
content:
A writ of sequestration of real or personal property of an estate or trust, or of
   the respondent, to enforce an order or decree of the orphans' court division in the
   administration of the estate or trust shall be allowed by the orphans' court division
   as fully as in any court of equity, and shall be directed to and executed by the sheriff
   of the county in which the court or branch of the court is located or of any county
   where property to be sequestered is located.  The orphans' court division, by general rule or special order, may prescribe the
   practice relating to sequestration of real and personal property.  To the extent not provided for by general rule or special order, the practice relating
   to sequestration shall conform to the practice in the division of the court having
   jurisdiction over actions at law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 782. Procedure on attachment of the person
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 782. Procedure on attachment of the person
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 782. Procedure on attachment of the person (2023)
content:
(a) Direction of writs.--A writ of attachment of the person shall be directed to and executed by the sheriff
      of the county in which the court or branch of the court is located or of any county
      where the person to be attached is located.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 785. Procedure on attachment execution
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 785. Procedure on attachment execution
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 785. Procedure on attachment execution (2023)
content:
Writs of attachment execution shall be allowed by the orphans' court division and
   directed to and executed by the sheriff of the proper county.  The proceedings thereon shall be the same as attachment executions issued out of
   the division of the court having jurisdiction over actions at law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 786. Procedure on execution on real estate
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 786. Procedure on execution on real estate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 786. Procedure on execution on real estate (2023)
content:
(a) Filing.--The prothonotary of any court of common pleas shall, on demand of the fiduciary or
      of any party in interest, file and docket a certified transcript or extract from the
      record showing that an orphans' court division has adjudged an amount to be due by
      any person, and such transcripts or extract shall constitute a judgment of the court
      against such person from the time of its filing with the same effect as if it had
      been obtained in an action in the division of the court having jurisdiction over actions
      at law.  If the amount adjudged to be due shall be increased or decreased on appeal, the
      prothonotary shall, if the decree of the appellate court is certified to him, change
      his records accordingly, and if the appellate court has increased the amount, the
      excess shall constitute a judgment from the time when the records are so changed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 903. Witnesses; testimony
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 903. Witnesses; testimony
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 903. Witnesses; testimony (2023)
content: The register shall have power to:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 902. Deputy register
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 902. Deputy register
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 902. Deputy register (2023)
content:
Every register shall appoint a deputy or two deputies who shall have power to perform
   the duties of the office in his behalf and for whose conduct he and his surety shall
   be accountable.  In case of a vacancy in the office of register, the first deputy shall exercise
   all the powers of the register until a successor is appointed or elected.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 905. Enforcement of subpoenas, orders and costs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 905. Enforcement of subpoenas, orders and costs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 905. Enforcement of subpoenas, orders and costs (2023)
content:
Should any person refuse to comply with any subpoena or order of the register or to
   pay all costs, the register shall forthwith certify the record of the proceedings
   to the court.  The court, upon petition of any party in interest, shall compel payment of the costs
   and shall enforce obedience to the subpoena or order in the same manner as in cases
   of subpoenas and orders issued or made by the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 910. Transmission of accounts to the court
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 910. Transmission of accounts to the court
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 910. Transmission of accounts to the court (2023)
content:
All accounts filed with the register shall be transmitted to the court for audit and
   confirmation on dates fixed by the court by general rule or special order and shall
   be advertised as required by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions›Subchapter G. Procedure›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 793. Effect of appeal
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 7. Orphans' Court Divisions › Subchapter G. Procedure › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 793. Effect of appeal
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 793. Effect of appeal (2023)
content:
No appeal from an order or decree of an orphans' court division concerning the validity
   of a will or the right to administer shall suspend the powers or prejudice the acts
   of a personal representative acting thereunder.  The reversal or modification of any decree of an orphans' court division in a proceeding
   in which the division has jurisdiction of the sale, mortgage, exchange or conveyance
   of real or personal estate shall not divest any estate or interest acquired thereunder
   by a person not a party to the appeal.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 911. Attestation of certain applications and documents
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 911. Attestation of certain applications and documents
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 911. Attestation of certain applications and documents (2023)
content:
Except as provided otherwise in section 3154 (relating to affidavit and oath), applications
   and documents submitted to the register for which attestation is required may be attested
   either by an affidavit or by a verified statement.  In case of the latter alternative, the statement shall set forth that it is subject
   to the penalties of18 Pa.C.S. § 4904(relating to unsworn falsification to authorities).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 906. Caveat
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 906. Caveat
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 906. Caveat (2023)
content:
(a) Bond.--When a caveat has been filed, the register shall not delay the probate of a will or
      the grant of letters for more than ten days after the filing of the petition for probate
      or for the grant of letters, or after the filing of the caveat, whichever shall be
      later, unless within such ten-day period a party in interest shall file with the register
      his bond in the name of the Commonwealth with sufficient surety in such amount, not
      less than $500 or more than $5,000, as the register considers necessary, conditioned
      for the payment of any costs which may be decreed against the caveator.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 907. Certification of records to court
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 907. Certification of records to court
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 907. Certification of records to court (2023)
content:
Whenever a caveat shall be filed or a dispute shall arise before the register concerning
   the probate of a will, the grant of letters or the performance of any other function
   by the register, he may certify, or the court upon petition of any party in interest
   may direct the register at any stage of the proceedings to certify, the entire record
   to the court, which shall proceed to a determination of the issue in dispute.  No letters of administration pendente lite shall be granted by the register after
   proceedings have been removed to the court except by leave of court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 904. Witness fees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 904. Witness fees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 904. Witness fees (2023)
content:
Witnesses appearing before the register in obedience to the register's subpoena shall
   be entitled to the same fees and mileage as are allowed by law to witnesses in the
   orphans' court division.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 924. Recording proceedings in another county
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 924. Recording proceedings in another county
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 924. Recording proceedings in another county (2023)
content:
Copies of wills and probate proceedings and records of the grant of letters of administration
   and proceedings relating thereto, duly certified by the register, may be filed in
   the office of the register in any county where real estate of the decedent is located.  The register with whom such papers are filed shall forthwith record the same, and
   the record thereof shall be as valid and effectual in law as the original, or its
   duly certified copy, or its record would be for all purposes of vesting title, of
   evidence, and of notice.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 923. Certified copies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 923. Certified copies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 923. Certified copies (2023)
content:
Every register upon the request of any person paying the fee therefor, shall make
   and certify under the seal of his office true copies of his records or of papers filed
   with him or of proceedings before him.  Such certified copies shall be as good evidence as the original in any judicial
   proceeding in the Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 922. Inventories
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 922. Inventories
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 922. Inventories (2023)
content: The register shall index and record all inventories filed with him.  The recording may be accomplished by photographic or other mechanical process.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 908. Appeals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 908. Appeals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 908. Appeals (2023)
content:
(a) When allowed.--Any party in interest seeking to challenge the probate of a will or who is otherwise
      aggrieved by a decree of the register, or a fiduciary whose estate or trust is so
      aggrieved, may appeal therefrom to the court within one year of the decree:  Provided,
      That the executor designated in an instrument shall not by virtue of such designation
      be deemed a party in interest who may appeal from a decree refusing probate of it.  The court, upon petition of a party in interest, may limit the time for appeal to
      three months.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 921. Wills
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 921. Wills
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 921. Wills (2023)
content:
All probated wills shall be indexed and recorded by the register, and shall remain
   in his office, except for the period required to be in the custody of a higher court.  The recording may be accomplished by photographic or other mechanical process.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2102. Share of surviving spouse
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2102. Share of surviving spouse
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2102. Share of surviving spouse (2023)
content: The intestate share of a decedent's surviving spouse is:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 925. Certificates and affidavits of death
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 925. Certificates and affidavits of death
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 925. Certificates and affidavits of death (2023)
content:
Where it is not necessary to have letters granted to administer a decedent's estate
   but it is desired to have a public record of his death, a certificate of death may
   be filed with the register except that where a certificate of death cannot be obtained
   the affidavit of a relative or other interested party may be filed with the register
   setting forth the decedent's name, residence, date, time and place of death, and age
   at death.  The register shall index and record all such certificates and affidavits filed with
   him.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2101. Intestate estate
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2101. Intestate estate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2101. Intestate estate (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--All or any part of the estate of a decedent not effectively disposed of by will or
      otherwise passes to his heirs as prescribed in this chapter, except as modified by
      the decedent's will.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2103. Shares of others than surviving spouse
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2103. Shares of others than surviving spouse
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2103. Shares of others than surviving spouse (2023)
content:
The share of the estate, if any, to which the surviving spouse is not entitled, and
   the entire estate if there is no surviving spouse, shall pass in the following order:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2105. Spouse's rights
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2105. Spouse's rights
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2105. Spouse's rights (2023)
content:
(a) Widow.--The share of the estate to which a widow is entitled under this title shall be in
      lieu and full satisfaction of her dower at common law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2104. Rules of succession
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2104. Rules of succession
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2104. Rules of succession (2023)
content:
The provisions of this chapter shall be applied to both real and personal estate in
   accordance with the following rules:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2106. Forfeiture
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2106. Forfeiture
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2106. Forfeiture (2023)
content: (a) Spouse's share.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2110. Spouse's allowance; procedure
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2110. Spouse's allowance; procedure
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2110. Spouse's allowance; procedure (2023)
content:
The allowance shall be set aside and awarded in distribution to the surviving spouse,
   or his successor in interest, in the same manner as other distributive shares of the
   estate are awarded, without any right in the surviving spouse to choose particular
   real or personal property in satisfaction thereof.  Nothing herein shall be construed as limiting the right of the surviving spouse
   and other distributees to demand that property, not theretofore sold, be distributed
   in kind to them.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2107. Persons born out of wedlock
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2107. Persons born out of wedlock
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2107. Persons born out of wedlock (2023)
content:
(a) Child of mother.--For purposes of descent by, from and through a person born out of wedlock, he shall
      be considered the child of his mother.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2109.1. Advancements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2109.1. Advancements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2109.1. Advancements (2023)
content:
If a person dies intestate as to all or any part of his estate, property which he
   gave in his lifetime to an heir is treated as an advancement against the latter's
   share of the estate only if declared in a writing by the decedent or acknowledged
   in writing by the heir to be an advancement.  For this purpose the property advanced is valued as of the time the heir came into
   possession or enjoyment of the property or as of the time of death of the decedent,
   whichever first occurs.  If the recipient of the property fails to survive the decedent, the property is
   not taken into account in computing the intestate share to be received by the recipient's
   issue unless the declaration or acknowledgment so provides.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2201. Definition of conveyance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2201. Definition of conveyance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2201. Definition of conveyance (2023)
content:
As used in this chapter, unless the context clearly indicates otherwise, “conveyance” means an act by which it is intended to create an interest in real or personal property
   whether the act is intended to have inter vivos or testamentary operation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2203. Right of election; resident decedent
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2203. Right of election; resident decedent
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2203. Right of election; resident decedent (2023)
content:
(a) Property subject to election.--Except as provided in subsection (c), when a married person domiciled in this Commonwealth
      dies, his surviving spouse has a right to an elective share of one-third of the following
      property:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2108. Adopted person
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2108. Adopted person
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2108. Adopted person (2023)
content:
For purposes of inheritance by, from and through an adopted person he shall be considered
   the issue of his adopting parent or parents.  An adopted person shall not be considered as continuing to be the child or issue
   of his natural parents except in distributing the estate of a natural kin, other than
   the natural parent, who has maintained a family relationship with the adopted person.  If a natural parent shall have married the adopting parent, the adopted person for
   purposes of inheritance by, from and through him shall also be considered the issue
   of such natural parent.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2502. Form and execution of a will
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2502. Form and execution of a will
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2502. Form and execution of a will (2023)
content:
Every will shall be in writing and shall be signed by the testator at the end thereof,
   subject to the following rules and exceptions:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2205. Transfers for value excluded
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2205. Transfers for value excluded
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2205. Transfers for value excluded (2023)
content:
Conveyances and contracts made by the decedent are excluded from the provisions of
   section 2203 (relating to right of election;  resident decedent) and section 2204
   (relating to disclaimers, releases and charges against elective share), to the extent
   that the decedent received adequate consideration therefor in money or money's worth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2202. Right of election; nonresident decedent
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2202. Right of election; nonresident decedent
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2202. Right of election; nonresident decedent (2023)
content:
When a married person not domiciled in this Commonwealth dies, the rights, if any,
   of his surviving spouse to an elective share in property in this Commonwealth are
   governed by the laws of the decedent's domicile at death, but the rights of the electing
   spouse shall be subject to the rights of fiduciaries, custodians and obligors within
   this Commonwealth and transferees for value of and holders of liens for value on real
   estate or tangible personal property located in this Commonwealth under section 2211
   (relating to determination of effect of election;  enforcement).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2206. Right of election personal to surviving spouse
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2206. Right of election personal to surviving spouse
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2206. Right of election personal to surviving spouse (2023)
content:
The right of election of the surviving spouse may be exercised in whole or in part
   only during his lifetime by him or by his agent in accordance with section 5603(d)
   (relating to implementation of power of attorney).  In the case of a minor spouse, the right of election may be exercised in whole or
   in part only by the spouse's guardian;  in the case of an incapacitated spouse, the
   right of election may be exercised in whole or in part only by the spouse's guardian
   or by his agent in accordance with section 5603(d) if the power of attorney qualifies
   as a durable power of attorney under section 5604 (relating to durable powers of attorney);
   provided, that, in each case, the election shall be exercised only upon order of the
   court having jurisdiction of the minor's or the incapacitated person's estate, after
   finding that exercise of the right is advisable.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2208. Forfeiture of right of election
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2208. Forfeiture of right of election
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2208. Forfeiture of right of election (2023)
content:
A surviving spouse who under the provisions of section 2106 (relating to forfeiture)
   would not be entitled to a share of the decedent's estate had he died intestate shall
   have no right of election.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2204. Disclaimers, releases and charges against elective share
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2204. Disclaimers, releases and charges against elective share
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2204. Disclaimers, releases and charges against elective share (2023)
content:
(a) Disclaimers.--Except as provided in subsections (b) and (c), an election by a spouse to take his
      elective share shall be deemed a disclaimer of any beneficial interest of the spouse
      in the following, to the extent that such interest would otherwise be payable to or
      enjoyed by the spouse after the decedent's death:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2209. Surviving spouse as witness
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2209. Surviving spouse as witness
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2209. Surviving spouse as witness (2023)
content:
A person who is or claims to be the surviving spouse shall be a competent witness
   as to all matters pertinent to his rights under this chapter other than the creation
   of his status as the surviving spouse.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2207. Waiver of right to elect
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2207. Waiver of right to elect
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2207. Waiver of right to elect (2023)
content:
The right of election of a surviving spouse may be waived, wholly or partially, before
   or after marriage or before or after the death of the decedent.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2501. Who may make a will
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2501. Who may make a will
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2501. Who may make a will (2023)
content: Any person 18 or more years of age who is of sound mind may make a will.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2504.1. Validity of execution
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2504.1. Validity of execution
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2504.1. Validity of execution (2023)
content:
A will is validly executed if executed in compliance with section 2502 (relating to
   form and execution of a will), or in compliance with the law of the jurisdiction where
   the testator was domiciled at the time of the execution of the will or at the time
   of his death.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2505. Revocation of a will
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2505. Revocation of a will
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2505. Revocation of a will (2023)
content:
No will or codicil in writing, or any part thereof, can be revoked or altered otherwise
   than:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2507. Modification by circumstances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2507. Modification by circumstances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2507. Modification by circumstances (2023)
content:
Wills shall be modified upon the occurrence of any of the following circumstances,
   among others:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2210. Procedure for election; time limit
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2210. Procedure for election; time limit
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2210. Procedure for election; time limit (2023)
content:
(a) How election made.--A surviving spouse's election to take or not to take his elective share shall be
      by a writing signed by him and filed with the clerk of the orphans' court division
      of the county where the decedent died domiciled.  Notice of the election shall be given to the decedent's personal representative,
      if any.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2514. Rules of interpretation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2514. Rules of interpretation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2514. Rules of interpretation (2023)
content:
In the absence of a contrary intent appearing therein, wills shall be construed as
   to real and personal estate in accordance with the following rules:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2506. Revival of revoked or invalid will
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2506. Revival of revoked or invalid will
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2506. Revival of revoked or invalid will (2023)
content:
If, after the making of any will, the testator shall execute a later will which expressly
   or by necessary implication revokes the earlier will, the revocation of the later
   will shall not revive the earlier will, unless the revocation is in writing and declares
   the intention of the testator to revive the earlier will, or unless, after such revocation,
   the earlier will shall be reexecuted.  Oral republication of itself shall be ineffective to revive a will.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2211. Determination of effect of election; enforcement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2211. Determination of effect of election; enforcement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2211. Determination of effect of election; enforcement (2023)
content:
(a) Power of court of domicile.--After notice and hearing, the orphans' court division of the county of the decedent's
      domicile shall determine all matters concerning the spouse's election, including the
      interests and liabilities of the spouse and others in or with respect to all property,
      regardless of its situs, which is subject to the election or which must be disclaimed,
      released or conveyed by the spouse or charged against the elective share.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2515. Devise or bequest to trust
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2515. Devise or bequest to trust
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2515. Devise or bequest to trust (2023)
content:
A devise or bequest in a will may be made to the trustee of a trust, including any
   unfunded trust, established in writing by the testator or any other person before,
   concurrently with or after the execution of the will.  Such devise or bequest shall not be invalid because the trust is amendable or revocable,
   or both, or because the trust was amended after execution of the will.  Unless the will provides otherwise, the property so devised or bequeathed shall
   not be deemed held under a testamentary trust of the testator but shall become and
   be a part of the principal of the trust to which it is given to be administered and
   disposed of in accordance with the provisions of the instrument establishing that
   trust and any amendment thereof.  An entire revocation of the trust prior to the testator's death shall invalidate
   the devise or bequest unless the will directs otherwise.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2518. Alienage
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2518. Alienage
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2518. Alienage (2023)
content:
Real and personal estate shall pass without regard to whether the testator or any
   devisee or legatee is or has been an alien.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2517. Rule in Shelley's case and doctrine of worthier title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2517. Rule in Shelley's case and doctrine of worthier title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2517. Rule in Shelley's case and doctrine of worthier title (2023)
content:
(a) Rule in Shelley's case.--The rule in Shelley's case and its corollaries shall not be applied, and a devise
      or bequest directly or in trust which shall express an intent to create an estate
      for life with remainder to the life tenant's heirs or the heirs of his body or his
      issue or his next of kin or persons described by words of similar import shall not
      operate to give such life tenant an estate in fee in real estate or an absolute estate
      in personalty.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2516. Devise in fee tail abolished
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2516. Devise in fee tail abolished
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2516. Devise in fee tail abolished (2023)
content:
Whenever by any devise an estate in fee tail would be created according to the common
   law of the Commonwealth, it shall pass an estate in fee simple, and as such shall
   be inheritable and freely alienable.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter A. Dispositions Independent of Letters›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3101. Payments to family and funeral directors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter A. Dispositions Independent of Letters › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3101. Payments to family and funeral directors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3101. Payments to family and funeral directors (2023)
content:
(a) Wages, salary or employee benefits.--Any employer of a person dying domiciled in this Commonwealth at any time after the
      death of the employee, whether or not a personal representative has been appointed,
      may pay wages, salary or any employee benefits due the deceased in an amount not exceeding
      $10,000 to the spouse, any child, the father or mother, or any sister or brother (preference
      being given in the order named) of the deceased employee.  Any employer making such a payment shall be released to the same extent as if payment
      had been made to a duly appointed personal representative of the decedent and he shall
      not be required to see to the application thereof.  Any person to whom payment is made shall be answerable therefor to anyone prejudiced
      by an improper distribution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2521. Penalty clause for contest
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2521. Penalty clause for contest
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2521. Penalty clause for contest (2023)
content:
A provision in a will or trust purporting to penalize an interested person for contesting
   the will or trust or instituting other proceedings relating to the estate or trust
   is unenforceable if probable cause exists for instituting proceedings.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2519. Testamentary guardian
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2519. Testamentary guardian
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2519. Testamentary guardian (2023)
content:
(a) Guardian of the person.--A person competent to make a will, being the sole surviving parent or adopting parent
      of any unmarried minor child, may appoint a testamentary guardian of the person of
      such child during his minority, or for any shorter period except that no parent who,
      for one year or upwards previous to his death, shall have willfully neglected or refused
      to provide for his child, or who, for a like period, shall have deserted the child
      or willfully failed to perform parental duties, shall have the right to appoint a
      testamentary guardian of the person of such child.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 28. Formula Clauses for Federal Tax Purposes›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2802. Interpretation of formula clauses
