path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 61. Estates›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108. Designation of beneficiaries of insurance or employee death benefits not testamentary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 61. Estates › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108. Designation of beneficiaries of insurance or employee death benefits not testamentary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108. Designation of beneficiaries of insurance or employee death benefits not testamentary (2023)
content:
(a) In general.--The designation of beneficiaries of life insurance, annuity or endowment contracts,
      or of any agreement entered into by an insurance company in connection therewith,
      supplemental thereto or in settlement thereof, and the designation of beneficiaries
      of benefits payable upon or after the death of a participant under any pension, bonus,
      profit-sharing, retirement annuity, or other employee-benefit plan, shall not be considered
      testamentary and shall not be subject to any law governing the transfer of property
      by will.  This section shall apply regardless of whether the insurance contract or the employee-benefit
      plan designates the ultimate beneficiaries or makes the proceeds payable, directly
      or indirectly, to a trustee of a trust under a will or under a separate trust instrument
      which designates the ultimate beneficiaries, and regardless of whether any such trust
      is amendable or revocable, or both, or is funded or unfunded, and notwithstanding
      a reservation to the settlor of all rights of ownership in the insurance contracts
      or under the employee-benefit plans.   Unless otherwise expressly provided in the conveyance, funds or other property
      so passing to a trust under a will shall become and be a part of the testamentary
      trust to be administered and disposed of in accordance with the provisions thereof,
      without forming any part of the testator's estate for administration by his personal
      representative.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 61. Estates›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6115. Estates pur autre vie
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 61. Estates › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6115. Estates pur autre vie
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6115. Estates pur autre vie (2023)
content:
An interest conveyed to a person for the life of another, whether or not such conveyance
   is to him and his heirs, shall, on his death before expiration of the interest, be
   considered as personal property forming a part of his estate and shall be subject
   to distribution in like manner as a lease for a term of years.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 61. Estates › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6116. Estates in fee tail abolished

content:

   common law of the Commonwealth, it shall pass an estate in fee simple, and as such
   shall be inheritable and freely alienable.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 62. Disclaimers›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6202. Disclaimers by fiduciaries or agents
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 62. Disclaimers › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6202. Disclaimers by fiduciaries or agents
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6202. Disclaimers by fiduciaries or agents (2023)
content:
A disclaimer on behalf of a decedent, a minor or an incapacitated person may be made
   by his personal representative, the guardian of his estate or in the case of an incapacitated
   person who executed a power of attorney which confers the authority to disclaim upon
   his agent and which qualifies as a durable power of attorney under section 5604 (relating
   to durable powers of attorney) by such agent, if, in each case, the court having jurisdiction
   of the estate authorizes the disclaimer after finding that it is advisable and will
   not materially prejudice the rights of creditors, heirs or beneficiaries of the decedent,
   the minor or his creditors, or the incapacitated person or his creditors, as the case
   may be.  A personal representative may make a disclaimer on behalf of his decedent without
   court authorization if the will of the decedent so authorizes him.

(a) Acceptance.--A disclaimer may be made at any time before acceptance.  An acceptance may be express or may be inferred from actions of the person entitled
      to receive an interest in property such as the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 62. Disclaimers›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6201. Right to disclaim
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 62. Disclaimers › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6201. Right to disclaim
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6201. Right to disclaim (2023)
content:
A person to whom an interest in property would have devolved by whatever means, including
   a beneficiary under a will, an appointee under the exercise of a power of appointment,
   a person entitled to take by intestacy, a joint tenant with right of survivorship,
   a donee of an inter vivos transfer, a donee under a third-party beneficiary contract
   (including beneficiaries of life insurance and annuity policies and pension, profit-sharing
   and other employee benefit plans), and a person entitled to a disclaimed interest,
   may disclaim it in whole or in part by a written disclaimer which shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 62. Disclaimers›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6205. Effect of disclaimer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 62. Disclaimers › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6205. Effect of disclaimer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6205. Effect of disclaimer (2023)
content:
(a) In general.--A disclaimer relates back for all purposes to the date of the death of the decedent
      or the effective date of the inter vivos transfer or third-party beneficiary contract
      as the case may be.  The disclaimer shall not in any way diminish the interest of any person other than
      the disclaimant in such person's own right under the instrument creating the disclaimed
      interest or under the intestate laws nor diminish any interest to which such person
      becomes entitled under subsection (b) by reason of the disclaimer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 62. Disclaimers›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6203. Interests subject to disclaimer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 62. Disclaimers › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6203. Interests subject to disclaimer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6203. Interests subject to disclaimer (2023)
content:
A disclaimer in whole or in part may be made of any present or future interest, vested
   or contingent, including a possible future right to take as an appointee under an
   unexercised power of appointment or under a discretionary power to distribute income
   or principal.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 61. Estates›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6117. Rule in Shelley's case and doctrine of worthier title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 61. Estates › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6117. Rule in Shelley's case and doctrine of worthier title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6117. Rule in Shelley's case and doctrine of worthier title (2023)
content:
(a) Rule in Shelley's case.--The rule in Shelley's case and its corollaries shall not be applied, and a conveyance
      directly or in trust which shall express an intent to create an estate for life with
      remainder to the life tenant's heirs or the heirs of his body or his issue or his
      next of kin or persons described by words of similar import, shall not operate to
      give such life tenant an estate in fee in real estate or an absolute estate in personalty.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 62. Disclaimers›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6207. Other statutes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 62. Disclaimers › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6207. Other statutes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6207. Other statutes (2023)
content:
The provisions of this chapter do not abridge the right of a person to disclaim interests
   under any other statute and do not affect any additional requirements for a disclaimer
   to be effective for inheritance tax purposes or other purposes covered specifically
   in other statutory provisions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 62. Disclaimers›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6204. Filing, delivery and recording
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 62. Disclaimers › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6204. Filing, delivery and recording
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6204. Filing, delivery and recording (2023)
content:
(a) Will or intestacy.--If the interest would have devolved to the disclaimant by will or by intestacy,
      the disclaimer shall be filed with the clerk of the orphans' court division of the
      county where the decedent died domiciled or, if the decedent was not domiciled in
      this Commonwealth, of the county where the property involved is located, and a copy
      of the disclaimer shall be delivered to any personal representative, trustee or other
      fiduciary in possession of the property.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 63. Multiple-Party Accounts›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6303. Ownership during lifetime
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 63. Multiple-Party Accounts › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6303. Ownership during lifetime
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6303. Ownership during lifetime (2023)
content:
(a) Joint account.--A joint account belongs, during the lifetime of all parties, to the parties in proportion
      to the net contributions by each to the sum on deposit, unless there is clear and
      convincing evidence of a different intent.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 63. Multiple-Party Accounts›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6301. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 63. Multiple-Party Accounts › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6301. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6301. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this chapter shall have, unless the context
   clearly indicates otherwise, the meanings given to them in this section:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 63. Multiple-Party Accounts›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6304. Right of survivorship
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 63. Multiple-Party Accounts › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6304. Right of survivorship
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6304. Right of survivorship (2023)
content:
(a) Joint account.--Any sum remaining on deposit at the death of a party to a joint account belongs
      to the surviving party or parties as against the estate of the decedent unless there
      is clear and convincing evidence of a different intent at the time the account is
      created.  If there are two or more surviving parties, their respective ownerships during lifetime
      shall be in proportion to their previous ownership interests under section 6303 (relating
      to ownership during lifetime) augmented by an equal per capita share for each survivor
      of any interest the decedent may have owned in the account immediately before his
      death;  and the right of survivorship continues between the surviving parties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6401. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6401. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6401. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this chapter shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 63. Multiple-Party Accounts›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6302. Applicability of chapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 63. Multiple-Party Accounts › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6302. Applicability of chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6302. Applicability of chapter (2023)
content:
The provisions of this chapter are applicable solely to the determination of property
   rights among parties to multiple-party accounts and all claims made through them but
   do not apply to and do not affect financial institutions or their rights and liabilities
   with respect to multiple-party accounts, which shall be determined exclusively by
   applicable law other than this chapter.  No right or claim against a financial institution may be based on this chapter.  Nothing in this chapter shall affect the taxability of transfers under the act of
   June 15, 1961 (P.L. 373, No. 207), known as the “Inheritance and Estate Tax Act of
   1961.”1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6402. Registration in beneficiary form
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6402. Registration in beneficiary form
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6402. Registration in beneficiary form (2023)
content:
Only individuals whose registration of a security shows sole ownership by one individual
   or multiple ownership by two or more with right of survivorship, rather than as tenants
   in common, may obtain registration in beneficiary form.  Multiple owners of a security registered in beneficiary form hold as joint tenants
   with right of survivorship, as tenants by the entireties or as owners of community
   property held in survivorship form and not as tenants in common.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 63. Multiple-Party Accounts›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6306. Accounts and transfers nontestamentary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 63. Multiple-Party Accounts › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6306. Accounts and transfers nontestamentary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6306. Accounts and transfers nontestamentary (2023)
content:
No transfer resulting from the application of section 6304 (relating to right of survivorship)
   shall be considered as testamentary or subject to Chapter 21 (relating to intestate
   succession) or Chapter 25 (relating to wills).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 63. Multiple-Party Accounts›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6305. Form of account
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 63. Multiple-Party Accounts › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6305. Form of account
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6305. Form of account (2023)
content:
The applicability of the provisions of section 6304 (relating to right of survivorship)
   is determined by the form of the account at the death of a party.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6404. Origination of registration in beneficiary form
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6404. Origination of registration in beneficiary form
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6404. Origination of registration in beneficiary form (2023)
content:
A security, whether evidenced by certificate or account, is registered in beneficiary
   form when the registration includes a designation of a beneficiary, which may include
   a trustee of a trust, to take the ownership at the death of the owner or the deaths
   of all multiple owners.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6406. Effect of registration in beneficiary form
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6406. Effect of registration in beneficiary form
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6406. Effect of registration in beneficiary form (2023)
content:
The designation of a TOD beneficiary on a registration in beneficiary form has no
   effect on ownership until the owner's death.  A registration of a security in beneficiary form may be canceled or changed at any
   time by the sole owner or all then surviving owners, without the consent of the beneficiary.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6405. Form of registration in beneficiary form
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6405. Form of registration in beneficiary form
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6405. Form of registration in beneficiary form (2023)
content:
Registration in beneficiary form may be shown by the words “transfer on death” or
   the acronym “TOD,” or by the words “pay on death” or the acronym “POD,” after the
   name of the registered owner and before the name of a beneficiary.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6411. Transfers of securities and security accounts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6411. Transfers of securities and security accounts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6411. Transfers of securities and security accounts (2023)
content:
(a) Payment of inheritance tax.--No corporation, financial institution, broker or similar entity shall transfer on
      its books or issue a new certificate for any share of its capital stock, its registered
      bonds, a security or a security account, belonging to or standing in the name of a
      resident decedent, belonging to or standing in the joint names of a resident decedent
      and one or more persons, held in trust by or for a resident decedent or in a beneficiary
      form indicating that a resident decedent was the present owner or became the owner
      upon the death of another, unless the inheritance tax upon the transfer has actually
      been paid, or the written consent of the Secretary of Revenue, or its designee, is
      first secured, or there is presented to it an affidavit of the personal representative
      or heir of the decedent, or his or their attorney, that the decedent was a nonresident
      at the time of his death, or that the person in whose name said security, security
      account, shares of registered bond stands jointly with the decedent by right of survivorship
      was the spouse of the decedent at the time of death and that the ownership in or designation
      of such spouse was not created within one year before the decedent's death, or written
      notification of the transfer is given to the Secretary of Revenue within ten days
      of the transfer as provided in subsection (d).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6407. Ownership on death of owner
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6407. Ownership on death of owner
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6407. Ownership on death of owner (2023)
content:
On death of a sole owner or the last to die of all multiple owners, ownership of securities
   registered in beneficiary form passes to the beneficiary or beneficiaries who survive
   all owners.  On proof of death of all owners and compliance with any applicable requirements
   of the registering entity, a security registered in beneficiary form may be reregistered
   in the name of the beneficiary or beneficiaries who survived the death of all owners.  Until division of the security after the death of all owners, multiple beneficiaries
   surviving the death of all owners hold their interests as tenants in common.  If no beneficiary survives the death of all owners, the security belongs to the
   estate of the deceased sole owner or the estate of the last to die of all multiple
   owners.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6403. Law applicable to registration
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6403. Law applicable to registration
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6403. Law applicable to registration (2023)
content:
A security may be registered in beneficiary form if the form is authorized by this
   or a similar statute of the state of organization of the issuer or registering entity,
   the location of the registering entity's principal office, the office of its transfer
   agent or its office making the registration or by this or a similar statute of the
   law of the state listed as the owner's address at the time of registration.  A registration governed by the law of a jurisdiction in which this or similar legislation
   is not in force or was not in force when a registration in beneficiary form was made
   is nevertheless presumed to be valid and authorized as a matter of contract law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6410. Terms, conditions and forms for registration
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6410. Terms, conditions and forms for registration
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6410. Terms, conditions and forms for registration (2023)
content:
(a) Terms and conditions.--A registering entity offering to accept registrations in beneficiary form may establish
      the terms and conditions under which it will receive requests for registrations in
      beneficiary form and for implementation of registrations in beneficiary form, including
      requests for cancellation of previously registered TOD beneficiary designations and
      requests for reregistration to effect a change of beneficiary.  The terms and conditions so established may provide for proving death, avoiding
      or resolving any problems concerning fractional shares, designating primary and contingent
      beneficiaries and substituting a named beneficiary's descendants to take in the place
      of the named beneficiary in the event of the beneficiary's death.  Substitution may be indicated by appending to the name of the primary beneficiary
      the letters “LDPS,” standing for “lineal descendants per stirpes.”  This designation substitutes a deceased beneficiary's descendants who survive the
      owner for a beneficiary who fails to so survive, the descendants to be identified
      and to share in accordance with the law of the beneficiary's domicile at the owner's
      death governing inheritance by descendants of an intestate.  Other forms of identifying beneficiaries who are to take on one or more contingencies,
      and rules for providing proofs and assurances needed to satisfy reasonable concerns
      by registering entities regarding conditions and identities relevant to accurate implementation
      of registrations in beneficiary form, may be contained in a registering entity's terms
      and conditions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6409. Nontestamentary transfer on death
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6409. Nontestamentary transfer on death
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6409. Nontestamentary transfer on death (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A transfer on death resulting from a registration in beneficiary form is effective
      by reason of the contract regarding the registration between the owner and the registering
      entity and this chapter and is not testamentary.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6412. Construction of chapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6412. Construction of chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6412. Construction of chapter (2023)
content:
This chapter shall be liberally construed and applied to promote its underlying purposes
   and policy and to make uniform the laws with respect to the subject of this chapter
   among states enacting it.  Unless displaced by the particular provisions of this chapter, the principles of
   law and equity supplement its provisions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6408. Protection of registering entity
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6408. Protection of registering entity
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6408. Protection of registering entity (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A registering entity is not required to offer or to accept a request for security
      registration in beneficiary form.  If a registration in beneficiary form is offered by a registering entity, the owner
      requesting registration in beneficiary form assents to the protections given to the
      registering entity by this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 72. Prudent Investor Rule›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7201. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 72. Prudent Investor Rule › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7201. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7201. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this chapter shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6413. Application of chapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 64. Transfer on Death Security Registration › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6413. Application of chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 6413. Application of chapter (2023)
content:
This chapter applies to registration of securities in beneficiary form made before
   or after the effective date of this chapter by decedents dying on or after the effective
   date of this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 72. Prudent Investor Rule›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7203. Prudent investor rule
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 72. Prudent Investor Rule › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7203. Prudent investor rule
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7203. Prudent investor rule (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A fiduciary shall invest and manage property held in a trust as a prudent investor
      would, by considering the purposes, terms and other circumstances of the trust and
      by pursuing an overall investment strategy reasonably suited to the trust.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 72. Prudent Investor Rule›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7204. Diversification
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 72. Prudent Investor Rule › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7204. Diversification
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7204. Diversification (2023)
content:
(a) Requirement.--Except as provided in section 7205 (relating to retention of inception assets), a
      fiduciary shall reasonably diversify investments, unless the fiduciary reasonably
      determines that it is in the interests of the beneficiaries not to diversify, taking
      into account the purposes, terms and other circumstances of the trust and the requirements
      of this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 72. Prudent Investor Rule›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7202. Default rule
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 72. Prudent Investor Rule › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7202. Default rule
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7202. Default rule (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided by the governing instrument, a fiduciary shall invest
      and manage property held in a trust in accordance with the provisions of this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 72. Prudent Investor Rule›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7205. Retention of inception assets
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 72. Prudent Investor Rule › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7205. Retention of inception assets
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7205. Retention of inception assets (2023)
content:
A fiduciary, in the exercise of reasonable care, skill and caution, may retain any
   asset received in kind, even though the asset constitutes a disproportionally large
   share of the portfolio.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 72. Prudent Investor Rule›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7208. Life insurance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 72. Prudent Investor Rule › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7208. Life insurance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7208. Life insurance (2023)
content:
A trustee may acquire or retain a contract of life insurance upon the life of the
   settlor or the settlor's spouse, or both, without liability for a loss arising from
   the trustee's failure to:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 72. Prudent Investor Rule›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7206. Delegation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 72. Prudent Investor Rule › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7206. Delegation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7206. Delegation (2023)
content:
(a) Permissible delegation.--A fiduciary may delegate investment and management functions that a prudent investor
      of comparable skills might delegate under the circumstances.

content:
Notwithstanding that a bank or trust company or an affiliate provides services to
   the investment company or investment trust, including that of an investment advisor,
   custodian, transfer agent, registrar, sponsor, distributor or manager, and receives
   reasonable compensation for those services and notwithstanding any other provision

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 73. Municipalities Investments›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7301. Definition of fiduciary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 73. Municipalities Investments › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7301. Definition of fiduciary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7301. Definition of fiduciary (2023)
content:
The term“fiduciary”as used in this chapter shall include an administrator of a municipal pension or
   retirement plan and any other person whose fiduciary duties are, by statute, governed
   by the principles of this chapter.  The provisions of this chapter shall apply only to such fiduciaries.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 72. Prudent Investor Rule›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7213. Judgment of fiduciary's decisions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 72. Prudent Investor Rule › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7213. Judgment of fiduciary's decisions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7213. Judgment of fiduciary's decisions (2023)
content:
The rules of this chapter are standards of conduct and not of outcome or performance.  Compliance with the rules of this chapter shall be determined in light of the facts
   and circumstances prevailing at the time of the fiduciary's decision or action and
   not by hindsight.  A fiduciary is not liable to the extent the fiduciary acted in substantial compliance
   with the rules of this chapter or in reasonable reliance on the terms and provisions
   of the governing instrument.  A fiduciary's investment and management decisions respecting individual assets shall
   be considered in the context of the trust portfolio as a whole and as part of an overall
   investment strategy, and not in isolation.  No specific investment or course of action, taken alone, shall be considered inherently
   prudent or imprudent.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 72. Prudent Investor Rule›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7214. Language invoking chapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 72. Prudent Investor Rule › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7214. Language invoking chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7214. Language invoking chapter (2023)
content:
The following terms or words or words of similar import in the provisions of a trust,
   unless otherwise limited or modified, shall authorize any investment or investment
   strategy permitted under this chapter:  “investments permissible by law for investment
   of trust funds,” “legal investments,” “authorized investments,” “using the judgment
   and care under the circumstances then prevailing that persons of prudence, discretion
   and intelligence exercise in the management of their own affairs, not in regard to
   speculation but in regard to the permanent disposition of their own funds, considering
   the probable income as well as the probable safety of their capital,” “prudent man
   rule,” “prudent trustee rule,” “prudent person rule” and “prudent investor rule.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 73. Municipalities Investments›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7302. Authorized investments; in general
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 73. Municipalities Investments › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7302. Authorized investments; in general
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7302. Authorized investments; in general (2023)
content:
(a) Specifically authorized.--Subject only to the provisions of the governing instrument, if any, a fiduciary may
      accept, hold, invest in, and retain, any of the investments authorized by this chapter,
      and shall not be liable for loss on such investments so long as he exercises due care
      and prudence in the performance of his duties in regard to them.  “Legal investment” or “authorized investment” or words of similar import used in a trust instrument shall be construed to mean
      any investment authorized by this chapter.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7211. Further investment authority (2023)
content:
Unless a contrary intent is clearly expressed in the instrument, the authority to
   invest in specified types of investments includes authorization to invest in a mutual
   fund, or in any common or collective trust fund established and maintained by a corporate
   fiduciary, or by any affiliate of a corporate fiduciary within the meaning ofsection 1504 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986(Public Law 99-514,26 U.S.C. § 1504) or any successor provision, if the portfolio of the mutual fund or of the common
   or collective trust fund consists of the specified types of investments and is otherwise
   in conformity with the laws of this Commonwealth and of the United States.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 73. Municipalities Investments›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7306. Obligations of governmental organizations existing pursuant to the laws of Pennsylvania, other states and the District of Columbia
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 73. Municipalities Investments › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7306. Obligations of governmental organizations existing pursuant to the laws of Pennsylvania, other states and the District of Columbia
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7306. Obligations of governmental organizations existing pursuant to the laws of Pennsylvania, other states and the District of Columbia (2023)
content:
Obligations of any authority, commission or similar governmental organization existing
   pursuant to the laws of this Commonwealth or the laws of any other state or of the
   District of Columbia shall be authorized investments if purchased or retained in the
   exercise of that degree of judgment and care, under circumstances then prevailing,
   which men of prudence, discretion and intelligence exercise in the management of their
   own affairs, not in regard to speculation but in regard to the permanent disposition
   of their funds, considering the probable income to be derived therefrom as well as
   the probable safety of their capital.  The authorization to make and retain investments pursuant to this section shall
   be in addition to, and independent of, authorizations to make investments pursuant
   to other provisions of this chapter and requirements applicable under other provisions
   of this chapter shall not affect investments also authorized by this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 72. Prudent Investor Rule›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7212. Degree of care

   investment and management decisions.  A fiduciary who represents that he has special investment skills shall exercise
   those skills.

content:

   to or in place of the investments authorized by this chapter, may make and retain
   without liability for resulting loss, such investments as the court, upon petition
   of the fiduciary or of any party in interest, and after such notice as it shall direct,
   aided by the report of a master if necessary, shall authorize or direct, subject only
   to such conditions and limitations as shall be fixed by the court in the decree authorizing
   or directing the investment.

   shall be an authorized investment if the reserved annual rent, capitalized at the
   rate of 5% per annum, shall not exceed four-fifth of the fair value of the real estate
   out of which it issues, determined by appraisal, as in the case of mortgages.

content:
(a) General rule.--The testator or settlor in the instrument establishing a trust may prescribe the powers,
      duties and liabilities of the fiduciary regarding the investment or noninvestment
      of principal and income and the acquisition, by purchase or otherwise, retention,
      and disposition, by sale or otherwise, of any property which, at any time or by reason
      of any circumstance, shall come into his control;  and whenever any such provision
      shall conflict with this chapter, such provision shall control notwithstanding this
      chapter, unless the court having jurisdiction over the trust shall otherwise decree
      pursuant to subsection (b) of this section.  In the absence, however, of an express restriction to the contrary in the trust
      instrument, the fiduciary may invest in any investment authorized by this chapter.

content:

      in which the decedent's estate is being administered.

content: A trust may be created by:

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7735. Charitable purposes; enforcement - UTC 405
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7735. Charitable purposes; enforcement - UTC 405 (2023)
content:
(a) Purposes.--A charitable trust may be created for the relief of poverty, the advancement of education
      or religion, the promotion of health, governmental or municipal purposes or other
      purposes the achievement of which is beneficial to the community.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7736. Creation of trust induced by fraud, duress or undue influence - UTC 406
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7736. Creation of trust induced by fraud, duress or undue influence - UTC 406
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7736. Creation of trust induced by fraud, duress or undue influence - UTC 406 (2023)
content:
A trust or an amendment to a trust is voidable to the extent its creation was induced
   by fraud, duress or undue influence.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7738. Trust for care of animal - UTC 408
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7738. Trust for care of animal - UTC 408
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7738. Trust for care of animal - UTC 408 (2023)
content:
(a) Creation and termination.--A trust may be created to provide for the care of an animal alive during the settlor's
      lifetime.  The trust terminates upon the death of the animal or, if the trust was created to
      provide for the care of more than one animal alive during the settlor's lifetime,
      upon the death of the last surviving animal.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7737. Oral trusts unenforceable
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7737. Oral trusts unenforceable
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7737. Oral trusts unenforceable (2023)
content: Oral trusts are unenforceable in this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.1. Modification or termination of noncharitable irrevocable trust by consent - UTC 411
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.1. Modification or termination of noncharitable irrevocable trust by consent - UTC 411
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.1. Modification or termination of noncharitable irrevocable trust by consent - UTC 411 (2023)
content:
(a) Consent by settlor and beneficiaries.--A noncharitable irrevocable trust may be modified or terminated upon consent of the
      settlor and all beneficiaries even if the modification or termination is inconsistent
      with a material purpose of the trust.  A settlor's power to consent to a trust's modification or termination may be exercised
      by a guardian, an agent under the settlor's general power of attorney or an agent
      under the settlor's limited power of attorney that specifically authorizes that action.  Notwithstanding Subchapter C (relating to representation), the settlor may not represent
      a beneficiary in the modification or termination of a trust under this subsection.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.3. Charitable trusts - UTC 413

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.3. Charitable trusts - UTC 413 (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided in subsection (b), if a particular charitable purpose
      becomes unlawful, impracticable or wasteful:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.5. Reformation to correct mistakes - UTC 415
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.5. Reformation to correct mistakes - UTC 415
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.5. Reformation to correct mistakes - UTC 415 (2023)
content:
The court may reform the terms of a trust, even if unambiguous, to conform to the
   settlor's probable intention if it is proved by clear and convincing evidence that
   both the settlor's intent and the terms of the trust were affected by a mistake of
   fact or law, whether in expression or inducement.  The court may provide that the modification have retroactive effect.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.6. Modification to achieve settlor's tax objectives - UTC 416
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.6. Modification to achieve settlor's tax objectives - UTC 416
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.6. Modification to achieve settlor's tax objectives - UTC 416 (2023)
content:
The court may modify the terms of a trust in a manner that is not contrary to the
   settlor's probable intention in order to achieve the settlor's tax objectives.  The court may provide that the modification have retroactive effect.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter E. Creditor's Claims; Spendthrift and Discretionary Trusts›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7745. Creditor's claim against settlor - UTC 505(a)
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter E. Creditor's Claims; Spendthrift and Discretionary Trusts › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7745. Creditor's claim against settlor - UTC 505(a)
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7745. Creditor's claim against settlor - UTC 505(a) (2023)
content:
Whether or not the terms of a trust contain a spendthrift provision and notwithstanding
   section 7744 (relating to discretionary trusts;  effect of standard -UTC 504):

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.2. Modification or termination of noncharitable irrevocable trust by court - UTC 412
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.2. Modification or termination of noncharitable irrevocable trust by court - UTC 412
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.2. Modification or termination of noncharitable irrevocable trust by court - UTC 412 (2023)
content:
(a) Unanticipated circumstances.--The court may modify the administrative or dispositive provisions of a noncharitable
      irrevocable trust, make an allowance from the principal of the trust or terminate
      the trust if, because of circumstances that apparently were not anticipated by the
      settlor, modification, allowance or termination will further the purposes of the trust.  To the extent practicable, the modification or allowance shall approximate the settlor's
      probable intention.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.4. Modification or termination of noncharitable trust - UTC 414
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.4. Modification or termination of noncharitable trust - UTC 414
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.4. Modification or termination of noncharitable trust - UTC 414 (2023)
content:
(a) Trustee's authority.--A trustee of a noncharitable trust may terminate the trust if the trustee concludes
      that the value of the trust property is insufficient to justify the cost of administration,
      the trustee has given written notice to the qualified beneficiaries at least 60 days
      before the proposed termination and no qualified beneficiary provides the trustee
      with a written objection to the proposed termination on or before the date specified
      in the notice.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.8. Combination of trusts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.8. Combination of trusts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.8. Combination of trusts (2023)
content:
(a) With court approval.--The court, for cause shown, may authorize the combination of separate trusts with
      substantially similar provisions upon terms and conditions and with notice as the
      court shall direct notwithstanding that the trusts may have been created by separate
      instruments and by different persons.  If necessary to protect possibly different future interests, the assets shall be
      valued at the time of the combination, and a record made of the proportionate interest
      of each separate trust in the combined fund.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter E. Creditor's Claims; Spendthrift and Discretionary Trusts›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7743. Exceptions to spendthrift provision - UTC 503
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter E. Creditor's Claims; Spendthrift and Discretionary Trusts › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7743. Exceptions to spendthrift provision - UTC 503
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7743. Exceptions to spendthrift provision - UTC 503 (2023)
content: (a) (Reserved).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.7. Division of trusts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter D. Creation, Validity, Modification and Termination of Trust › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.7. Division of trusts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7740.7. Division of trusts (2023)
content:
(a) Without court approval.--A trustee may, without court approval, divide a trust into separate trusts, allocating
      to each separate trust either a fractional share of each asset and each liability
      held by the original trust or assets having an appropriate aggregate fair market value
      and fairly representing the appreciation or depreciation in the assets of the original
      trust as a whole.  The beneficiaries of the separate trusts may be different so long as their rights
      are not impaired.  If the division reflects disclaimers or different tax elections, the division shall
      relate back to the date to which the disclaimer or tax election relates.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter E. Creditor's Claims; Spendthrift and Discretionary Trusts›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7742. Spendthrift provision - UTC 502
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter E. Creditor's Claims; Spendthrift and Discretionary Trusts › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7742. Spendthrift provision - UTC 502
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7742. Spendthrift provision - UTC 502 (2023)
content:
(a) Validity.--A spendthrift provision is valid only if it restrains both voluntary and involuntary
      transfer of a beneficiary's interest.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter E. Creditor's Claims; Spendthrift and Discretionary Trusts›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7744. Discretionary trusts; effect of standard - UTC 504
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter E. Creditor's Claims; Spendthrift and Discretionary Trusts › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7744. Discretionary trusts; effect of standard - UTC 504
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7744. Discretionary trusts; effect of standard - UTC 504 (2023)
content: (a) (Reserved).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter E. Creditor's Claims; Spendthrift and Discretionary Trusts›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7741. Rights of beneficiary's creditor or assignee - UTC 501
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter E. Creditor's Claims; Spendthrift and Discretionary Trusts › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7741. Rights of beneficiary's creditor or assignee - UTC 501
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7741. Rights of beneficiary's creditor or assignee - UTC 501 (2023)
content:
A judgment creditor or assignee of the beneficiary may reach the beneficiary's interest
   by attachment of present or future distributions to or for the benefit of the beneficiary
   or other means to the extent the beneficiary's interest is not subject to a spendthrift
   provision.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter E. Creditor's Claims; Spendthrift and Discretionary Trusts›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7746. Overdue distribution - UTC 506
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter E. Creditor's Claims; Spendthrift and Discretionary Trusts › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7746. Overdue distribution - UTC 506
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7746. Overdue distribution - UTC 506 (2023)
content:
(a) Distribution not made within reasonable time.--Whether or not the interest of the beneficiary in the trust is subject to a spendthrift
      provision, a creditor or assignee of a beneficiary may reach a mandatory distribution
      of income or principal, including a distribution upon termination of the trust, if
      the trustee has not made the distribution to the beneficiary within a reasonable time
      after the mandated distribution date.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter E. Creditor's Claims; Spendthrift and Discretionary Trusts›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7748. Property subject to power of withdrawal - UTC 505(b)
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter E. Creditor's Claims; Spendthrift and Discretionary Trusts › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7748. Property subject to power of withdrawal - UTC 505(b)
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7748. Property subject to power of withdrawal - UTC 505(b) (2023)
content:
Trust property that is subject to a power of withdrawal, during the period the power
   may be exercised and after its lapse, release or waiver, may be reached by a creditor
   or an assignee of the holder of the power whether or not the interest of the holder
   in the trust is subject to a spendthrift provision.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter F. Revocable Trusts›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7754. Actions contesting validity of revocable trust
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter F. Revocable Trusts › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7754. Actions contesting validity of revocable trust
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7754. Actions contesting validity of revocable trust (2023)
content:
(a) How action may be commenced.--A person having standing to do so may contest the validity of a revocable trust by
      filing a petition with the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter F. Revocable Trusts›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7753. Trustee's duties; powers of withdrawal - UTC 603
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter F. Revocable Trusts › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7753. Trustee's duties; powers of withdrawal - UTC 603
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7753. Trustee's duties; powers of withdrawal - UTC 603 (2023)
content:
(a) Power of settlor.--Regardless of the legal capacity of the settlor, the rights of the beneficiaries are
      subject to the control of, and the duties of the trustee are owed exclusively to,
      the settlor to the extent a trust is revocable.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter G. Office of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7761. Accepting or declining trusteeship - UTC 701

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7761. Accepting or declining trusteeship - UTC 701 (2023)
content:
(a) Accepting trusteeship.--Except as otherwise provided in subsection (c), a person designated as trustee accepts
      the trusteeship:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter F. Revocable Trusts›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7752. Revocation or amendment of revocable trust - UTC 602
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter F. Revocable Trusts › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7752. Revocation or amendment of revocable trust - UTC 602
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7752. Revocation or amendment of revocable trust - UTC 602 (2023)
content:
(a) Power to revoke or amend.--The settlor may revoke or amend a trust unless the terms of the trust expressly provide
      that the trust is irrevocable.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter F. Revocable Trusts›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7755. Claims and distribution after settlor's death
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter F. Revocable Trusts › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7755. Claims and distribution after settlor's death
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7755. Claims and distribution after settlor's death (2023)
content:
(a) Creditors' rights.--Creditors of the settlor of a revocable trust shall have the same rights against the
      trust assets determined immediately before the settlor's death as they have against
      the settlor's estate, but the assets of the settlor's estate shall be applied first
      toward satisfaction of the creditors' claims.  This subsection shall not expose to creditors' claims trust assets for which other
      provisions of substantive law provide exemption from the claims of the settlor's creditors.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter F. Revocable Trusts›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7751. Capacity of settlor of revocable trust - UTC 601
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter F. Revocable Trusts › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7751. Capacity of settlor of revocable trust - UTC 601
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7751. Capacity of settlor of revocable trust - UTC 601 (2023)
content:
The capacity required to create, amend, revoke or add property to a revocable trust
   or to direct the actions of the trustee of a revocable trust is the same as that required
   to make a will.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter G. Office of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7762. Trustee's bond - UTC 702
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter G. Office of Trustee › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7762. Trustee's bond - UTC 702
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7762. Trustee's bond - UTC 702 (2023)
content:
(a) When required.--A trustee shall give bond to secure performance of the trustee's duties only if the
      court finds that a bond is needed to protect the interests of the beneficiaries or
      is required by the terms of the trust and the court has not dispensed with the requirement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter G. Office of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7764. Vacancy in trusteeship; appointment of successor - UTC 704
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter G. Office of Trustee › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7764. Vacancy in trusteeship; appointment of successor - UTC 704
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7764. Vacancy in trusteeship; appointment of successor - UTC 704 (2023)
content: (a) When vacancy occurs.--A vacancy in a trusteeship occurs if:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter E. Creditor's Claims; Spendthrift and Discretionary Trusts›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7747. Personal obligations of trustee - UTC 507
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter E. Creditor's Claims; Spendthrift and Discretionary Trusts › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7747. Personal obligations of trustee - UTC 507
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7747. Personal obligations of trustee - UTC 507 (2023)
content:
Trust property is not subject to personal obligations of the trustee even if the trustee
   becomes insolvent or bankrupt.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter G. Office of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7767. Delivery of property by former trustee - UTC 707
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter G. Office of Trustee › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7767. Delivery of property by former trustee - UTC 707
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7767. Delivery of property by former trustee - UTC 707 (2023)
content:
(a) Duties and powers of trustee.--Unless a cotrustee remains in office or the court otherwise orders, a trustee who
      has resigned or been removed has the duties of a trustee and the powers necessary
      to protect the trust property until the trust property is delivered to a successor
      trustee or other person entitled to it.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter G. Office of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7765. Resignation of trustee; filing resignation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter G. Office of Trustee › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7765. Resignation of trustee; filing resignation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7765. Resignation of trustee; filing resignation (2023)
content: (a) Deleted by2016, July 8, P.L. 497, No. 79, § 15, effective Jan. 1, 2017.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter G. Office of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7763. Cotrustees - UTC 703
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter G. Office of Trustee › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7763. Cotrustees - UTC 703
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7763. Cotrustees - UTC 703 (2023)
content: (a) Majority decision.--Cotrustees who do not reach a unanimous decision may act by majority decision.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter G. Office of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7766. Removal of trustee - UTC 706
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter G. Office of Trustee › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7766. Removal of trustee - UTC 706
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7766. Removal of trustee - UTC 706 (2023)
content:
(a) Request to remove trustee;  court authority.--The settlor, a cotrustee or a beneficiary may request the court to remove a trustee
      or a trustee may be removed by the court on its own initiative.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter G. Office of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7768. Compensation of trustee - UTC 708
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter G. Office of Trustee › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7768. Compensation of trustee - UTC 708
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7768. Compensation of trustee - UTC 708 (2023)
content:
(a) If unspecified.--If neither the terms of a trust nor a separate written agreement signed by the settlor
      or anyone who is authorized by the terms of the trust to do so specifies the trustee's
      compensation, the trustee is entitled to compensation that is reasonable under the
      circumstances. Neither a compensation provision in the terms of a trust nor a fee agreement governs
      compensation payable from trust principal unless it explicitly so provides.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter G. Office of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7769. Reimbursement of expenses - UTC 709
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter G. Office of Trustee › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7769. Reimbursement of expenses - UTC 709
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7769. Reimbursement of expenses - UTC 709 (2023)
content:
(a) Reimbursement from trust property.--A trustee is entitled to be reimbursed out of the trust property, with interest as
      appropriate, for:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7772. Duty of loyalty - UTC 802
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7772. Duty of loyalty - UTC 802
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7772. Duty of loyalty - UTC 802 (2023)
content: (a) Duty of trustee.--A trustee shall administer the trust solely in the interests of the beneficiaries.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter G. Office of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7770. Liability of successor trustee
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter G. Office of Trustee › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7770. Liability of successor trustee
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7770. Liability of successor trustee (2023)
content:
A successor trustee shall not be personally liable for the acts or omissions of the
   trustee's predecessor and shall have no duty to investigate the acts or omissions
   of the predecessor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7771. Duty to administer trust - UTC 801
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7771. Duty to administer trust - UTC 801
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7771. Duty to administer trust - UTC 801 (2023)
content:
Upon acceptance of a trusteeship, the trustee shall administer the trust in good faith,
   in accordance with its terms and purposes and the interests of the beneficiaries and
   in accordance with applicable law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7780.3. Duty to inform and report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7780.3. Duty to inform and report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7780.3. Duty to inform and report (2023)
content:
(a) Duty to respond to requests.--A trustee shall promptly respond to a reasonable request by the settlor of a trust
      or by a beneficiary of an irrevocable trust for information related to the trust's
      administration. A trustee shall promptly respond to the Department of Human Services' reasonable request
      for information related to the trust's administration when a settlor or beneficiary
      is a resident in a State-owned facility or an applicant for or recipient of cash or
      medical assistance from the Commonwealth and the department certifies in writing that
      it has obtained a currently valid consent for the disclosure of such information from
      the settlor or beneficiary of the trust. A trustee may rely upon the department's certification without investigating its accuracy.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7776. Trustee's skills - UTC 806
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7776. Trustee's skills - UTC 806
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7776. Trustee's skills - UTC 806 (2023)
content:
A trustee who has special skills or expertise relevant to a trust or who is named
   trustee in reliance upon the trustee's representation that the trustee has special
   skills or expertise relevant to a trust shall use those special skills or expertise
   in the administration of the trust.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7773. Impartiality - UTC 803
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7773. Impartiality - UTC 803
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7773. Impartiality - UTC 803 (2023)
content:
If a trust has two or more beneficiaries, the trustee shall act impartially in investing,
   managing and distributing the trust property, giving due regard to the beneficiaries'
   respective interests in light of the purposes of the trust.  The duty to act impartially does not mean that the trustee must treat the beneficiaries
   equally.  Rather, the trustee must treat the beneficiaries equitably in light of the purposes
   of the trust.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7775. Costs of administration - UTC 805
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7775. Costs of administration - UTC 805
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7775. Costs of administration - UTC 805 (2023)
content:
In administering a trust, the trustee may incur only costs that are reasonable in
   relation to the trust property, the purposes of the trust and the skills of the trustee.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7774. Prudent administration - UTC 804
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7774. Prudent administration - UTC 804
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7774. Prudent administration - UTC 804 (2023)
content:
A trustee shall administer the trust as a prudent person would, by considering the
   purposes, provisions, distributional requirements and other circumstances of the trust
   and by exercising reasonable care, skill and caution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7778. Powers to direct
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7778. Powers to direct
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7778. Powers to direct (2023)
content: (a) to (d) Deleted by2024, July 15, P.L. 786, No. 64, § 4, effective in 90 days [Oct. 14, 2024].

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7779. Control and protection of trust property - UTC 809
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7779. Control and protection of trust property - UTC 809
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7779. Control and protection of trust property - UTC 809 (2023)
content: A trustee shall take reasonable steps to take control of and protect the trust property.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7780.4. Discretionary powers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 77. Trusts › Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7780.4. Discretionary powers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7780.4. Discretionary powers (2023)
content:
The trustee shall exercise a discretionary power in good faith and in accordance with
   the terms and purposes of the trust and the interests of the beneficiaries, notwithstanding
   the breadth of discretion granted to a trustee by the terms of the trust, including
   the use of such terms as “absolute,” “sole” or “uncontrolled.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 77. Trusts›Subchapter H. Duties and Powers of Trustee›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 7777. Delegation by trustee
