content:
(a) Existing and certain future orders.--All orders of support existing as of the effective date of this provision, as well
      as all orders of support entered or modified after the effective date of this provision
      but before June 30, 1990, shall provide for mandatory attachment of income:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter C. Proceedings Generally›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4347. Security for attendance or performance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter C. Proceedings Generally › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4347. Security for attendance or performance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4347. Security for attendance or performance (2023)
content:
At any stage of the proceedings under this chapter, upon affidavit filed that the
   obligor is about to leave this Commonwealth or the judicial district or, where in
   the judgment of the court, the obligor has habitually failed to comply with court
   orders under this chapter, the court may, as prescribed by general rule, issue appropriate
   process directing that the obligor be brought before the court and may direct that
   the obligor give security to appear when directed by the court or to comply with any
   order of the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter C. Proceedings Generally›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4355. Denial or suspension of licenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter C. Proceedings Generally › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4355. Denial or suspension of licenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4355. Denial or suspension of licenses (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as provided in subsection (d.1), where the domestic relations section or the
      department has been unable to attach the income of an obligor and the obligor owes
      support in an amount equal to or greater than three months of the monthly support
      obligation or where an individual has failed to comply with a visitation or partial
      custody order pursuant to section 4346 (relating to contempt for noncompliance with
      visitation or partial custody order) or an individual has failed, after appropriate
      notice, to comply with subpoenas or warrants relating to paternity or child support
      proceedings, the court, the domestic relations section or the department shall issue
      an order directing any licensing authority to:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter C. Proceedings Generally›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4350. Effect of appeal
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter C. Proceedings Generally › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4350. Effect of appeal
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4350. Effect of appeal (2023)
content:
An appeal from an order of support entered pursuant to this chapter shall not operate
   as a supersedeas unless so ordered by the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter C. Proceedings Generally›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4351. Costs and fees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter C. Proceedings Generally › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4351. Costs and fees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4351. Costs and fees (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If an obligee prevails in a proceeding to establish paternity or to obtain a support
      order, the court may assess against the obligor filing fees, reasonable attorney fees
      and necessary travel and other reasonable costs and expenses incurred by the obligee
      and the obligee's witnesses.  Attorney fees may be taxed as costs and shall be ordered to be paid directly to
      the attorney, who may enforce the order in the attorney's own name.  Payment of support owed to the obligee shall have priority over fees, costs and
      expenses.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter C. Proceedings Generally›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4349. Consolidation of proceedings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter C. Proceedings Generally › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4349. Consolidation of proceedings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4349. Consolidation of proceedings (2023)
content:
In order to facilitate frequent and unimpeded contact between children and parents,
   a judge may consolidate with a support action or proceeding any proceeding commenced
   for visitation rights, sole or shared custody, temporary or permanent custody or any
   other matters pertaining to support authorized by law which fairly and expeditiously
   may be determined and disposed of in the support action or proceeding.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter C. Proceedings Generally›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4353. Duty to report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter C. Proceedings Generally › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4353. Duty to report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4353. Duty to report (2023)
content:
(a) Notice of changes affecting support.--An individual who is a party to a support proceeding shall notify the domestic relations
      section, the department and the other parties in writing or by personal appearance
      within seven days of any material change in circumstances relevant to the level of
      support or the administration of the support order, including, but not limited to:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter C. Proceedings Generally›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4354. Willful failure to pay support order
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter C. Proceedings Generally › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4354. Willful failure to pay support order
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4354. Willful failure to pay support order (2023)
content:
(a) Offense defined.--An individual who willfully fails to comply with a support order of a court of this
      Commonwealth when the individual has the financial ability to comply with the support
      order commits an offense.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter D. Proceedings Against Entireties Property›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4363. Trustee to distribute proceeds of sale
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter D. Proceedings Against Entireties Property › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4363. Trustee to distribute proceeds of sale
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4363. Trustee to distribute proceeds of sale (2023)
content:
(a) Appointment of trustee.--The court shall, at the time of the hearing or thereafter, appoint a trustee who shall
      receive from the sheriff the proceeds of the sale of the property after the costs
      have been paid.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter D. Proceedings Against Entireties Property›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4362. Plaintiff's share of proceeds of sale
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter D. Proceedings Against Entireties Property › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4362. Plaintiff's share of proceeds of sale
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4362. Plaintiff's share of proceeds of sale (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The plaintiff spouse shall be entitled, out of the proceeds of this sale, to such
      sums of money as represents the share in the property, based on the proportionate
      part of the original purchase money furnished by the plaintiff spouse for the purchase
      of the property.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter D. Proceedings Against Entireties Property›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4364. Credit to plaintiff who purchases property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter D. Proceedings Against Entireties Property › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4364. Credit to plaintiff who purchases property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4364. Credit to plaintiff who purchases property (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If the plaintiff spouse becomes the purchaser at the execution sale, the plaintiff
      shall be entitled to a credit on the purchase price thereof for the sum of money found
      by the court to represent the plaintiff's share in the property and also for the sums
      of money due the plaintiff from the defendant under the order of support upon which
      the execution was issued at the time of the sale, together with interest on the sums
      due the plaintiff for support from the time the respective sums become due.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter D. Proceedings Against Entireties Property›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4361. Execution of support order against entireties property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter D. Proceedings Against Entireties Property › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4361. Execution of support order against entireties property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4361. Execution of support order against entireties property (2023)
content:
(a) Entry of order.--Whenever married persons hold real property by the entireties and one spouse secures
      an order of court against the other spouse for the support of the plaintiff spouse
      or of a child of both persons or the defendant or for the support of both the plaintiff
      spouse and child and a copy of the order has been certified to the court of common
      pleas of the county in this Commonwealth in which the property is situated, the order
      shall be entered in that court as a judgment with the same effect as if it had been
      recovered as a judgment of that court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter D. Proceedings Against Entireties Property›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4365. Rights of divorced person in entireties property sold for support
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter D. Proceedings Against Entireties Property › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4365. Rights of divorced person in entireties property sold for support
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4365. Rights of divorced person in entireties property sold for support (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--After the divorce of any spouse who is a tenant by the entireties of real property
      with the former spouse, the divorced spouse is entitled to all the rights and remedies
      provided in this subchapter for the collection of any sums of money ordered by a court
      to be paid to the divorced spouse for the support of the children of the former spouse
      as fully as if no divorce had occurred.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter D. Proceedings Against Entireties Property›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4366. Other enforcement remedies preserved
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter D. Proceedings Against Entireties Property › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4366. Other enforcement remedies preserved
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4366. Other enforcement remedies preserved (2023)
content:
This subchapter and other provisions of this chapter do not remove from the plaintiff
   the rights to any other existing remedies to enforce a support order, including, but
   not limited to, the right of the plaintiff to institute proceedings against the real
   or personal property of the defendant.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter E. Title IV-D Program and Related Matters›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4372. Establishment of Title IV-D program
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter E. Title IV-D Program and Related Matters › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4372. Establishment of Title IV-D program
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4372. Establishment of Title IV-D program (2023)
content:
(a) Designation of Title IV-D agency.--The department is the Title IV-D State agency.  The department shall create a single and separate organizational unit which shall
      be responsible for developing and implementing, subject to the approval of the secretary,
      a federally approved State plan for child support.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter E. Title IV-D Program and Related Matters›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4373. Administration of Title IV-D program
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter E. Title IV-D Program and Related Matters › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4373. Administration of Title IV-D program
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4373. Administration of Title IV-D program (2023)
content:
(a) Parent locator service.--The department shall maintain a parent locator service for the purpose of establishing
      parentage, for establishing, setting the amount of, modifying or enforcing child support,
      establishing or enforcing visitation or custody orders and locating legally responsible
      relatives.  The locator services shall utilize all sources of information and legally available
      records.  In addition, the department shall utilize the parent locator service of the Federal
      Government pursuant to Federal law and shall only make disclosures of information
      to individuals as provided by Federal law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter E. Title IV-D Program and Related Matters›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4371. Definitions

content:
(a) Central registry created.--A central registry of records shall be maintained in the department showing, as far
      as it is known, with respect to any absent parent against whom support is sought,
      all of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4301. Scope of chapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4301. Scope of chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4301. Scope of chapter (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Actions or proceedings provided by this chapter are in addition to and not in substitution
      of actions or proceedings provided by unsuspended statutes where there is desertion
      or a failure to perform a duty to support.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter E. Title IV-D Program and Related Matters›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4378. Assistance recipients to seek support
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter E. Title IV-D Program and Related Matters › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4378. Assistance recipients to seek support
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4378. Assistance recipients to seek support (2023)
content:
(a) Seeking support required.--Prior to authorization, every applicant for assistance whose circumstances include
      the reported absence of a legally responsible relative from the household or the presence
      of a putative father shall appear before the domestic relations section or other applicable
      division of the court of common pleas.  Upon the request of a family court or domestic relations section, the secretary
      is authorized to waive the requirement of personal appearance before a family court
      or domestic relations section if another procedure would be as efficient and effective.  Subject to Federal approval, only when necessary, assistance shall not be authorized
      by the department until it has been certified that the applicant has cooperated in
      determining paternity and enforcing support.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4302. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4302. Definitions

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4303. Information to consumer reporting agency
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4303. Information to consumer reporting agency
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4303. Information to consumer reporting agency (2023)
content:
Information regarding the name and the amount of arrearages owed by an obligor shall
   be provided periodically to consumer reporting agencies whenever the obligor owes
   overdue support, subject to the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter E. Title IV-D Program and Related Matters›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4374. State disbursement unit
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter E. Title IV-D Program and Related Matters › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4374. State disbursement unit
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4374. State disbursement unit (2023)
content:
(a) Establishment.--The department shall establish and operate a State disbursement unit for collection
      and disbursement of payments on child support orders consistent with Federal law.  The State disbursement unit shall also monitor support orders for enforcement action
      consistent with Federal law.  At the option of the department, the domestic relations sections may be linked into
      the State disbursement unit and perform some or all of the functions thereof.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter E. Title IV-D Program and Related Matters›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4377. Power to expedite support cases
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter E. Title IV-D Program and Related Matters › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4377. Power to expedite support cases
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4377. Power to expedite support cases (2023)
content:
(a) Administrative powers.--The department shall have Statewide jurisdiction to issue the following administrative
      orders to expedite the establishment and enforcement of support on behalf of any assistance
      recipient or nonrecipient receiving Title IV-D services:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter E. Title IV-D Program and Related Matters›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4379. Cooperation required
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter E. Title IV-D Program and Related Matters › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4379. Cooperation required
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4379. Cooperation required (2023)
content:
In accordance with a child support plan approved by the Federal Government, the department
   shall have the power and its duty shall be to:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter E. Title IV-D Program and Related Matters›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4380. Enforcement of cooperation requirements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter E. Title IV-D Program and Related Matters › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4380. Enforcement of cooperation requirements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4380. Enforcement of cooperation requirements (2023)
content:
(a) Cooperation required.--It is essential to the effective and responsible utilization of assistance funds that
      applicants and recipients who are caretakers of a child whose circumstances include
      the reported absence of a legally responsible relative from the household or presence
      of a putative father cooperate fully with the department and the court or domestic
      relations section in establishing paternity and in securing child support payments
      and in all matters set forth in section 4379 (relating to cooperation required).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4304.1. Cooperation of government and nongovernment agencies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4304.1. Cooperation of government and nongovernment agencies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4304.1. Cooperation of government and nongovernment agencies (2023)
content:
(a) Cooperation of government agencies.--Notwithstanding any other provision of law, including the provisions of section 731
      of the act of April 9, 1929 (P.L. 343, No. 176),1known as The Fiscal Code, all government agencies shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter E. Title IV-D Program and Related Matters›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4375. Access to records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter E. Title IV-D Program and Related Matters › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4375. Access to records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4375. Access to records (2023)
content:
(a) Access to be granted.--The secretary or his designees in writing shall have access to all records, and the
      department in cooperation with all other agencies of the executive branch shall establish
      a single, uniform system of information clearance and retrieval.  Information collected as a result of the use of tax records shall include the full
      name, residence or address, name and address of the employer, income and assets and
      the Social Security number of the noncustodial parent.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter E. Title IV-D Program and Related Matters›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4381. Garnishment of wages of Commonwealth employees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter E. Title IV-D Program and Related Matters › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4381. Garnishment of wages of Commonwealth employees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4381. Garnishment of wages of Commonwealth employees (2023)
content:
Notwithstanding any other provision of law, moneys due from or payable by the Commonwealth,
   including any agency, instrumentality or authority thereof, due to any individual
   shall be subject, in like manner and to the same extent as if the Commonwealth were
   a private person, to legal process brought for the enforcement against such individual
   of his legal obligations to provide support for a child or spouse.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4306. Duties of Title IV-D attorney
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4306. Duties of Title IV-D attorney
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4306. Duties of Title IV-D attorney (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The county Title IV-D attorney shall at all times aid in the enforcement of the duty
      of child support and child and spousal support and shall cooperate with the domestic
      relations section in the presentation of complaints or in any proceeding designed
      to obtain compliance with any order of the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4305. General administration of support matters
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4305. General administration of support matters
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4305. General administration of support matters (2023)
content:
(a) Powers and duties.--Subject to any inconsistent general rules and to the supervision and direction of

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4307. State income tax intercept
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4307. State income tax intercept
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4307. State income tax intercept (2023)
content:
The department shall have the authority to implement a State income tax refund intercept
   program pursuant to section 466(a)(3) of the Social Security Act (Public Law 74-271,42 U.S.C. § 666(a)(3)) when, in the judgment of the department, it is cost effective to do so.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4308. Lottery winnings intercept
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4308. Lottery winnings intercept
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4308. Lottery winnings intercept (2023)
content:
(a) Duty of Department of Revenue.--In the case of any person winning more than $2,500 in the Pennsylvania State Lottery,
      the Department of Revenue shall request the department to make all reasonable efforts
      to determine if the winner is a delinquent support obligor prior to making any lottery
      winnings payment.   If the winner is so found, the amount of any arrearages shall be deducted from
      the amount of lottery winnings and paid to the obligee in the manner provided in this
      title for the administration of support payments.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4308.1. Collection of overdue support from monetary awards
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4308.1. Collection of overdue support from monetary awards
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4308.1. Collection of overdue support from monetary awards (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Overdue support shall be a lien by operation of law against the net proceeds of any
      monetary award, as defined in subsection (i), owed to an obligor, and distribution
      of any such award shall be stayed in an amount equal to the child support lien provided
      for under this section pending payment of the lien.  Except as provided in subsection (c) or (f), nothing in this section shall provide
      a basis for a paying agent or an insurer to delay payment of a settlement, verdict
      or judgment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4309. Publication of delinquent support obligors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4309. Publication of delinquent support obligors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4309. Publication of delinquent support obligors (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Any county, through its domestic relations section, may publish the names of delinquent
      support obligors who are in arrears 30 days or more in newspapers of general or special
      circulation in the county.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter F. New Hire Reporting›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4392. Employer reporting
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter F. New Hire Reporting › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4392. Employer reporting
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4392. Employer reporting (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--For purposes of enhancing child support enforcement activities, including the location
      of individuals, the establishment of paternity and the enforcement of child support
      obligations pursuant to this subchapter, a Commonwealth directory of new hires shall
      be established within the Department of Labor and Industry.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter F. New Hire Reporting›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4394. Guidelines

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4394. Guidelines (2023)
content:
The Department of Labor and Industry shall develop guidelines for employers to use
   to determine if an individual qualifies as an employee under this subchapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter F. New Hire Reporting›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4393. Use of information
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter F. New Hire Reporting › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4393. Use of information
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4393. Use of information (2023)
content:
(a) Access to information.--The domestic relations sections and the department shall have access to all information
      required under this subchapter for purposes of locating individuals, establishing
      paternity and establishing, modifying and enforcing child support obligations.  The domestic relations sections and the department may disclose such information
      to its employees, agents and contractors solely for the purposes set forth in this
      subsection.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 51. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5104. Blood tests to determine paternity
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 51. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5104. Blood tests to determine paternity
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5104. Blood tests to determine paternity (2023)
content:
(a) Short title of section.--This section shall be known and may be cited as the Uniform Act on Blood Tests to
      Determine Paternity.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter F. New Hire Reporting›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4395. Confidentiality
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter F. New Hire Reporting › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4395. Confidentiality
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4395. Confidentiality (2023)
content:
All information received pursuant to this subchapter shall be confidential and shall
   be used only for the purposes set forth herein.  A person commits a summary offense if he or she discloses information received pursuant
   to this subchapter to an unauthorized person or for an unauthorized purpose and shall
   be subject to a civil penalty of up to $250 per offense.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter F. New Hire Reporting›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4391. Definitions

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally›Subchapter F. New Hire Reporting›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4396. Penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 43. Support Matters Generally › Subchapter F. New Hire Reporting › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4396. Penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4396. Penalties (2023)
content:
An employer that fails to report pursuant to this subchapter may be provided a written
   warning for the first violation and is subject to a civil penalty of up to $25 for
   each violation which is subsequent to the warning.  The civil penalty shall be payable to the Department of Labor and Industry.  If the failure to report or the submission of a false report is the result of a
   conspiracy between the employer and the employee, the employer shall be subject to
   a civil penalty of up to $500.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 51. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5102. Children declared to be legitimate
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 51. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5102. Children declared to be legitimate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5102. Children declared to be legitimate (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--All children shall be legitimate irrespective of the marital status of their parents,
      and, in every case where children are born out of wedlock, they shall enjoy all the
      rights and privileges as if they had been born during the wedlock of their parents
      except as otherwise provided in Title 20 (relating to decedents, estates and fiduciaries).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 52. Uniform Child Abduction Prevention›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5201. Scope of chapter

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 51. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5105. Fingerprinting of children
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 51. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5105. Fingerprinting of children
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5105. Fingerprinting of children (2023)
content:
Notwithstanding the provisions of54 Pa.C.S. § 702(b)(relating to change by order of court), a child who is 12 years of age or younger
   shall not be required to submit a set of fingerprints for the purpose of a name change
   under 54 Pa.C.S. Ch. 7 (relating to judicial change of name).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 51. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5103. Acknowledgment and claim of paternity
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 51. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5103. Acknowledgment and claim of paternity
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5103. Acknowledgment and claim of paternity (2023)
content:
(a) Acknowledgment of paternity.--The father of a child born to an unmarried woman may file with the Department of Public
      Welfare,1on forms prescribed by the department, an acknowledgment of paternity of the child
      which shall include the consent of the mother of the child, supported by her witnessed
      statement subject to18 Pa.C.S. § 4904(relating to unsworn falsification to authorities).  In such case, the father shall have all the rights and duties as to the child which
      he would have had if he had been married to the mother at the time of the birth of
      the child, and the child shall have all the rights and duties as to the father which
      the child would have had if the father had been married to the mother at the time
      of birth.  The hospital or other person accepting an acknowledgment of paternity shall provide
      written and oral notice, which may be through the use of video or audio equipment,
      to the birth mother and birth father of the alternatives to, the legal consequences
      of and the rights and responsibilities that arise from, signing the acknowledgment.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 52. Uniform Child Abduction Prevention › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5203. Cooperation and communication among courts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5203. Cooperation and communication among courts (2023)
content:
Sections 5410 (relating to communication between courts), 5411 (relating to taking
   testimony in another state) and 5412 (relating to cooperation between courts;  preservation
   of records) apply to cooperation and communication among courts in proceedings under
   this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 52. Uniform Child Abduction Prevention›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5205. Jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 52. Uniform Child Abduction Prevention › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5205. Jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5205. Jurisdiction (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A petition under this chapter may be filed only in a court that has jurisdiction to
      make a child custody determination with respect to the child at issue under Chapter
      54 (relating to uniform child custody jurisdiction and enforcement).

   reasonably ascertainable, the petition must contain:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 51. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5101. Attainment of full age

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5101. Attainment of full age (2023)
content:
(a) Age for entering into contracts.--Any individual 18 years of age and older shall have the right to enter into binding
      and legally enforceable contracts and the defense of minority shall not be available
      to such individuals.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 52. Uniform Child Abduction Prevention›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5209. Warrant to take physical custody of child
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 52. Uniform Child Abduction Prevention › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5209. Warrant to take physical custody of child

content:
(a) Ex parte.--If a petition under this chapter contains allegations and the court finds that there
      is a credible risk that the child is imminently likely to be wrongfully removed, the
      court may issue an ex parte warrant to take physical custody of the child.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 52. Uniform Child Abduction Prevention›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5204. Actions for abduction prevention measures

(a) Court.--A court on its own motion may order abduction prevention measures in a child custody

content:
In applying and construing this chapter, consideration must be given to the need to
   promote uniformity of the law with respect to its subject matter among states that
   enact it.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 53. Child Custody›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5327. Presumption in cases concerning primary physical custody
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 53. Child Custody › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5327. Presumption in cases concerning primary physical custody
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5327. Presumption in cases concerning primary physical custody (2023)
content:
(a) Between parents.--In any action regarding the custody of the child between the parents of the child,
      there shall be no presumption that custody should be awarded to a particular parent.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 53. Child Custody›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5331. Parenting plan
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 53. Child Custody › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5331. Parenting plan

content:
(a) Purpose.--In a contested custody proceeding, the court may require the parties to submit parenting
      plans for the care and custody of the child to aid the court in resolving the custody
      dispute.  A parenting plan and the position of a party as set forth in that parenting plan
      shall not be admissible as evidence by another party.

content:
(a) Expedited hearing.--A party who has obtained information under42 Pa.C.S. § 1904(relating to availability of criminal charge information in child custody proceedings)
      or otherwise about a charge filed against the other party for an offense listed under
      section 5329(a) (relating to consideration of criminal conviction) may move for a
      temporary custody order or modification of an existing custody order.  The court shall hold the hearing under this subsection in an expeditious manner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 53. Child Custody›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5324. Standing for any form of physical custody or legal custody
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 53. Child Custody › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5324. Standing for any form of physical custody or legal custody
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5324. Standing for any form of physical custody or legal custody (2023)
content:
The following individuals may file an action under this chapter for any form of physical
   custody or legal custody:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 53. Child Custody›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5329.1. Consideration of child abuse and involvement with protective services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 53. Child Custody › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5329.1. Consideration of child abuse and involvement with protective services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5329.1. Consideration of child abuse and involvement with protective services (2023)
content:
(a) Information sharing.--In accordance with section 6340(a)(5.1) (relating to release of information in confidential
      reports), where a party seeks any form of custody, subject to the examination of the
      parties, the court shall determine:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 53. Child Custody›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5326. Effect of adoption
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 53. Child Custody › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5326. Effect of adoption
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5326. Effect of adoption (2023)
content:
Any rights to seek physical custody or legal custody rights and any custody rights
   that have been granted under section 5324 (relating to standing for any form of physical
   custody or legal custody) or 5325 (relating to standing for partial physical custody
   and supervised physical custody) to a grandparent or great-grandparent prior to the
   adoption of the child by an individual other than a stepparent, grandparent or great-grandparent
   shall be automatically terminated upon such adoption.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 53. Child Custody›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5329. Consideration of criminal conviction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 53. Child Custody › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5329. Consideration of criminal conviction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5329. Consideration of criminal conviction (2023)
content:
(a) Offenses.--Where a party seeks any form of custody, the court shall consider whether that party
      or member of that party's household has been convicted of or has pleaded guilty or
      no contest to any of the offenses in this section or an offense in another jurisdiction
      substantially equivalent to any of the offenses in this section.  The court shall consider such conduct and determine that the party does not pose
      a threat of harm to the child before making any order of custody to that party when
      considering the following offenses:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 53. Child Custody›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5335. Counsel for child
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 53. Child Custody › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5335. Counsel for child
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5335. Counsel for child (2023)
content:
(a) Appointment.--The court may appoint counsel to represent the child if the court determines that
      the appointment will assist in resolving the issues in the custody proceeding.  If a child has legal counsel and a guardian ad litem, counsel shall represent the
      legal interests of the child and the guardian ad litem shall represent the best interests
      of the child.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 53. Child Custody›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5334. Guardian ad litem for child
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 53. Child Custody › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5334. Guardian ad litem for child
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5334. Guardian ad litem for child (2023)
content:
(a) Appointment.--The court may on its own motion or the motion of a party appoint a guardian ad litem
      to represent the child in the action.  The court may assess the cost upon the parties or any of them or as otherwise provided
      by law.  The guardian ad litem must be an attorney at law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 53. Child Custody›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5337. Relocation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 53. Child Custody › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5337. Relocation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5337. Relocation (2023)
content: (a) Applicability.--This section applies to any proposed relocation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 53. Child Custody›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5332. Informational programs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 53. Child Custody › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5332. Informational programs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5332. Informational programs (2023)
content:
(a) Attendance.--The court may direct the parties to attend informational programs concerning parental
      duties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 53. Child Custody›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5339. Award of counsel fees, costs and expenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 53. Child Custody › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5339. Award of counsel fees, costs and expenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5339. Award of counsel fees, costs and expenses (2023)
content:
Under this chapter, a court may award reasonable interim or final counsel fees, costs
   and expenses to a party if the court finds that the conduct of another party was obdurate,
   vexatious, repetitive or in bad faith.  This section may not apply if that party engaged the judicial process in good faith
   to protect the child from harm.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 53. Child Custody›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5333. Counseling as part of order
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 53. Child Custody › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5333. Counseling as part of order
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5333. Counseling as part of order (2023)
content:
(a) Attendance.--The court may, as part of a custody order, require the parties to attend counseling
      sessions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 53. Child Custody›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5340. Court-appointed child custody health care or behavioral health practitioners
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 53. Child Custody › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5340. Court-appointed child custody health care or behavioral health practitioners
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5340. Court-appointed child custody health care or behavioral health practitioners (2023)
content:
No party to a child custody matter in which the court has appointed a licensed health
   care or behavioral health practitioner to assist the court by conducting an examination
   or evaluation of the parties involved or making a recommendation concerning a child
   custody agreement or order may be permitted to file a complaint against the practitioner
   with the practitioner's State licensing board prior to the final agreement or order
   being issued and for 60 days thereafter.  As used in this section, “licensed health care or behavioral health practitioner” means a person who is licensed, certified, accredited or otherwise regulated by
   the Commonwealth to provide health care or behavioral health services.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 53. Child Custody›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5338. Modification of existing order
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 53. Child Custody › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5338. Modification of existing order
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5338. Modification of existing order (2023)
content:
(a) Best interest of the child.--Upon petition, a court may modify a custody order to serve the best interest of the
      child.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5401. Short title of chapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5401. Short title of chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5401. Short title of chapter (2023)
content:
This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction
   and Enforcement Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5402. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5402. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5402. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this chapter shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5403. Proceedings governed by other law
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5403. Proceedings governed by other law
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5403. Proceedings governed by other law (2023)
content:
This chapter does not govern an adoption proceeding or a proceeding pertaining to
   the authorization of emergency medical care for a child.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5407. Priority
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5407. Priority
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5407. Priority (2023)
content:
If a question of existence or exercise of jurisdiction under this chapter is raised
   in a child custody proceeding, the question, upon request of a party, must be given
   priority on the calendar and handled expeditiously.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5406. Effect of child custody determination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5406. Effect of child custody determination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5406. Effect of child custody determination (2023)
content:
A child custody determination made by a court of this Commonwealth that had jurisdiction
   under this chapter binds all persons who have been served in accordance with the laws
   of this Commonwealth or notified in accordance with section 5408 (relating to notice
   to persons outside Commonwealth) or who have submitted to the jurisdiction of the
   court and who have been given an opportunity to be heard.  As to those persons, the determination is conclusive as to all decided issues of
   law and fact except to the extent the determination is modified.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5405. International application of chapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5405. International application of chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5405. International application of chapter (2023)
content:
(a) Foreign country treated as state.--A court of this Commonwealth shall treat a foreign country as if it were a state of
      the United States for the purpose of applying Subchapter B (relating to jurisdiction)
      and this subchapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5404. Application to Native American tribes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5404. Application to Native American tribes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5404. Application to Native American tribes (2023)
content:
(a) Primacy of Indian Child Welfare Act.--A child custody proceeding that pertains to a Native American child as defined in
      the Indian Child Welfare Act of 1978 (Public Law 95-608,25 U.S.C. § 1901 et seq.) is not subject to this chapter to the extent that it is governed by the Indian Child
      Welfare Act of 1978.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5408. Notice to persons outside Commonwealth
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5408. Notice to persons outside Commonwealth
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5408. Notice to persons outside Commonwealth (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Notice required for the exercise of jurisdiction when a person is outside this Commonwealth
      may be given in a manner prescribed by the laws of this Commonwealth for service of
      process or by the law of the state in which the service is made.  Notice must be given in a manner reasonably calculated to give actual notice but
      may be by publication if other means are not effective.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5409. Appearance and limited immunity
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5409. Appearance and limited immunity
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5409. Appearance and limited immunity (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A party to a child custody proceeding, including a modification proceeding or a petitioner
      or respondent in a proceeding to enforce or register a child custody determination,
      is not subject to personal jurisdiction in this Commonwealth for another proceeding
      or purpose solely by reason of having participated or of having been physically present
      for the purpose of participating in the proceeding.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5411. Taking testimony in another state
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5411. Taking testimony in another state
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5411. Taking testimony in another state (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In addition to other procedures available to a party, a party to a child custody proceeding
      may offer testimony of witnesses who are located in another state, including testimony
      of the parties and the child, by deposition or other means allowable in this Commonwealth
      for testimony taken in another state.  The court on its own motion may order that the testimony of a person be taken in
      another state and may prescribe the manner in which and the terms upon which the testimony
      is taken.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5412. Cooperation between courts; preservation of records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5412. Cooperation between courts; preservation of records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5412. Cooperation between courts; preservation of records (2023)
content: (a) Assistance of another state.--A court of this Commonwealth may request the appropriate court of another state to:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5422. Exclusive, continuing jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5422. Exclusive, continuing jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5422. Exclusive, continuing jurisdiction (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided in section 5424 (relating to temporary emergency jurisdiction),
      a court of this Commonwealth which has made a child custody determination consistent
      with section 5421 (relating to initial child custody jurisdiction) or 5423 (relating
      to jurisdiction to modify determination) has exclusive, continuing jurisdiction over
      the determination until:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5442. Enforcement under Hague Convention
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5442. Enforcement under Hague Convention
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5442. Enforcement under Hague Convention (2023)
content:
Under this subchapter a court of this Commonwealth may enforce an order for the return
   of the child made under the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International
   Child Abduction as if it were a child custody determination.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5410. Communication between courts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5410. Communication between courts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5410. Communication between courts (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A court of this Commonwealth may communicate with a court in another state concerning
      a proceeding arising under this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5425. Notice; opportunity to be heard; joinder
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5425. Notice; opportunity to be heard; joinder
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5425. Notice; opportunity to be heard; joinder (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Before a child custody determination is made under this chapter, notice and an opportunity
      to be heard in accordance with the standards of section 5408 (relating to notice to
      persons outside Commonwealth) must be given to all persons entitled to notice under
      the laws of this Commonwealth as in child custody proceedings between residents of
      this Commonwealth, any parent whose parental rights have not been previously terminated
      and any person having physical custody of the child.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5426. Simultaneous proceedings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5426. Simultaneous proceedings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5426. Simultaneous proceedings (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided in section 5424 (relating to temporary emergency jurisdiction),
      a court of this Commonwealth may not exercise its jurisdiction under this subchapter
      if, at the time of the commencement of the proceeding, a proceeding concerning the
      custody of the child has been commenced in a court of another state having jurisdiction
      substantially in conformity with this chapter unless the proceeding has been terminated
      or is stayed by the court of the other state because a court of this Commonwealth
      is a more convenient forum under section 5427 (relating to inconvenient forum).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5427. Inconvenient forum
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5427. Inconvenient forum
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5427. Inconvenient forum (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A court of this Commonwealth which has jurisdiction under this chapter to make a child
      custody determination may decline to exercise its jurisdiction at any time if it determines
      that it is an inconvenient forum under the circumstances and that a court of another
      state is a more appropriate forum.  The issue of inconvenient forum may be raised upon motion of a party, the court's
      own motion or request of another court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5421. Initial child custody jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5421. Initial child custody jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5421. Initial child custody jurisdiction (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided in section 5424 (relating to temporary emergency jurisdiction),
      a court of this Commonwealth has jurisdiction to make an initial child custody determination
      only if:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5424. Temporary emergency jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5424. Temporary emergency jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5424. Temporary emergency jurisdiction (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A court of this Commonwealth has temporary emergency jurisdiction if the child is
      present in this Commonwealth and the child has been abandoned or it is necessary in
      an emergency to protect the child because the child or a sibling or parent of the
      child is subjected to or threatened with mistreatment or abuse.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5423. Jurisdiction to modify determination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5423. Jurisdiction to modify determination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5423. Jurisdiction to modify determination (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise provided in section 5424 (relating to temporary emergency jurisdiction),
   a court of this Commonwealth may not modify a child custody determination made by
   a court of another state unless a court of this Commonwealth has jurisdiction to make
   an initial determination under section 5421 (a)(1) or (2) (relating to initial child
   custody jurisdiction) and:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5428. Jurisdiction declined by reason of conduct
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5428. Jurisdiction declined by reason of conduct
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5428. Jurisdiction declined by reason of conduct (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided in section 5424 (relating to temporary emergency jurisdiction)
      or by other laws of this Commonwealth, if a court of this Commonwealth has jurisdiction
      under this chapter because a person seeking to invoke its jurisdiction has engaged
      in unjustifiable conduct, the court shall decline to exercise its jurisdiction unless:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5429. Information to be submitted to court
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5429. Information to be submitted to court
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5429. Information to be submitted to court (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Subject to the rules set forth in Chapter 53 (relating to child custody) providing
      for the confidentiality of procedures, addresses and other identifying information
      in a child custody proceeding, each party in its first pleading or in an attached
      affidavit shall give information, if reasonably ascertainable, under oath as to the
      child's present address or whereabouts, the places where the child has lived during
      the last five years and the names and present addresses of the persons with whom the
      child has lived during that period.  The pleading or affidavit must state whether the party:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5430. Appearance of parties and child
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5430. Appearance of parties and child
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5430. Appearance of parties and child (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In a child custody proceeding in this Commonwealth, the court may order a party to
      the proceeding who is in this Commonwealth to appear before the court in person with
      or without the child.  The court may order any person who is in this Commonwealth and who has physical
      custody or control of the child to appear in person with the child.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5445. Registration of child custody determination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5445. Registration of child custody determination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5445. Registration of child custody determination (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A child custody determination issued by a court of another state may be registered
      in this Commonwealth, with or without a simultaneous request for enforcement, by sending
      to the appropriate court in this Commonwealth:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5441. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5441. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5441. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this subchapter shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5443. Duty to enforce
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5443. Duty to enforce
